lines.text: The bells ring whenever they feel like it. Every clock says a different time. And the sign-up sheet ran off.
lines.script: [rattled, ticking it off] The bells ring whenever they feel like it. Every clock says a different time. [heavy, deadpan] And the sign-up sheet ran off.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Ran off? Like, RAN? On legs?
lines.script: [incredulous, dramatic] Ran off? [wide-eyed, delighted] Like, RAN? On legs?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: On little paper legs. Mrs. Kowalski saw it. She's still upset about it.
lines.script: [grave, confiding] On little paper legs. [pointed] Mrs. Kowalski saw it. [sympathetic, shaking her head] She's still upset about it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Mom. Mom. Are we going to SCHOOL? At NIGHT? That's the best thing that ever happened.
lines.script: [bouncing, whisper-shouting, thrilled] Mom. Mom. [ecstatic] Are we going to SCHOOL? At NIGHT? [reverent] That's the best thing that ever happened.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody is coming. I have a clipboard, and I'm not afraid to use it.
lines.script: [rallying, commanding, taking charge] Everybody is coming. [wry, fierce] I have a clipboard, and I'm not afraid to use it.

lines.speaker: School bell
lines.text: BRRRRRING. From inside the school. Then again. Then a little one: brring?
lines.script: [reading aloud, clanging, echoing] BRRRRRING. From inside the school. [clanging again, ominous] Then again. [tiny, uncertain] Then a little one: brring?

lines.speaker: School bell
lines.text: BRRRRRING. From inside the school. Then again. Then a little one: brring?
lines.script: [reading aloud, clanging, echoing] BRRRRRING. From inside the school. [clanging again, ominous] Then again. [tiny, uncertain] Then a little one: brring?

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Mrs. Gregori! Thank goodness. And you brought the whole family.
lines.script: [relieved, harried principal] Mrs. Gregori! Thank goodness. [warm, grateful] And you brought the whole family.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Principal Pruitt, my brother Tom. He's very good in a crisis. He's also very calm about it, which is annoying.
lines.script: [brisk, introducing, wry] Principal Pruitt, my brother Tom. [proud, teasing] He's very good in a crisis. [dry] He's also very calm about it, which is annoying.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hello. I hear your bells are haunted.
lines.script: [calm, dry, polite] Hello. [deadpan] I hear your bells are haunted.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Not haunted. Grumpy. Thirty-one years in this building. I know the difference.
lines.script: [stiff, offended, dignified] Not haunted. Grumpy. [firm, weathered] Thirty-one years in this building. I know the difference.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: The bells ring at random. The clocks in the hall all say different times. And the sign-up sheet got up off the table and walked into the school.
lines.script: [weary, listing, disbelieving] The bells ring at random. The clocks in the hall all say different times. [deadpan, haunted] And the sign-up sheet got up off the table and walked into the school.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: The Cafetorium doors run on the bell system. The bells run on the hallway clocks. Thirty parents are on their way, and those doors won't open.
lines.script: [urgent, laying out the problem] The Cafetorium doors run on the bell system. The bells run on the hallway clocks. [anxious] Thirty parents are on their way, and those doors won't open.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Doors don't just not open. That's not how doors work.
lines.script: [skeptical, bossy, arms crossed] Doors don't just not open. [matter-of-fact, smug] That's not how doors work.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Set every clock in the hall to seven. Seven o’clock. Not seven-thirty. Not six-fifty-nine. Seven.
lines.script: [precise, firm, instructing] Set every clock in the hall to seven. [insistent] Seven o'clock. [emphatic, ticking it off] Not seven-thirty. Not six-fifty-nine. [crisp] Seven.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. A school. At NIGHT. With MONSTERS, probably.
lines.script: [hushed, thrilled, tugging his sleeve] Tah Tah. [whispering, awestruck] A school. At NIGHT. [spooked, delighted] With MONSTERS, probably.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Stay close, everybody. This is a professional learning environment.
lines.script: [calm, protective, deadpan] Stay close, everybody. [dry] This is a professional learning environment.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...Every clock in this hall says a different time.
lines.script: [quiet, wary, scanning the hall] ...Every clock in this hall says a different time.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That one says four. That one says nine. That one is going BACKWARDS. I teach time, Tom. This is personal.
lines.script: [outraged, pointing at the clocks] That one says four. That one says nine. [indignant] That one is going BACKWARDS. [seething, personal] I teach time, Tom. [tight] This is personal.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata! Tata! SPARKLY FOOTPRINTS!
lines.script: [squealing, whisper-shout, discovery] Tah Tah! Tah Tah! [thrilled] SPARKLY FOOTPRINTS!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Little paper feet. With glitter. They go EVERYWHERE.
lines.script: [awed, tracing with her finger] Little paper feet. [excited, glee] With glitter. [sweeping, huge] They go EVERYWHERE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I can read the doors. Room One is ART. Room Two is MUSIC. Room Three is the GYM.
lines.script: [proud, reading, showing off] I can read the doors. [smug] Room One is ART. Room Two is MUSIC. [hesitant, unsure] Room Three is the GYM.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The gym isn't a room. It's a gym. It has a number anyway.
lines.script: [puzzled, fussy] The gym isn't a room. [shrugging, matter-of-fact] It's a gym. It has a number anyway.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The footprints go into all three. Then out again. Then east, to the Cafetorium.
lines.script: [detective, tracing the trail, serious] The footprints go into all three. Then out again. [pointing, dramatic] Then east, to the Cafetorium.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Girls. That's excellent detective work. Gold stars. Both of you.
lines.script: [proud, warm, teacher praise] Girls. That's excellent detective work. [cheerful, brisk] Gold stars. Both of you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we clear Art, Music and the Gym. After each one, we fix its clock. Seven o’clock.
lines.script: [calm, planning] Then we clear Art, Music and the Gym. [practical] After each one, we fix its clock. [firm] Seven o'clock.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: FOR EVERYONE, LOVE DEEDEE. That's Deedee’s handwriting! Everyone means us!
lines.script: [gasping, reading a note, thrilled] FOR EVERYONE, LOVE DEEDEE. [triumphant, bossy] That's Deedee's handwriting! [delighted, certain] Everyone means us!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Rhubarb crisp! Deedee brings the teachers CRISP?
lines.script: [astonished, delighted] Rhubarb crisp! [scandalized, impressed] Deedee brings the teachers CRISP?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: She never told me that. Of course she never told me that.
lines.script: [amused, exasperated, rueful] She never told me that. [resigned, fond] Of course she never told me that.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: To the moon and back. And apparently to the staff room.
lines.script: [dry, warm, fond] To the moon and back. [deadpan] And apparently to the staff room.

lines.speaker: Tardy Bell
lines.text: DING! You're LATE! Everybody is late! I ring and I ring and nobody is ever on time!
lines.script: [accusing, clanging, righteous] DING! You're LATE! [rising, aggrieved] Everybody is late! [wailing, bitter] I ring and I ring and nobody is ever on time!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I've never been late in my life. Not once. Not even when I was born. I was early.
lines.script: [stiff, offended, proud] I've never been late in my life. Not once. [dry, smug] Not even when I was born. [beat] I was early.

lines.speaker: Tardy Bell
lines.text: ...DING. Prove it.
lines.script: [sulky, deadpan, flat] ...DING. [challenging, sullen] Prove it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up! Everybody up! Walk it off. Hydrate. We go again.
lines.script: [coaching, brisk, clapping her hands] Up! Everybody up! [energetic] Walk it off. Hydrate. [rallying] We go again.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, listen. The clock outside the Art room stopped spinning.
lines.script: [hushed, noticing, tilting her head] Tah Tah, listen. [wondering] The clock outside the Art room stopped spinning.

lines.speaker: Glitter Glue
lines.text: Squelch. I glued the piano. I glued the xylophone. I glued a recorder to a tuba. It's ART.
lines.script: [sticky, gleeful, defiant] Squelch. I glued the piano. I glued the xylophone. [giddy, proud] I glued a recorder to a tuba. [defensive, grand] It's ART.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, it's SPARKLY. I love it. I hate it. I love it.
lines.script: [torn, whispering, dazzled] Tah Tah, it's SPARKLY. [dreamy] I love it. [scowling] I hate it. [swooning] I love it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You can't glue a xylophone. That's not how xylophones work.
lines.script: [bossy, scandalized, correcting] You can't glue a xylophone. [stern] That's not how xylophones work.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The glitter footprints stop here! And over there. And on Tata.
lines.script: [detective, excited, pointing] The glitter footprints stop here! And over there. [giggling] And on Tah Tah.

lines.speaker: Dodgeball Dread
lines.text: BOING. Everybody against the wall. Nobody picks me first. Nobody EVER picks me first.
lines.script: [bouncing, bitter, bellowing] BOING. Everybody against the wall. [wounded, sulky] Nobody picks me first. [aching] Nobody EVER picks me first.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Oh, I remember you. Fourth grade. You and me. Every Friday.
lines.script: [dawning recognition, gleeful menace] Oh, I remember you. [relishing] Fourth grade. You and me. [fond, competitive] Every Friday.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Amy was the scariest kid in dodgeball. They had to make a rule about her.
lines.script: [dry, amused, telling the girls] Amy was the scariest kid in dodgeball. [deadpan] They had to make a rule about her.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The Gregori Rule. No throwing at teachers. It's still on the wall.
lines.script: [proud, mock formal] The Gregori Rule. No throwing at teachers. [smug, fond] It's still on the wall.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You know I was terrified of that thing? Every Friday. That's why I threw so hard.
lines.script: [confessing, laughing at herself] You know I was terrified of that thing? Every Friday. [sheepish, competitive] That's why I threw so hard.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know. You threw one at me at Thanksgiving. I was holding a pie.
lines.script: [dry, long-suffering] I know. [deadpan] You threw one at me at Thanksgiving. [pointed] I was holding a pie.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You caught the pie, though.
lines.script: [sly, teasing, proud] You caught the pie, though.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I caught the pie.
lines.script: [dry, quietly smug] I caught the pie.

lines.speaker: School bell
lines.text: BRRRRRING. One bell. Right on time. Then silence. The good kind.
lines.script: [reading aloud, one clean ring, satisfied] BRRRRRING. One bell. Right on time. [hushed, peaceful] Then silence. The good kind.

lines.speaker: School bell
lines.text: BRRRRRING. One bell. Right on time. Then silence. The good kind.
lines.script: [reading aloud, one clean ring, satisfied] BRRRRRING. One bell. Right on time. [hushed, peaceful] Then silence. The good kind.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: (on the intercom) ...ksssh... Attention, please. The Cafetorium doors are OPEN. Parents, please wait in the hall. There's something in the Cafetorium.
lines.script: [crackling intercom, formal, relieved] (on the intercom) ...ksssh... Attention, please. [clear, announcing] The Cafetorium doors are OPEN. [measured] Parents, please wait in the hall. [ominous, careful] There's something in the Cafetorium.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Mrs. Gregori’s brother, please go into the Cafetorium. Thank you. ...ksssh.
lines.script: [intercom, polite, apologetic] Mrs. Gregori's brother, please go into the Cafetorium. [brisk] Thank you. [static fading] ...ksssh.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The footprints go in there. The sign-up sheet is in there.
lines.script: [tense, determined, low] The footprints go in there. The sign-up sheet is in there.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And the something.
lines.script: [hushed, ominous] And the something.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: There! The sign-up sheet! On the podium!
lines.script: [gasping, pointing, urgent] There! The sign-up sheet! On the podium!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It's covered in RED.
lines.script: [hushed, unnerved, small] It's covered in RED.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: Click. Wrong. Wrong. Wrong. Every name on this sheet is written wrong.
lines.script: [prissy, cold, tapping] Click. [scolding, clipped] Wrong. Wrong. Wrong. [disdainful] Every name on this sheet is written wrong.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: Kowalski has a W. Delgado has a G. Gregori has TWO Rs, and nobody ever writes them neatly.
lines.script: [nitpicky, indignant, rapid] Kowalski has a W. Delgado has a G. [aggrieved] Gregori has TWO Rs, [bitter] and nobody ever writes them neatly.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That's the conference sign-up sheet. Thirty parents are waiting for it.
lines.script: [stern, controlled, teacher voice] That's the conference sign-up sheet. [pointed] Thirty parents are waiting for it.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: A hundred thousand wrong answers, I've marked. Every quiz. Every spelling test. Every crooked line.
lines.script: [weary, aggrieved, building] A hundred thousand wrong answers, I've marked. [bitter] Every quiz. Every spelling test. [seething] Every crooked line.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: Nobody ever grades ME. Nobody ever writes NEAT next to ME. So tonight, I grade the grown-ups.
lines.script: [wounded, bitter] Nobody ever grades ME. [aching] Nobody ever writes NEAT next to ME. [cold, menacing] So tonight, I grade the grown-ups.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You took the sign-up sheet to grade it.
lines.script: [calm, perceptive, gentle] You took the sign-up sheet to grade it.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: And the bells. And the clocks. Late is late. Points off.
lines.script: [snippy, officious] And the bells. And the clocks. [curt, final] Late is late. Points off.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, it's a PEN. With GLASSES.
lines.script: [whisper-shout, thrilled] Tah Tah, it's a PEN. [delighted] With GLASSES.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I'm going to count to three, and you're going to put the sheet down. One.
lines.script: [steely, calm, teacher count] I'm going to count to three, and you're going to put the sheet down. [ominous, slow] One.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's her teacher voice. I'd listen.
lines.script: [low, dry, impressed, to the girls] That's her teacher voice. [deadpan] I'd listen.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up. Everybody. Walk it off.
lines.script: [rallying, coaching] Up. Everybody. [firm] Walk it off.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom, when it says SEE ME, step in front of them. Grace, Squishy anyone it circles. And somebody tell it its handwriting is nice. Three times.
lines.script: [tactical, brisk, coaching] Tom, when it says SEE ME, step in front of them. [directing] Grace, Squishy anyone it circles. [sly, strategic] And somebody tell it its handwriting is nice. [emphatic] Three times.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: Click. Fine. FINE. Pencils down. I'm going back in my cup.
lines.script: [deflated, huffy, grudging] Click. Fine. FINE. [sulky, small] Pencils down. [muttering] I'm going back in my cup.

lines.speaker: Podium
lines.text: The Red Pen clicks itself shut, rolls off the podium, and hops away down the hall toward the second grade room.
lines.script: [reading aloud, dry, amused] The Red Pen clicks itself shut, rolls off the podium, and hops away down the hall toward the second grade room.

lines.speaker: Podium
lines.text: The Red Pen clicks itself shut, rolls off the podium, and hops away down the hall toward the second grade room.
lines.script: [reading aloud, dry, amused] The Red Pen clicks itself shut, rolls off the podium, and hops away down the hall toward the second grade room.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: ...It's going to my desk. Of course it's going to my desk.
lines.script: [dawning dread, wry] ...It's going to my desk. [resigned, deadpan] Of course it's going to my desk.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The sign-up sheet! It's a bit crumpled. And look, Tata. Something is taped to the bottom.
lines.script: [excited, then curious] The sign-up sheet! It's a bit crumpled. [noticing, hushed] And look, Tah Tah. Something is taped to the bottom.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A gold coin. Again. Same little clock face.
lines.script: [quiet, studying the coin, wary] A gold coin. Again. [thoughtful] Same little clock face.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The sundial. The steamer. Now the sign-up sheet. Somebody keeps leaving these where we'll find them.
lines.script: [musing, piecing it together, low] The sundial. The steamer. Now the sign-up sheet. [uneasy, dry] Somebody keeps leaving these where we'll find them.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Whoever it is has very neat tape. Look at those corners.
lines.script: [admiring, wry, teacherly] Whoever it is has very neat tape. [impressed, leaning in] Look at those corners.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can we keep it? I'll keep it inside Lamby.
lines.script: [pleading, earnest] Can we keep it? [solemn, certain] I'll keep it inside Lamby.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We keep it. In my pocket. Not inside Lamby.
lines.script: [firm, dry, gentle] We keep it. In my pocket. [deadpan] Not inside Lamby.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: The sheet! The bells! The clocks! Parents, come on in! Conference night is ON!
lines.script: [jubilant, announcing] The sheet! The bells! The clocks! [booming, thrilled] Parents, come on in! Conference night is ON!

lines.speaker: Conference night
lines.text: For two hours, Amy talks to thirty parents. Grace hands out cookies. Rose tells everybody the pen had glasses. Tom stacks chairs and nods calmly.
lines.script: [reading aloud, wry, brisk summary] For two hours, Amy talks to thirty parents. Grace hands out cookies. [amused] Rose tells everybody the pen had glasses. [deadpan] Tom stacks chairs and nods calmly.

lines.speaker: Conference night
lines.text: For two hours, Amy talks to thirty parents. Grace hands out cookies. Rose tells everybody the pen had glasses. Tom stacks chairs and nods calmly.
lines.script: [reading aloud, wry, brisk summary] For two hours, Amy talks to thirty parents. Grace hands out cookies. [amused] Rose tells everybody the pen had glasses. [deadpan] Tom stacks chairs and nods calmly.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Mrs. Gregori. Best conference night in thirty-one years. Not one parent cried. Well. Mr. Delgado. Happy tears.
lines.script: [glowing, amazed, formal] Mrs. Gregori. Best conference night in thirty-one years. [dry, then softening] Not one parent cried. Well. [fond] Mr. Delgado. Happy tears.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: This is for you. My Golden Stopwatch. Thirty-one Field Days. It's never once stopped early.
lines.script: [solemn, touched, presenting it] This is for you. My Golden Stopwatch. [reverent, proud] Thirty-one Field Days. [tender] It's never once stopped early.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Principal Pruitt, I can't take this.
lines.script: [overwhelmed, polite, protesting] Principal Pruitt, I can't take this.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: ...I'm taking it. Thank you.
lines.script: [beat, yielding, delighted] ...I'm taking it. [warm, sincere] Thank you.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: And Field Day shirts. Staff shirts. You're all staff now. Even the small loud ones.
lines.script: [cheerful, generous] And Field Day shirts. Staff shirts. [warm, teasing] You're all staff now. [wry, glancing at Rose] Even the small loud ones.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Thirty conferences. Zero tears. One very well-behaved pen.
lines.script: [triumphant, tired, proud] Thirty conferences. Zero tears. [dry, satisfied] One very well-behaved pen.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Oh. A text. From Justin.
lines.script: [perking up, glancing at her phone, soft] Oh. A text. From Justin.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: "Heard it went great. Proud of you. Stuck at work till nine. Save me a cookie." With a little heart.
lines.script: [reading a text aloud, in Justin's easy voice] "Heard it went great. Proud of you. [tired, apologetic] Stuck at work till nine. [affectionate] Save me a cookie." [softening, smiling] With a little heart.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dad used the heart! He only uses the heart on special days!
lines.script: [gasping, thrilled, authoritative] Dad used the heart! [emphatic, certain] He only uses the heart on special days!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Girls. Did we save a cookie for Dad?
lines.script: [pointed, mock stern, to the girls] Girls. [teasing] Did we save a cookie for Dad?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: ...Define save.
lines.script: [caught, sly, innocent] ...Define save.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. Tata. There's a man.
lines.script: [hushed, tugging his sleeve, uneasy] Tah Tah. Tah Tah. [whisper] There's a man.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: By the last car. In a long coat. He's looking at us.
lines.script: [whispering, spooked, pointing] By the last car. [low, wide-eyed] In a long coat. [barely audible] He's looking at us.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...Nobody there.
lines.script: [quiet, scanning, uneasy] ...Nobody there.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Probably a parent. A late one. There's always a late one.
lines.script: [breezy, dismissive, a bit too quick] Probably a parent. [dry] A late one. There's always a late one.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Probably.
lines.script: [quiet, unconvinced] Probably.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A long coat. Gold coins. That's what Oolong’s kettle said, too. I'm keeping a list.
lines.script: [low, thinking, pulling a thread] A long coat. Gold coins. [dry, wry] That's what Oolong's kettle said, too. [deadpan] I'm keeping a list.

lines.script: [thrilled, hushed, delighted] Forty loaves, babe. FORTY. [giddy, listening] They're crackling. Listen to them. [tender, amazed] They're singing.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: That's the crust. That's what crust does when it's done right. Here. Take my peel. Fifty-one years of biscuits. It wants to work again.
lines.script: [warm, proud, rumbling] That's the crust. That's what crust does when it's done right. [gentle, offering] Here. Take my peel. [tender, hopeful] Fifty-one years of biscuits. It wants to work again.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The sundial. The steamer. The sign-up sheet. My jar. The book from 1952. And now an oven nobody has opened since 1963.
lines.script: [low, ticking it off, uneasy] The sundial. The steamer. The sign-up sheet. My jar. The book from nineteen fifty-two. [quiet, incredulous] And now an oven nobody has opened since nineteen sixty-three.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Somebody keeps getting into places nobody gets into. Very neat. Very quiet. Very spooky. I love it. I hate it.
lines.script: [hushed, relishing, delighted dread] Somebody keeps getting into places nobody gets into. Very neat. Very quiet. Very spooky. [giddy] I love it. [mock-pained] I hate it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Look at the corners. Not a speck of ash on it. Somebody put it there after the fire went out. I'm adding it to the list.
lines.script: [dry, sleuthing, quietly sure] Look at the corners. Not a speck of ash on it. [low, thoughtful] Somebody put it there after the fire went out. [flat, resolved] I'm adding it to the list.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Forty loaves. Six o’clock. On the dot. Potluck committee report: we're a success.
lines.script: [crisp, proud, officious] Forty loaves. Six o'clock. On the dot. [pleased, formal] Potluck committee report: we're a success.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: The gumbo is hot. The casserole is hot. Everything is hot. I'd like it noted.
lines.script: [smug, satisfied, prim] The gumbo is hot. The casserole is hot. Everything is hot. [pointed] I'd like it noted.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Noted, Bernadette.
lines.script: [amused, warm, easy] Noted, Bernadette.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: Tom. TOM. Nara is eating. Look at her. She's EATING.
lines.script: [overjoyed, breathless, tugging at Tom] Tom. TOM. [tearful, delighted] Nara is eating. Look at her. She's EATING.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Tom. Come here. This was my daddy’s. He drove the 7 line out of that barn for thirty years. Night run. He swore by the biscuits.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: He'd want it on somebody who went back in there and lit that stove. Here.
lines.script: [quiet, tender, moved] He'd want it on somebody who went back in there and lit that stove. [gentle, pressing it into his hand] Here.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...Thank you. I'll take very good care of it.
lines.script: [moved, quiet, a little choked] ...Thank you. [sincere, soft] I'll take very good care of it.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: I know you will. Now stand up straight. He'd say that too.
lines.script: [warm, knowing, gently teasing] I know you will. [gruff, fond] Now stand up straight. He'd say that too.

lines.speaker: Michael
lines.text: Lachlan has eaten three rolls and fallen asleep in the bread basket. I'm leaving him there. He's happy.
lines.script: [tired, deadpan, fond] Lachlan has eaten three rolls and fallen asleep in the bread basket. [dry, content] I'm leaving him there. He's happy.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You know what tonight was, babe? Toast.
lines.script: [mellow, setting up a joke, sly] You know what tonight was, babe? [beat, smug] Toast.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Because the bread. And we're TOASTING. It works on two levels.
lines.script: [proud, delighted, explaining] Because the bread. [grinning] And we're TOASTING. It works on two levels.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It works on one level. Barely.
lines.script: [flat, deadpan, dry] It works on one level. [beat] Barely.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...I love that level.
lines.script: [soft, fond, surrendering] ...I love that level.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A text from Deedee. "Honey. A letter came for you at our house. Fancy envelope. Gold wax seal with a little clock on it."
lines.script: [reading aloud, in Deedee's fussy warm voice, curious] A text from Deedee. "Honey. A letter came for you at our house. [intrigued] Fancy envelope. Gold wax seal with a little clock on it."

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: "It says THE MOON CLUB. Nobody gets invited to the Moon Club. I've lived here forty years. I love you to the moon and back. Call me."
lines.script: [reading aloud, in Deedee's breathless voice, awed] "It says THE MOON CLUB. [emphatic] Nobody gets invited to the Moon Club. I've lived here forty years. [loving, warm] I love you to the moon and back. Call me."

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The Moon Club. Babe. That's a secret society. I've seen this movie. Several times. It never goes well for the tall one.
lines.script: [delighted dread, dramatic, leaning in] The Moon Club. Babe. That's a secret society. [wry, knowing] I've seen this movie. Several times. [deadpan, teasing] It never goes well for the tall one.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A little clock. On the seal.
lines.script: [quiet, dry, turning it over] A little clock. [low, uneasy] On the seal.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. TATA. Deedee has a LETTER for you. It's GOLD. She won't let us open it.
lines.script: [breathless, bursting, bossy] Tah Tah. TAH TAH. Deedee has a LETTER for you. [thrilled] It's GOLD. [aggrieved] She won't let us open it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: She let us hold it. For one second. Then she took it back and said, careful, that's wax.
lines.script: [wistful, indignant, recounting] She let us hold it. For one second. [mimicking, prim] Then she took it back and said, careful, that's wax.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It smells like a candle. I licked it a little.
lines.script: [earnest, matter of fact, sheepish] It smells like a candle. [small, guilty] I licked it a little.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You licked my mail.
lines.script: [deadpan, flat, accusing] You licked my mail.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: A LITTLE.
lines.script: [defensive, firm, whisper-shout] A LITTLE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Also the moon is gone. Look. It's supposed to be a full moon. Luna said so. Luna is very upset.
lines.script: [dramatic, urgent, pointing at the sky] Also the moon is gone. Look. [insistent] It's supposed to be a full moon. Luna said so. [solemn, worried] Luna is very upset.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...There's no moon.
lines.script: [quiet, stunned, looking up] ...There's no moon.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: There's no moon, and I have a gold letter. Okay.
lines.script: [dry, bewildered, resigned] There's no moon, and I have a gold letter. [flat, steeling himself] Okay.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tommy! There you are. Sit. No, stand. Read it. Read it out loud. I have read it eleven times.
lines.script: [bossy, bursting, fussing] Tommy! There you are. Sit. [flustered] No, stand. [urgent, pushing it at him] Read it. Read it out loud. [proud, breathless] I have read it eleven times.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: "THE MOON CLUB requests the pleasure of TOM. Tonight, at moonrise. Admit three. Adults only. Dress: your very best."
lines.script: [reading aloud, formal, grand, dry] "THE MOON CLUB requests the pleasure of TOM. [slow, mysterious] Tonight, at moonrise. Admit three. Adults only. [stiffly, a little amused] Dress: your very best."

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Gold wax seal. A little clock on it.
lines.script: [quiet, studying, wary] Gold wax seal. [low] A little clock on it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: ADULTS ONLY? I'm basically an adult. I have a YouTube channel. I have a SKINCARE ROUTINE.
lines.script: [scandalized, outraged, indignant] ADULTS ONLY? [dramatic, arguing] I'm basically an adult. I have a YouTube channel. [haughty, proud] I have a SKINCARE ROUTINE.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I'm six. Is six adults?
lines.script: [small, hopeful, earnest] I'm six. [innocent, literal] Is six adults?

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: Girls. You're staying with me. I brought cards. I cheat. You'll learn a great deal.
lines.script: [dry, grand, indulgent, wicked] Girls. You're staying with me. [sly, relishing] I brought cards. I cheat. [serene] You'll learn a great deal.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Forty years I've lived in this town. Every full moon, the lights used to go on in that dome above Luna’s. Nobody I know has ever been invited. Not once.
lines.script: [wistful, marveling, a little hurt] Forty years I've lived in this town. [recalling] Every full moon, the lights used to go on in that dome above Luna's. [emphatic] Nobody I know has ever been invited. Not once.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Admit three, Tommy. You. Me. And Boppy.
lines.script: [decisive, bossy, proud] Admit three, Tommy. [brisk, counting off] You. Me. [pointed] And Boppy.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I'm not wearing a tie.
lines.script: [gruff, grumbling, dreading it] I'm not wearing a tie.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: You're wearing the tie.
lines.script: [firm, sweet-bossy, no argument] You're wearing the tie.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...I'm wearing the tie.
lines.script: [beat, grumbling, defeated, dry] ...I'm wearing the tie.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: The Moon Club. I haven't heard that name since 1971.
lines.script: [hushed, faraway, wistful] The Moon Club. [slow, dreamy, amused] I haven't heard that name since nineteen seventy-one.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You went?
lines.script: [surprised, curious, a beat] You went?

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: Darling, I went to everything. The last dance. A big silver ball turned all night. Then they locked the doors and nobody ever said why.
lines.script: [grand, breezy, nostalgic] Darling, I went to everything. [dreamy, savoring] The last dance. A big silver ball turned all night. [dropping, mysterious] Then they locked the doors and nobody ever said why.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: I left a coat there. Purple velvet. I was in a hurry.
lines.script: [airy, offhand, rueful] I left a coat there. Purple velvet. [sheepish, shrugging] I was in a hurry.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: And now the moon is missing. Three nights. I power walk at nine. I walked straight into the Hendersons’ hedge.
lines.script: [exasperated, wounded, indignant] And now the moon is missing. Three nights. [dry, aggrieved] I power walk at nine. [flat] I walked straight into the Hendersons' hedge.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A missing moon, a locked club, and a little gold clock. Everybody get your shoes.
lines.script: [dry, resolute, rallying] A missing moon, a locked club, and a little gold clock. [firm, brisk] Everybody get your shoes.

lines.speaker: Luna
lines.text: Oh! Visitors. At night. Is that... is that an INVITATION?
lines.script: [startled, delighted, breathless] Oh! Visitors. [hushed wonder] At night. [giddy] Is that... is that an INVITATION?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The Moon Club. Tonight. Admit three.
lines.script: [dry, formal, handing over the envelope] The Moon Club. Tonight. [crisp] Admit three.

lines.speaker: Luna
lines.text: Twelve years I have swept this floor. That little silver door in the back has never once opened. I thought it was a closet.
lines.script: [wistful, a little sheepish] Twelve years I have swept this floor. [puzzled] That little silver door in the back has never once opened. [rueful] I thought it was a closet.

lines.speaker: Luna
lines.text: And my telescope can't find the moon. It's not behind a cloud. It's not anywhere. It's just GONE.
lines.script: [wistful, then rising worry] And my telescope can't find the moon. [anxious] It's not behind a cloud. It's not anywhere. [stricken] It's just GONE.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Honey, show her the seal.
lines.script: [warm, nudging, bossy love] Honey, show her the seal.

lines.speaker: Little silver door
lines.text: Tom holds up the invitation. The brass moon on the little door clicks, and the door swings open by itself.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed storybook narrator] Tom holds up the invitation. [soft magic] The brass moon on the little door clicks, and the door swings open by itself.

lines.speaker: Little silver door
lines.text: Tom holds up the invitation. The brass moon on the little door clicks, and the door swings open by itself.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed storybook narrator] Tom holds up the invitation. [soft magic] The brass moon on the little door clicks, and the door swings open by itself.

lines.speaker: Luna
lines.text: ...It wasn't a closet.
lines.script: [stunned, whispering, awed] ...It wasn't a closet.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Stairs. Of course it's stairs. Nobody take them fast.
lines.script: [gruff, resigned groan] Stairs. [dry, grumbling] Of course it's stairs. [warning, pointed] Nobody take them fast.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh. Oh, Tommy. It's beautiful.
lines.script: [hushed, moved, hand on heart] Oh. Oh, Tommy. [tender] It's beautiful.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: It's FILTHY. Fifty years of dust. Somebody hand me a mop.
lines.script: [switching to briskly appalled] It's FILTHY. [rolling up sleeves, commanding] Fifty years of dust. Somebody hand me a mop.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Nobody is here. A party and nobody is here.
lines.script: [gruff, unimpressed, looking around] Nobody is here. [grumbling] A party and nobody is here.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Look at the east window. Moonlight. Just a thread of it.
lines.script: [quiet, noticing, pointing] Look at the east window. [soft, wondering] Moonlight. Just a thread of it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The moon isn't gone. Something up in the Dome is pulling all of its light inside. Only a little gets out.
lines.script: [thoughtful, working it out] The moon isn't gone. [serious, low] Something up in the Dome is pulling all of its light inside. [grave] Only a little gets out.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Somebody read me that plaque. My glasses are in my other purse.
lines.script: [bustling, mildly flustered] Somebody read me that plaque. [fussing, patting her purse] My glasses are in my other purse.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: You're wearing them, Dee.
lines.script: [dry, patient, deadpan] You're wearing them, Dee.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh. So I am. Well then.
lines.script: [blinking, caught out] Oh. So I am. [breezy, unbothered] Well then.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: The plaque says MEMBERS ARE ADMITTED BY MOONLIGHT. And look, three little brass stands. Somebody took the mirrors.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: A coat check, a card room, a ballroom. Three rooms. Three stands. I count three suspects.
lines.script: [gruff, detective mode, counting off] A coat check, a card room, a ballroom. Three rooms. Three stands. [flat, certain] I count three suspects.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Assistant Deputy Warden. Rikers. I know what a lineup looks like.

lines.speaker: The Hanger-On
lines.text: That was 1971. I haven't let go once. I'm VERY good at hanging on.
lines.script: [faint, wistful, then proud] That was nineteen seventy-one. [steady, stubborn] I haven't let go once. [chirpy, boasting] I'm VERY good at hanging on.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Purple velvet. Tommy. That's Aunt Ellie’s coat.
lines.script: [gasping, delighted recognition] Purple velvet. Tommy. [hushed, thrilled] That's Aunt Ellie’s coat.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And our mirror is hanging off your other shoulder.
lines.script: [dry, calm, pointing] And our mirror is hanging off your other shoulder.

lines.speaker: The Hanger-On
lines.text: Nobody gets anything without a ticket.

lines.text: Okay, everybody up. Deedee is a nurse. Up, up. Little sip of water. Good.

lines.text: ...Okay. Okay. You can take it to her. Tell her I held on the whole time.

lines.text: We'll tell her, honey. She'll be so pleased. She'll pretend not to be. That's how you know.

lines.text: A round mirror in a brass frame. It says MIRROR 1 on the back. It goes on a stand in the hall.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Three mirrors. Three stands. One little moonbeam. I didn't drive a car for forty years without learning about mirrors.
lines.script: [gruff, puffed up, lecturing] Three mirrors. Three stands. One little moonbeam. [smug] I didn't drive a car for forty years without learning about mirrors.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: You drove into the mailbox twice, honey.
lines.script: [sweet, gently teasing] You drove into the mailbox twice, honey.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The mailbox moved.
lines.script: [deadpan, dignified, not backing down] The mailbox moved.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Gin rummy with Deedee, fifty years. I've never won a hand. Not one. I know a sore loser when I see one.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: You ARE a sore loser, honey.
lines.script: [teasing, affectionate] You ARE a sore loser, honey.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I'm a sore WINNER. Who hasn't won yet.
lines.script: [grumbling, indignant, sulky] I'm a sore WINNER. [dry mutter] Who hasn't won yet.

lines.speaker: The Sore Loser
lines.text: ...Best two out of three?
lines.script: [sulky, hopeful, small] ...Best two out of three?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Sunday. My house. Bring your own deck. You'll lose. I'll lose too. We can lose together.
lines.script: [gruff, warming, kindly] Sunday. My house. Bring your own deck. [dry] You'll lose. I'll lose too. [chuckling] We can lose together.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Look at you. Making a friend.
lines.script: [delighted, proud, warm] Look at you. Making a friend.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: A round mirror in a brass frame. It says MIRROR 2 on the back. It goes on a stand in the hall.
lines.script: [reading aloud, dry, matter of fact] A round mirror in a brass frame. It says MIRROR two on the back. It goes on a stand in the hall.

lines.text: Oh. Oh no. People. Don't look at me. I'm just here. With the wall. And this mirror. Which I'm hiding behind.
lines.script: [panicked whisper, shrinking] Oh. Oh no. People. [frantic, small] Don't look at me. I'm just here. [mumbling] With the wall. And this mirror. [tiny] Which I'm hiding behind.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh, sweetheart. Nobody asked you to dance, did they?
lines.script: [soft, sympathetic, motherly] Oh, sweetheart. [gentle] Nobody asked you to dance, did they?

lines.speaker: The Wallflower
lines.text: Every song, 1924 to 1971. I stood right here. Nobody. Ever.
lines.script: [quiet, aching, lonely] Every song, nineteen twenty-four to nineteen seventy-one. I stood right here. [barely a whisper] Nobody. Ever.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we'll ask. Nicely. After you give us the mirror.
lines.script: [gentle, kind, firm] Then we'll ask. Nicely. [dry, warm] After you give us the mirror.

lines.speaker: The Wallflower
lines.text: ...You were very nice about it. For a fight. Here. The mirror. It was the big one, over the bandstand, before she came.
lines.script: [softened, shy, surprised] ...You were very nice about it. For a fight. [offering, hesitant] Here. The mirror. [confiding, wistful] It was the big one, over the bandstand, before she came.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: She?
lines.script: [sharp, alert, quiet] She?

lines.speaker: The Wallflower
lines.text: The Mirrorball. Up in the Dome. She hasn't stopped spinning in three nights.
lines.script: [hushed, uneasy, looking up] The Mirrorball. Up in the Dome. [worried] She hasn't stopped spinning in three nights.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: A round mirror in a brass frame. It says MIRROR 3 on the back. It goes on a stand in the hall.
lines.script: [reading aloud, dry, matter of fact] A round mirror in a brass frame. It says MIRROR three on the back. It goes on a stand in the hall.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: A slow one. My stomach gets one song. One. Deedee. May I.
lines.script: [gruff, tender, courtly] A slow one. [dry, bargaining] My stomach gets one song. One. [softer, gallant] Deedee. May I.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Fifty-two years, and he still asks. Every time.
lines.script: [misty, fond, soft] Fifty-two years, and he still asks. [warm, tender] Every time.

lines.speaker: Ballroom
lines.text: They dance across the dusty floor, slow and small and very close. Boppy doesn't mention his stomach once.
lines.script: [reading aloud, soft, tender narrator] They dance across the dusty floor, slow and small and very close. [gently amused] Boppy doesn't mention his stomach once.

lines.speaker: Ballroom
lines.text: They dance across the dusty floor, slow and small and very close. Boppy doesn't mention his stomach once.
lines.script: [reading aloud, soft, tender narrator] They dance across the dusty floor, slow and small and very close. [gently amused] Boppy doesn't mention his stomach once.

lines.text: The thread of moonlight bounces off three mirrors and lands right in the middle of the moon-shaped lock. It glows. Click. CLUNK.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, magical narrator] The thread of moonlight bounces off three mirrors and lands right in the middle of the moon-shaped lock. It glows. [crisp] Click. [heavy, resonant] CLUNK.

lines.speaker: Dome doors
lines.text: The thread of moonlight bounces off three mirrors and lands right in the middle of the moon-shaped lock. It glows. Click. CLUNK.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, magical narrator] The thread of moonlight bounces off three mirrors and lands right in the middle of the moon-shaped lock. It glows. [crisp] Click. [heavy, resonant] CLUNK.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Admitted by moonlight. Oh, I have goosebumps. Tommy, feel my arm.
lines.script: [breathless, thrilled, goosebumps] Admitted by moonlight. Oh, I have goosebumps. [urgent, fussing] Tommy, feel my arm.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Somebody up there is playing music. Very loud music. In 1971 they called that a nuisance.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tommy. Over the bandstand. It's so BRIGHT. I can't look at it. I'm looking at it.

lines.text: Guests! GUESTS! Oh, at last. Welcome to the Moon Club. Nobody has come up those stairs since 1971.

lines.text: Every full moon, they danced under me. Then the last dance. The band said see you next moon. Nobody came back.

lines.text: So you took the moon.
lines.script: [dry, steady, putting it together] So you took the moon.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: I CAUGHT it. All of it. Every bit of moonlight, right here in me.
lines.script: [defiant, clutching, desperate pride] I CAUGHT it. [fierce, hugging it close] All of it. Every bit of moonlight, right here in me.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: If I'm the brightest thing in the whole sky, somebody will HAVE to come dance. And look. Somebody did.
lines.script: [desperate logic, glittering] If I'm the brightest thing in the whole sky, somebody will HAVE to come dance. [brightening, hopeful] And look. [thrilled, voice cracking] Somebody did.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Honey, there's a whole town walking into hedges down there.
lines.script: [gentle, practical, a little scolding] Honey, there's a whole town walking into hedges down there.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: Then they can come UP. One more dance. Just one. Everybody, under me, forever.
lines.script: [stubborn, escalating, pleading] Then they can come UP. [wheedling] One more dance. Just one. [ominous, possessive] Everybody, under me, forever.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Forever is a lot of dancing. And everybody dances too fast.
lines.script: [dry, gruff, deadpan] Forever is a lot of dancing. [grumbling aside] And everybody dances too fast.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Deedee, Boppy, behind me. No touching, please.
lines.script: [calm, protective, firm] Deedee, Boppy, behind me. [dry, steady] No touching, please.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Up, everybody. Deedee is a nurse.
lines.script: [brisk, rallying, nurse mode] Up, everybody. Deedee is a nurse.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tommy, whatever her shiny side shows bounces right back. Use something else. And honey, nobody has asked her to dance since 1971. Three times.
lines.script: [urgent, whispering a tip, coaching] Tommy, whatever her shiny side shows bounces right back. Use something else. [soft, tender, insightful] And honey, nobody has asked her to dance since nineteen seventy-one. [meaningful] Three times.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: ...Fine. The party is over. It was over in 1971. I just didn't want to be the one to turn off the lights.
lines.script: [deflated, quiet, giving up] ...Fine. [heavy, hollow] The party is over. It was over in nineteen seventy-one. [aching, small] I just didn't want to be the one to turn off the lights.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh, honey. Nobody has to turn off the lights. We'll come back. Every full moon. I'll bring crisp.
lines.script: [melting, tender, motherly] Oh, honey. [warm, reassuring] Nobody has to turn off the lights. We'll come back. Every full moon. [gently practical] I'll bring crisp.

lines.speaker: The Dome
lines.text: The Mirrorball turns once, slowly, and lets go. A great round light rises out of her, up through the glass, and settles in the sky. The moon. Right where it belongs.
lines.script: [reading aloud, soft, awestruck narrator] The Mirrorball turns once, slowly, and lets go. [hushed, glowing] A great round light rises out of her, up through the glass, and settles in the sky. [warm, satisfied] The moon. Right where it belongs.

lines.speaker: The Dome
lines.text: The Mirrorball turns once, slowly, and lets go. A great round light rises out of her, up through the glass, and settles in the sky. The moon. Right where it belongs.
lines.script: [reading aloud, soft, awestruck narrator] The Mirrorball turns once, slowly, and lets go. [hushed, glowing] A great round light rises out of her, up through the glass, and settles in the sky. [warm, satisfied] The moon. Right where it belongs.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: One dance. Before you go. Somebody. Please.
lines.script: [shy, small, hopeful plea] One dance. Before you go. [trembling] Somebody. Please.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tommy. Dance with your mother.
lines.script: [warm, bossy love, gently insistent] Tommy. Dance with your mother.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I mostly sway.
lines.script: [dry, sheepish, deadpan] I mostly sway.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Then sway with your mother.
lines.script: [tender, unbothered, smiling] Then sway with your mother.

lines.speaker: The Dome
lines.text: Tom and Deedee sway under the Mirrorball, and a thousand little moons go round and round the Dome. Boppy keeps time on the bass drum. Badly. Proudly.
lines.script: [reading aloud, soft, fond narrator] Tom and Deedee sway under the Mirrorball, and a thousand little moons go round and round the Dome. [amused, affectionate] Boppy keeps time on the bass drum. [wry beat] Badly. [warm] Proudly.

lines.speaker: The Dome
lines.text: Tom and Deedee sway under the Mirrorball, and a thousand little moons go round and round the Dome. Boppy keeps time on the bass drum. Badly. Proudly.
lines.script: [reading aloud, soft, fond narrator] Tom and Deedee sway under the Mirrorball, and a thousand little moons go round and round the Dome. [amused, affectionate] Boppy keeps time on the bass drum. [wry beat] Badly. [warm] Proudly.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: Here. One of my little mirrors. For the lady who said she'd come back. So you can carry a bit of the moon home.
lines.script: [tender, shy, offering a gift] Here. One of my little mirrors. [soft, grateful] For the lady who said she'd come back. [gentle] So you can carry a bit of the moon home.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Something fell out of her top. On the bandstand. Something gold.
lines.script: [gruff, alert, nodding toward it] Something fell out of her top. On the bandstand. [curious] Something gold.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The sundial. The steamer. The sign-up sheet. My jar. The book from 1952. The oven from 1963. Now a mirrorball from 1971.
lines.script: [dry, building momentum, ticking off a list] The sundial. The steamer. The sign-up sheet. My jar. The book from nineteen fifty-two. The oven from nineteen sixty-three. [quiet realization] Now a mirrorball from nineteen seventy-one.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Somebody invited you up here, Tommy. Not her. She can't hold a pen. She's a ball.
lines.script: [thoughtful, sharp, motherly deduction] Somebody invited you up here, Tommy. [gently amused] Not her. She can't hold a pen. She's a ball.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Somebody who knew you'd come. And that you'd bring your mother.
lines.script: [warm, quietly proud, knowing] Somebody who knew you'd come. [tender] And that you'd bring your mother.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Somebody with a little clock. I'm adding it to the list.
lines.script: [dry, resolute, mildly intrigued] Somebody with a little clock. [deadpan] I'm adding it to the list.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: TATA! The MOON came back! We saw it from the window! Aunt Ellie said it was probably you.
lines.script: [bursting, breathless, thrilled] TAH TAH! The MOON came back! [excited, bossy] We saw it from the window! [smug, delighted] Aunt Ellie said it was probably you.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I won at cards. I cheated. Aunt Ellie said I'm a natural.
lines.script: [smug, matter-of-fact, grinning] I won at cards. [proudly unrepentant] I cheated. [beaming] Aunt Ellie said I'm a natural.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: She is. It's frightening. Well? Was there a ball?
lines.script: [dry, grand, deadpan pride] She is. [low, wry] It's frightening. [imperious, curious] Well? Was there a ball?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Ellie. There was a BALL. A big silver one. She remembered you. And look what we brought home.
lines.script: [bursting with news, emphatic] Ellie. There was a BALL. [warm, tender] A big silver one. She remembered you. [proud, presenting] And look what we brought home.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: ...My coat. Ticket seven.
lines.script: [stunned, soft, a long-lost memory] ...My coat. [barely there] Ticket seven.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: I left it at the last dance. I was in a hurry. I had a date with a man who turned out to be a disappointment. The coat wasn't.
lines.script: [wry, grand, matter of fact] I left it at the last dance. I was in a hurry. [arch, deadpan] I had a date with a man who turned out to be a disappointment. [dry beat, then fond] The coat wasn't.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: It hasn't fit me since 1972. Keep it, Tom. Somebody in this family should wear velvet properly.
lines.script: [dry, imperious, secretly generous] It hasn't fit me since nineteen seventy-two. [gruff warmth] Keep it, Tom. [arch] Somebody in this family should wear velvet properly.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I wore the tie. Everybody saw. Nobody can say I didn't wear the tie.
lines.script: [gruff, dignified, chin up] I wore the tie. Everybody saw. [firm, deadpan] Nobody can say I didn't wear the tie.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tommy, there was something else in the envelope. Stuck to the bottom. I didn't see it. I read it eleven times and I didn't see it.
lines.script: [puzzled, a little embarrassed, earnest] Tommy, there was something else in the envelope. Stuck to the bottom. [baffled] I didn't see it. [rueful, emphatic] I read it eleven times and I didn't see it.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Eleven times. Without her glasses. Eleven.
lines.script: [dry, dead calm, pointed] Eleven times. [deadpan] Without her glasses. [flat] Eleven.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I couldn't FIND them, honey.
lines.script: [defensive, huffy, flustered] I couldn't FIND them, honey.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A boarding pass. "BOARDING GROUP 0. FROM: LONG ISLAND. TO: NOWHERE. GATE: TO BE ANNOUNCED." And a little gold clock.
lines.script: [reading aloud, dry, curious] A boarding pass. [crisp, reading the print] "BOARDING GROUP zero. FROM: LONG ISLAND. TO: NOWHERE. GATE: TO BE ANNOUNCED." [quiet, intrigued] And a little gold clock.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: There's no boarding group zero. I have flown Delta One forty times. I'd know.
lines.script: [dry, offended frequent flyer, flat] There's no boarding group zero. [deadpan, certain] I have flown Delta One forty times. I'd know.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. Somebody wants you to go on a TRIP.
lines.script: [bright, bossy, thrilled] Tah Tah. [delighted, certain] Somebody wants you to go on a TRIP.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can I come? I'll be good. I'll be medium good.
lines.script: [hopeful, earnest, bargaining] Can I come? [solemn promise] I'll be good. [honest, serious] I'll be medium good.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: TOM. Don't get in that cab.
lines.script: [sharp, urgent, commanding, sprinting up] TOM. [firm, protective] Don't get in that cab.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You're not taking my girls to a closed airport at midnight without me.
lines.script: [fierce, low, mother bear] You're not taking my girls to a closed airport at midnight without me.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Every clock in our house stopped at twelve. The microwave. The oven. My running watch. My RUNNING WATCH, Tom.
lines.script: [rising alarm, ticking off grievances] Every clock in our house stopped at twelve. The microwave. The oven. [aggrieved, escalating] My running watch. [outraged] My RUNNING WATCH, Tom.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Every clock in town. Sal says zero o’clock.
lines.script: [dry, calm, filling her in] Every clock in town. [deadpan] Sal says zero o’clock.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Mom, it's SO good. We have boarding passes. Well. Tata has one. And Sal has one. Group ZERO.
lines.script: [excited, bossy, talking fast] Mom, it's SO good. We have boarding passes. [correcting herself, matter of fact] Well. Tah Tah has one. And Sal has one. [triumphant] Group ZERO.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I'm in group zero too. I decided.
lines.script: [serious, earnest, declaring] I'm in group zero too. [firm, proud] I decided.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Fine. I have run through every airport in America. I've never missed a connection.
lines.script: [sighing, giving in, competitive] Fine. [brisk, proud] I have run through every airport in America. I've never missed a connection.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Justin is at the shop, rewiring the whole block by flashlight. He says go. He says bring snacks.
lines.script: [quick, softer, fond] Justin is at the shop, rewiring the whole block by flashlight. [light, amused] He says go. He says bring snacks.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Cab seven! Everybody in. Long Island Regional. The door nobody uses.
lines.script: [booming, cheerful, proud] Cab seven! Everybody in. [fast, official] Long Island Regional. [lowering, conspiratorial] The door nobody uses.

lines.speaker: Speaker
lines.text: DING. Good evening, and welcome to Terminal Zero. Flight Zero to Nowhere is now boarding at Gate Zero. Boarding Group Zero only.
lines.script: [cheerful chime, hollow echoing PA announcer] DING. Good evening, and welcome to Terminal Zero. [flat, bureaucratic] Flight Zero to Nowhere is now boarding at Gate Zero. [clipped] Boarding Group Zero only.

lines.speaker: Speaker
lines.text: DING. Passengers are reminded that the gate clock is missing its hands. Passengers will kindly find them.
lines.script: [hollow PA announcer, mild reproach] DING. Passengers are reminded that the gate clock is missing its hands. [flat, expectant] Passengers will kindly find them.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A gate agent who makes the passengers fix the clock. I have flown Delta One forty times. That's a first.
lines.script: [dry, mildly impressed, deadpan] A gate agent who makes the passengers fix the clock. [amused, flat] I have flown Delta One forty times. That's a first.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Directory. Security top left. Baggage Claim top right. The Lounge bottom left. Gate Zero, up the middle.
lines.script: [brisk, reading the map, pointing] Directory. Security top left. Baggage Claim top right. The Lounge bottom left. [decisive] Gate Zero, up the middle.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Everything is from the olden days. That phone has a CORD. Rose. Rose, don't lick the phone.
lines.script: [amazed, dramatic, scandalized by old tech] Everything is from the olden days. That phone has a CORD. [urgent, hissing, scolding] Rose. Rose, don't lick the phone.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I was SMELLING it.
lines.script: [indignant, serious, offended] I was SMELLING it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Every board says midnight. Every gate says zero. And somebody dusted the plants.
lines.script: [dry, observant, quietly uneasy] Every board says midnight. Every gate says zero. [wry beat, amused] And somebody dusted the plants.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Stay close, everybody. Shoes on. Liquids in a bag.
lines.script: [calm, parental, steady] Stay close, everybody. [dry, practical] Shoes on. Liquids in a bag.

lines.speaker: The Long Line
lines.text: Please wait to be called. PLEASE. WAIT. TO BE CALLED.
lines.script: [stern, bureaucratic, rising to a bark] Please wait to be called. [clipped, shouting each word] PLEASE. WAIT. TO BE CALLED.

lines.speaker: The Long Line
lines.text: Nobody has reached the front of me since 1989. I'm holding the hour hand. Nobody gets an hour without waiting for it.
lines.script: [weary, hollow, long-suffering] Nobody has reached the front of me since nineteen eighty-nine. [flat, matter of fact] I'm holding the hour hand. [grim, pronouncing like a rule] Nobody gets an hour without waiting for it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I don't wait in lines. I move to the front, and I say thank you to every single person on the way.
lines.script: [brisk, cocky, competitive] I don't wait in lines. [smug, breezy] I move to the front, and I say thank you to every single person on the way.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Shoes off, everyone. Not you, Rose. Rose, put your shoe back on.
lines.script: [dry, herding, brisk] Shoes off, everyone. [sharp, exasperated, quick] Not you, Rose. Rose, put your shoe back on.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up! Everybody up! Walk it off. Hydrate. We have a flight to catch. Probably.
lines.script: [coaching, energetic, clapping] Up! Everybody up! Walk it off. Hydrate. [dry, wry] We have a flight to catch. [shrug] Probably.

lines.speaker: The Long Line
lines.text: ...Next. NEXT! You. You're at the front. Somebody is finally at the front.
lines.script: [stunned, trembling, disbelieving] ...Next. [bursting, overjoyed] NEXT! [tearful, pointing] You. You're at the front. [wondering, cracking] Somebody is finally at the front.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I'm at the front! I'm the FRONT! Do I win?
lines.script: [squealing, thrilled, jumping] I'm at the front! I'm the FRONT! [breathless, hopeful] Do I win?

lines.speaker: The Long Line
lines.text: You win. Here. The hour hand. Go on through.
lines.script: [warm, proud, formal, a tear in the voice] You win. [gentle, handing it over] Here. The hour hand. Go on through.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: A long brass clock hand. Stamped on the back: GATE 0, HOUR. It goes on the gate clock.
lines.script: [reading aloud, dry, matter of fact] A long brass clock hand. Stamped on the back: GATE zero, HOUR. It goes on the gate clock.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Three hands. The clock still isn't moving. Tom. The slots round the face. There are seven of them.
lines.script: [counting, brisk, analytical] Three hands. The clock still isn't moving. [pointing, sharp] Tom. The slots round the face. [flat, noticing] There are seven of them.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Seven slots. And I have seven gold coins. In a sock. In my bag.
lines.script: [dry, quiet realization, a beat of sheepishness] Seven slots. [deadpan, confessing] And I have seven gold coins. In a sock. In my bag.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I've been keeping a list. I have also been keeping the coins.
lines.script: [dry, sheepish, deadpan] I've been keeping a list. [wry] I have also been keeping the coins.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: They go in the order we found them! Like a clock. Going round. I KNEW the list was important.
lines.script: [triumphant, bossy, lighting up] They go in the order we found them! Like a clock. Going round. [smug, vindicated] I KNEW the list was important.

lines.speaker: The Unclaimed
lines.text: Round and round. Round and round. Every other bag got picked up. Every one. Since 1989.
lines.script: [droning, wistful, weary] Round and round. Round and round. [flat, aggrieved] Every other bag got picked up. Every one. [small, forlorn] Since nineteen eighty-nine.

lines.speaker: The Unclaimed
lines.text: I have the minute hand. It goes round and round too. We understand each other.
lines.script: [mournful, quietly pleased to have company] I have the minute hand. It goes round and round too. [soft, wistful] We understand each other.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It has SO many stickers. Tata, look. Paris. Tokyo. Cleveland.
lines.script: [excited, impressed, fascinated] It has SO many stickers. Tah Tah, look. [reading off, awed] Paris. Tokyo. [flat, funny] Cleveland.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A well-traveled bag. We'll pick you up. After you give us the minute hand.
lines.script: [dry, kind, respectful] A well-traveled bag. [warm, gentle] We'll pick you up. [wry] After you give us the minute hand.

lines.speaker: The Unclaimed
lines.text: ...You stopped the carousel. For me.
lines.script: [hushed, disbelieving, moved] ...You stopped the carousel. [small, tender] For me.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I'm picking you up. Officially. You're claimed. I'm putting a sticker on you. It says GRACE.
lines.script: [bossy, tender, official] I'm picking you up. Officially. You're claimed. [delighted, announcing] I'm putting a sticker on you. [proud] It says GRACE.

lines.speaker: The Unclaimed
lines.text: Claimed. Oh. Here. The minute hand. Take it to the gate.
lines.script: [overwhelmed, glowing, tearful joy] Claimed. Oh. [gentle, handing it over] Here. The minute hand. Take it to the gate.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: A long brass clock hand. Stamped on the back: GATE 0, MINUTE. It goes on the gate clock.
lines.script: [reading aloud, dry, matter of fact] A long brass clock hand. Stamped on the back: GATE zero, MINUTE. It goes on the gate clock.

lines.speaker: The Armrest Hog
lines.text: Occupied. All of them. Both armrests. The middle seat. The window. Mine.
lines.script: [territorial, flat, sprawled out] Occupied. All of them. Both armrests. [possessive, smug] The middle seat. The window. [final] Mine.

lines.speaker: The Armrest Hog
lines.text: The second hand is mine too. I'm not giving up a single second.
lines.script: [petty, clutching, stubborn] The second hand is mine too. [tight, dug in] I'm not giving up a single second.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Lounge etiquette. You get one armrest. The middle seat gets both. That's the rule.
lines.script: [dry, calm, lecturing with total authority] Lounge etiquette. You get one armrest. [firm, deadpan] The middle seat gets both. That's the rule.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom has very strong opinions about armrests.
lines.script: [amused, teasing, loving] Tom has very strong opinions about armrests.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody should have very strong opinions about armrests.
lines.script: [deadpan, utterly serious] Everybody should have very strong opinions about armrests.

lines.speaker: The Armrest Hog
lines.text: ...Fine. You can sit. Here. The second hand. And you can have an armrest. One. The left one.
lines.script: [grudging, sulky, giving ground] ...Fine. You can sit. [reluctant, handing it over] Here. The second hand. [petty, bargaining] And you can have an armrest. One. [muttered] The left one.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thank you. That was very big of you.
lines.script: [dry, gracious, deadpan sincere] Thank you. [warm, mock solemn] That was very big of you.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom. The cabinet. Pajamas. With a little gold zero on the pocket.
lines.script: [quick, pointing, spotting a clue] Tom. The cabinet. Pajamas. [intrigued] With a little gold zero on the pocket.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: A long brass clock hand. Stamped on the back: GATE 0, SECOND. It goes on the gate clock.
lines.script: [reading aloud, dry, matter of fact] A long brass clock hand. Stamped on the back: GATE zero, SECOND. It goes on the gate clock.

lines.speaker: Photo booth
lines.text: Everybody squishes in. Rose on Tom’s lap. Grace in front, doing a pose. Amy at the edge, half out of frame, laughing.
lines.script: [reading aloud, fond, laughing narrator] Everybody squishes in. Rose on Tom’s lap. Grace in front, doing a pose. [warm, giggling] Amy at the edge, half out of frame, laughing.

lines.speaker: Photo booth
lines.text: Everybody squishes in. Rose on Tom’s lap. Grace in front, doing a pose. Amy at the edge, half out of frame, laughing.
lines.script: [reading aloud, fond, laughing narrator] Everybody squishes in. Rose on Tom’s lap. Grace in front, doing a pose. [warm, giggling] Amy at the edge, half out of frame, laughing.

lines.speaker: Photo booth
lines.text: FLASH. FLASH. FLASH. FLASH. Four little photos slide out, still warm.
lines.script: [reading aloud, bright, rapid camera-flash rhythm] FLASH. FLASH. FLASH. FLASH. [cozy, soft] Four little photos slide out, still warm.

lines.speaker: Photo booth
lines.text: FLASH. FLASH. FLASH. FLASH. Four little photos slide out, still warm.
lines.script: [reading aloud, bright, rapid camera-flash rhythm] FLASH. FLASH. FLASH. FLASH. [cozy, soft] Four little photos slide out, still warm.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Sending it to Justin.
lines.script: [quick, pleased, thumbs flying] Sending it to Justin.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: "Best one yet. Is that an airport? At midnight?? Proud of you guys." With the heart. He used the heart.
lines.script: [reading a text aloud, warm, then tickled] "Best one yet. Is that an airport? At midnight?? Proud of you guys." [teasing, delighted] With the heart. [mock amazed] He used the heart.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: TWO hearts this year! That's a record!
lines.script: [gasping, delighted, boasting] TWO hearts this year! [triumphant] That's a record!

lines.speaker: Gate clock
lines.text: The seventh coin clicks into its slot. All three hands shiver. The clock doesn't start. The middle slot is still empty.
lines.script: [reading aloud, suspenseful narrator] The seventh coin clicks into its slot. All three hands shiver. [letdown, ominous] The clock doesn't start. [low, uneasy] The middle slot is still empty.

lines.speaker: Gate clock
lines.text: The seventh coin clicks into its slot. All three hands shiver. The clock doesn't start. The middle slot is still empty.
lines.script: [reading aloud, suspenseful narrator] The seventh coin clicks into its slot. All three hands shiver. [letdown, ominous] The clock doesn't start. [low, uneasy] The middle slot is still empty.

lines.speaker: Gate clock
lines.text: But the doors under it go CLUNK, and swing open by themselves.
lines.script: [reading aloud, building, then heavy] But the doors under it go CLUNK, [hushed, wondrous] and swing open by themselves.

lines.speaker: Gate clock
lines.text: But the doors under it go CLUNK, and swing open by themselves.
lines.script: [reading aloud, building, then heavy] But the doors under it go CLUNK, [hushed, wondrous] and swing open by themselves.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The sundial, the steamer, the sign-up sheet, the jar, the book, the oven, the Mirrorball. I knew it. I KNEW the list was important.
lines.script: [rattling off, thrilled, bossy] The sundial, the steamer, the sign-up sheet, the jar, the book, the oven, the Mirrorball. [vindicated, beaming] I knew it. I KNEW the list was important.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Seven coins. Seven chapters of your life, Tom. Somebody has been planning this.
lines.script: [slow, thoughtful, a little awed] Seven coins. Seven chapters of your life, Tom. [wary, suspicious] Somebody has been planning this.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Somebody with a little clock. And one more coin.
lines.script: [dry, calm, resolved] Somebody with a little clock. [quiet, determined] And one more coin.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: A PLANE. A real one. Out the window. Its lights are on. Tata, its lights are ON.
lines.script: [awestruck whisper-shout, pressed to the window] A PLANE. A real one. Out the window. [thrilled] Its lights are on. [squealing] Tah Tah, its lights are ON.

lines.speaker: The Last Call
lines.text: DING. Passengers! Oh. Oh, PASSENGERS. At Gate Zero. This is the LAST CALL for Flight Zero.
lines.script: [blaring cheerful chime, then tearful, overjoyed PA voice] DING. Passengers! [choking up, ecstatic] Oh. Oh, PASSENGERS. [grand, announcing] At Gate Zero. This is the LAST CALL for Flight Zero.

lines.speaker: The Last Call
