lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dog on a leash. Girls on the buddy system. Here we go.
lines.script: [dry, steady, rallying] Dog on a leash. Girls on the buddy system. [determined, ready] Here we go.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Jefferson Park. Same jacarandas, same lemon tree, same wood door.
lines.script: [soft, wistful, taking it in] Jefferson Park. Same jacarandas, same lemon tree, same wood door.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nothing is paused here. The sprinklers are even on.
lines.script: [relieved, quiet, grateful] Nothing is paused here. [dry, small smile] The sprinklers are even on.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It smells like lemons. And a little bit like a burrito.
lines.script: [sniffing, delighted, matter of fact] It smells like lemons. [giggling] And a little bit like a burrito.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s the lemon tree and Doña Carmen’s. Welcome to 3468.
lines.script: [warm, proud, deadpan] That’s the lemon tree and Doña Carmen’s. [welcoming] Welcome to thirty-four sixty-eight.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, you live in a real grown-up house. With flax.
lines.script: [impressed, grown-up, dramatic] Tah Tah, you live in a real grown-up house. [grand, arch] With flax.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: What’s flax?
lines.script: [innocent, puzzled] What’s flax?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The red grass by the steps. It looks like it’s waving.
lines.script: [dry, patient, pointing] The red grass by the steps. [soft, fond] It looks like it’s waving.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s waving at ME.
lines.script: [thrilled, hushed, certain] It’s waving at ME.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Wood door. A welcome mat in Japanese. Not one thing out of place.
lines.script: [observing, impressed, brisk] Wood door. A welcome mat in Japanese. [amazed, teasing] Not one thing out of place.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I’ve known you thirty-some years, and I pictured a pile of laundry and a gaming chair.
lines.script: [amused, teasing, sisterly] I’ve known you thirty-some years, and I pictured a pile of laundry [dry, deadpan] and a gaming chair.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB is the reason nothing is out of place.
lines.script: [dry, affectionate, confessing] TNB is the reason nothing is out of place.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I’m the reason there are coasters.
lines.script: [easy, smug, amused] I’m the reason there are coasters.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Come in. I’ll show you where I live. Mind the dog. And the sourdough.
lines.script: [warm, welcoming, dry] Come in. I’ll show you where I live. [mock serious, warning] Mind the dog. And the sourdough.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. TATA. There’s a jar. It’s bubbling. It’s ALIVE.
lines.script: [whisper-shouting, thrilled, tugging his sleeve] Tah Tah. TAH TAH. There’s a jar. [wide-eyed] It’s bubbling. It’s ALIVE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s Bready Mercury. He’s nine years old, he’s flown Delta One, and he’s the only one in this house who gets fed on time.
lines.script: [proud, deadpan, fond] That’s Bready Mercury. [dry, deadpan] He’s nine years old, he’s flown Delta One, and he’s the only one in this house who gets fed on time.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You named your bread Mercury? Like the planet?
lines.script: [incredulous, amused, bossy] You named your bread Mercury? [teasing] Like the planet?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Like the singer. He’s a showman. He rises on command.
lines.script: [dry, tickled, deadpan] Like the singer. [proud] He’s a showman. He rises on command.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can he do a trick?
lines.script: [eager, earnest] Can he do a trick?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He rises. Every day. Without being asked. It’s the best trick anybody in this house does.
lines.script: [deadpan, then warm, sincere] He rises. Every day. Without being asked. [fond, quiet] It’s the best trick anybody in this house does.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I do a trick where I turn a lump into a bowl.
lines.script: [easy, playful, pretending to brag] I do a trick where I turn a lump into a bowl.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You do. Yours is better. Don’t tell Bready.
lines.script: [warm, teasing, conspiratorial] You do. Yours is better. [low, mock secret] Don’t tell Bready.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. There’s a picture of us. On the wall. In the nice frame.
lines.script: [soft, delighted, pointing] Tah Tah. There’s a picture of us. On the wall. [pleased, impressed] In the nice frame.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: There’s one of me with a sandwich. It’s my best side.
lines.script: [proud, serious, matter of fact] There’s one of me with a sandwich. [smug] It’s my best side.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s the wall I walk past every morning. Before work. Before coffee.
lines.script: [quiet, soft, a little shy] It’s the wall I walk past every morning. [gentle] Before work. Before coffee.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I say good morning to the two of you.
lines.script: [tender, low, bashful] I say good morning to the two of you.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Every morning?
lines.script: [soft, touched, wondering] Every morning?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Every morning. Rose usually says it back. In my head.
lines.script: [warm, wry, tender] Every morning. [dry, fond] Rose usually says it back. In my head.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I said it back just now. Good morning, Tata.
lines.script: [bright, sincere, proud to report] I said it back just now. [sweet] Good morning, Tah Tah.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Good morning, Rose.
lines.script: [soft, moved, warm] Good morning, Rose.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: So this is your house.
lines.script: [quiet, wondering, taking it in] So this is your house.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s yours too. I mean it. A snow globe called Long Island, and a house called this one. Both. Always both.
lines.script: [earnest, warm, quietly emphatic] It’s yours too. I mean it. [gentle, sincere] A snow globe called Long Island, and a house called this one. [tender, firm] Both. Always both.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom. That wall is the nicest thing I’ve seen in a house in years.
lines.script: [moved, quiet, sisterly] Tom. That wall is the nicest thing I’ve seen in a house in years.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s an Ikea frame. Don’t make it weird.
lines.script: [dry, embarrassed, deflecting] It’s an Ikea frame. [flat, pleading] Don’t make it weird.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s a very nice Ikea frame.
lines.script: [teasing, gentle, deadpan] It’s a very nice Ikea frame.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. Next stop, the loft. Everybody’s coming. I’ll show you where I break things on purpose.
lines.script: [easy, amused, ushering] Okay. Next stop, the loft. Everybody’s coming. [sly, playful] I’ll show you where I break things on purpose.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: This is it. The loft. Kiln, wheel, and a lot of clay in places clay shouldn’t be.
lines.script: [proud, relaxed, gesturing around] This is it. The loft. [wry, fond] Kiln, wheel, and a lot of clay in places clay shouldn’t be.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It’s so many mugs.
lines.script: [amazed, dramatic, wide-eyed] It’s so many mugs.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can I touch the clay?
lines.script: [eager, hopeful, hands out] Can I touch the clay?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Rose. Come here. Wet hands. Sit. Put your thumb in the middle. Don’t push. Just open it.
lines.script: [gentle, coaxing, patient teacher] Rose. Come here. Wet hands. Sit. [soft, guiding] Put your thumb in the middle. Don’t push. Just open it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s a hole.
lines.script: [flat, unimpressed, literal] It’s a hole.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s a bowl. It just doesn’t know yet.
lines.script: [warm, amused, encouraging] It’s a bowl. [soft, knowing] It just doesn’t know yet.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Mine is leaning.
lines.script: [concerned, a little defensive, pointing] Mine is leaning.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Leaning is a style. It’s called Pisa.
lines.script: [easy, playful, reassuring] Leaning is a style. [pleased with the pun] It’s called Pisa.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He taught my six-year-old to center clay in four minutes. I’ve been trying to get her to center her cereal for two years.
lines.script: [amazed, wry, sisterly exasperation] He taught my six-year-old to center clay in four minutes. [dry, rueful] I’ve been trying to get her to center her cereal for two years.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Clay doesn’t move. Cereal moves.
lines.script: [plain, serious, as if obvious] Clay doesn’t move. [matter of fact] Cereal moves.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: So. Tom. Tell me one thing he does when he thinks nobody is watching.
lines.script: [sly, playful, leaning in, sibling mischief] So. Tom. Tell me one thing he does when he thinks nobody is watching.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He checks the front door three times before bed. Tells me it’s for the dog.
lines.script: [amused, fond, easy] He checks the front door three times before bed. [dry, smiling] Tells me it’s for the dog.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He did that at nine. He told Mom it was for the cat.
lines.script: [laughing, nostalgic, wry] He did that at nine. [sly, deadpan] He told Mom it was for the cat.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You had a cat?
lines.script: [puzzled, curious, light] You had a cat?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: We never had a cat.
lines.script: [dry, flat, beat] We never had a cat.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The first night I fired the big kiln alone, it was three in the morning. I looked up and he was standing in the doorway. With a thermos and a blanket. Just in case.
lines.script: [soft, fond, remembering] The first night I fired the big kiln alone, it was three in the morning. I looked up and he was standing in the doorway. [tender, amused] With a thermos and a blanket. Just in case.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That is exactly him. He’s been standing in doorways with a thermos since he was nine.
lines.script: [laughing, warm, certain] That is exactly him. [fond, wry] He’s been standing in doorways with a thermos since he was nine.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He thinks I didn’t see him. I fired a second kiln so he’d have a reason to stay.
lines.script: [tender, quiet, sly smile] He thinks I didn’t see him. [soft, sweet] I fired a second kiln so he’d have a reason to stay.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Okay. I like you. Don’t tell him.
lines.script: [touched, gruff-soft, whispering] Okay. I like you. [conspiratorial, low] Don’t tell him.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He’s standing right behind you.
lines.script: [deadpan, smooth, barely containing a grin] He’s standing right behind you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I was looking at a mug.
lines.script: [flat, caught, dry, looking away] I was looking at a mug.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s a very nice mug.
lines.script: [teasing, gentle, deadpan] It’s a very nice mug.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Look! I made a bowl! It has a hat! The hat is a lump!
lines.script: [thrilled, bursting, holding it up] Look! I made a bowl! [giggling, proud] It has a hat! The hat is a lump!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s the best bowl in the loft. It goes in the kiln tonight. You can pick it up when we’re all home safe.
lines.script: [warm, proud, gentle] That’s the best bowl in the loft. It goes in the kiln tonight. [soft, reassuring] You can pick it up when we’re all home safe.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Love it. Love the block. Love the lemons. So many lemons. What is that, a jacaranda? Needs less.
lines.script: [glib, breezy, critiquing, bored] Love it. Love the block. Love the lemons. [dismissive, squinting] So many lemons. What is that, a jacaranda? [clipped, flat] Needs less.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Love it. Love the block. Love the lemons. So many lemons. What is that, a jacaranda? Needs less.
lines.script: [glib, breezy, critiquing, bored] Love it. Love the block. Love the lemons. [dismissive, squinting] So many lemons. What is that, a jacaranda? [clipped, flat] Needs less.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Excuse me. Who are you?
lines.script: [wary, polite, guarded] Excuse me. Who are you?

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Marlowe. Monochrome Marlowe. I fix places. This place has a lot going on. Too much color, too many porches, a dog doing something on a lawn.
lines.script: [smooth, patronizing, self-important] Marlowe. Monochrome Marlowe. I fix places. [airy, critical] This place has a lot going on. Too much color, too many porches, a dog doing something on a lawn.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Marlowe. Monochrome Marlowe. I fix places. This place has a lot going on. Too much color, too many porches, a dog doing something on a lawn.
lines.script: [smooth, patronizing, self-important] Marlowe. Monochrome Marlowe. I fix places. [airy, critical] This place has a lot going on. Too much color, too many porches, a dog doing something on a lawn.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s a neighborhood.
lines.script: [dry, unamused, flat] That’s a neighborhood.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: That’s the problem with a neighborhood. Notes.
lines.script: [breezy, dismissive, tapping his clipboard] That’s the problem with a neighborhood. [cold, crisp] Notes.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: That’s the problem with a neighborhood. Notes.
lines.script: [breezy, dismissive, tapping his clipboard] That’s the problem with a neighborhood. [cold, crisp] Notes.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: He lifts a clipboard. The top page says NOTES: LESS. He snaps his fingers.
lines.script: [reading aloud, ominous, deliberate] He lifts a clipboard. The top page says NOTES: LESS. [sharp, snap] He snaps his fingers.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: He lifts a clipboard. The top page says NOTES: LESS. He snaps his fingers.
lines.script: [reading aloud, ominous, deliberate] He lifts a clipboard. The top page says NOTES: LESS. [sharp, snap] He snaps his fingers.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He took the pink off the jacaranda!
lines.script: [gasping, outraged, pointing] He took the pink off the jacaranda!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You can’t just take the pink!
lines.script: [furious, bossy, dramatic] You can’t just take the pink!

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I can take the pink, the yellow, and the music out of that window. Mr. Vance likes it quiet. Quiet is safe. Quiet sells.
lines.script: [smooth, cold, matter of fact] I can take the pink, the yellow, and the music out of that window. [soft, salesman smooth] Mr. Vance likes it quiet. Quiet is safe. Quiet sells.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I can take the pink, the yellow, and the music out of that window. Mr. Vance likes it quiet. Quiet is safe. Quiet sells.
lines.script: [smooth, cold, matter of fact] I can take the pink, the yellow, and the music out of that window. [soft, salesman smooth] Mr. Vance likes it quiet. Quiet is safe. Quiet sells.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I have twelve kids in my room who’ve had harder mornings than you. You don’t scare me. Colors back, please.
lines.script: [teacher voice, steely, unflinching] I have twelve kids in my room who’ve had harder mornings than you. You don’t scare me. [firm, commanding] Colors back, please.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I don’t put things back. I take notes. Anyway, Mr. Prime will handle the intersection. Do take a look at the traffic. It’s very stationary.
lines.script: [airy, unbothered, dismissive] I don’t put things back. I take notes. [sly, smug] Anyway, Mr. Prime will handle the intersection. [dry, pleased] Do take a look at the traffic. It’s very stationary.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I don’t put things back. I take notes. Anyway, Mr. Prime will handle the intersection. Do take a look at the traffic. It’s very stationary.
lines.script: [airy, unbothered, dismissive] I don’t put things back. I take notes. [sly, smug] Anyway, Mr. Prime will handle the intersection. [dry, pleased] Do take a look at the traffic. It’s very stationary.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: He walks off into the grey, humming a jingle that never resolves.
lines.script: [reading aloud, dry, fading out] He walks off into the grey, [eerie, flat] humming a jingle that never resolves.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: He walks off into the grey, humming a jingle that never resolves.
lines.script: [reading aloud, dry, fading out] He walks off into the grey, [eerie, flat] humming a jingle that never resolves.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He’s turning the whole block into a backlot. And he stopped something. Look at Mr. Washington.
lines.script: [grim, alarmed, controlled] He’s turning the whole block into a backlot. [sharper, urgent] And he stopped something. Look at Mr. Washington.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s amber. It’s warmth that got stuck. Doña Carmen’s is right there, and the Alvarez house is down 2nd.
lines.script: [calm, gentle, explaining] That’s amber. It’s warmth that got stuck. [practical, steady] Doña Carmen’s is right there, and the Alvarez house is down 2nd.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We check on the neighbors first.
lines.script: [resolved, steady, protective] We check on the neighbors first.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. Doña Carmen turned into candy.
lines.script: [hushed, amazed, tugging his sleeve] Tah Tah. Doña Carmen turned into candy.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: She’s amber. Mid-sentence.
lines.script: [quiet, solemn, careful] She’s amber. [low, wry] Mid-sentence.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: She’s still pointing at the volcano.
lines.script: [whispering, amused, pointing] She’s still pointing at the volcano.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Amber is just warmth that got stuck. You don’t break it. You give it somewhere to go.
lines.script: [gentle, wise, calm] Amber is just warmth that got stuck. [soft, certain] You don’t break it. You give it somewhere to go.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Warmth. We’re good at warmth. Everybody find the warmest thing in the room.
lines.script: [coaching, upbeat, rallying] Warmth. We’re good at warmth. [brisk, clapping] Everybody find the warmest thing in the room.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The comal! The pupusas!
lines.script: [gasping, excited, pointing] The comal! The pupusas!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Tom lifts a pupusa off the comal. It’s still hot. Steam is coming off it, in a room where nothing else is moving.
lines.script: [reading aloud, soft, marveling] Tom lifts a pupusa off the comal. It’s still hot. [hushed, uncanny] Steam is coming off it, in a room where nothing else is moving.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Doña Carmen. It’s Tom. Nobody on this block has ever left your door hungry. We’re here to eat. Please wake up.
lines.script: [gentle, coaxing, warm, leaning in] Doña Carmen. It’s Tom. [tender, teasing] Nobody on this block has ever left your door hungry. We’re here to eat. [soft, pleading] Please wake up.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: A crack runs up the amber like sugar glass. Then another. Then it falls away in warm gold flakes.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, delicate] A crack runs up the amber like sugar glass. Then another. [warm, relieved] Then it falls away in warm gold flakes.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: ...and THEN I told the man, the loroco is not optional. Tom! When did you get here? Why is everything so quiet?
lines.script: [mid-rant, indignant, then startled] ...and THEN I told the man, the loroco is not optional. [bright, thrown] Tom! When did you get here? [confused, lowering her voice] Why is everything so quiet?

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: Where did my pupusas go?
lines.script: [alarmed, stricken, looking around] Where did my pupusas go?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You were amber for a little while.
lines.script: [gentle, careful, understated] You were amber for a little while.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: I was what? I had a whole sentence. I lost the sentence. It was a good sentence.
lines.script: [baffled, mournful, offended] I was what? [wistful, aggrieved] I had a whole sentence. I lost the sentence. [sorrowful] It was a good sentence.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: A man in a grey suit did it. His name is Marlowe.
lines.script: [serious, helpful, pointing] A man in a grey suit did it. [firm, accusing] His name is Marlowe.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: That man stood on my step and said my sign was “too busy.” I said the sign is busy because the food is good.
lines.script: [indignant, proud, scornful] That man stood on my step and said my sign was “too busy.” [fierce, deadpan] I said the sign is busy because the food is good.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: Go next door. The Alvarez house. They didn’t get any pupusas today. Take these. Feed the children first. The grown-ups will pretend they’re not hungry.
lines.script: [brisk, generous, bossy-warm] Go next door. The Alvarez house. They didn’t get any pupusas today. Take these. [firm, tender] Feed the children first. [knowing, wry] The grown-ups will pretend they’re not hungry.

lines.speaker: Daisy
lines.text: Tom! Tom! Everybody stopped! Abuela stopped in the middle of saying NO!
lines.script: [urgent, alarmed, breathless] Tom! Tom! Everybody stopped! [wide-eyed, awed] Abuela stopped in the middle of saying NO!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Okay. They’re amber. The grey got in through the front door.
lines.script: [calm, grim, assessing] Okay. They’re amber. [low, tense] The grey got in through the front door.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Heat is just movement. When the girls can’t sleep, we run. Nobody stays stuck when they’re moving.
lines.script: [coaching, confident, insightful] Heat is just movement. When the girls can’t sleep, we run. [firm, bright] Nobody stays stuck when they’re moving.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You mean...
lines.script: [hesitant, dawning, dread] You mean...

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody up. Girls, with me. We’re running laps around the kitchen table.
lines.script: [commanding, energized, clapping] Everybody up. Girls, with me. [bright, firm] We’re running laps around the kitchen table.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Run with us, Mommy!
lines.script: [delighted, squealing, begging] Run with us, Mommy!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lap one! Knees up, Rose!
lines.script: [coaching, pumped, loud] Lap one! [encouraging, brisk] Knees up, Rose!

lines.speaker: Don Beto
lines.text: ...and that is a FOUL! That is a foul! Who has the remote?
lines.script: [groggy, booming, mid-dream, confused] ...and that is a FOUL! [indignant, waking] That is a foul! [muddled] Who has the remote?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lap two! Grace, don’t look at the camera!
lines.script: [coaching, breathless, laughing] Lap two! [mock stern] Grace, don’t look at the camera!

lines.speaker: Tony
lines.text: Why is there a woman running around my table? Why is it a good idea? It’s a very good idea.
lines.script: [deadpan, bewildered, tired] Why is there a woman running around my table? [slow, thoughtful, dry] Why is it a good idea? [flat, surrendering] It’s a very good idea.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lap three! Everybody on the last one!
lines.script: [breathless, triumphant, rallying] Lap three! [urgent, pumped] Everybody on the last one!

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: ...NO. I said no. Why is everyone in my kitchen? Is that a mother running laps with two little girls?
lines.script: [waking mid-argument, indignant] ...NO. I said no. [bewildered, loud] Why is everyone in my kitchen? [softening, amazed] Is that a mother running laps with two little girls?

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: ...Okay. That one can stay.
lines.script: [grudging, melting, laughing] ...Okay. [warm, firm] That one can stay.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That wasn’t a lap. That was a Tombo. Run With Us, Mommy. Amy, Grace and Rose, together.
lines.script: [dry, proud, announcing, quietly moved] That wasn’t a lap. That was a Tombo. [warm, formal] Run With Us, Mommy. Amy, Grace and Rose, together.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: Take lemons. Take ALL the lemons. Every yard in this city has too many and somebody always leaves them on my step.
lines.script: [generous, brisk, laughing, pressing them on] Take lemons. Take ALL the lemons. [wry, exasperated] Every yard in this city has too many and somebody always leaves them on my step.

lines.speaker: Daisy
lines.text: Is it okay if I say that was the best thing that has ever happened in our kitchen?
lines.script: [earnest, politely asking permission, glowing] Is it okay if I say that was the best thing that has ever happened in our kitchen?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It was the best thing in OUR kitchen too. We don’t even have a kitchen table. We have a counter.
lines.script: [sweet, matter of fact, a little wistful] It was the best thing in OUR kitchen too. [literal, innocent] We don’t even have a kitchen table. We have a counter.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Look at that. You put the neighbors back. Very warm. Very busy. Very much not what I asked for.
lines.script: [smooth, cool, faintly annoyed] Look at that. You put the neighbors back. [dry, clipped] Very warm. Very busy. [cold] Very much not what I asked for.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Look at that. You put the neighbors back. Very warm. Very busy. Very much not what I asked for.
lines.script: [smooth, cool, faintly annoyed] Look at that. You put the neighbors back. [dry, clipped] Very warm. Very busy. [cold] Very much not what I asked for.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The rest of the colors too, please. All of them.
lines.script: [firm, steady, teacher patient] The rest of the colors too, please. [commanding] All of them.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Notes. This intersection has no flow. Let me introduce our new Head of Traffic.
lines.script: [crisp, bored, officious] Notes. This intersection has no flow. [slick, showman] Let me introduce our new Head of Traffic.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Notes. This intersection has no flow. Let me introduce our new Head of Traffic.
lines.script: [crisp, bored, officious] Notes. This intersection has no flow. [slick, showman] Let me introduce our new Head of Traffic.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Mr. Prime! Please give them a moment to rethink the neighborhood.
lines.script: [grandly calling, salesman bright] Mr. Prime! [breezy, smug] Please give them a moment to rethink the neighborhood.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Mr. Prime! Please give them a moment to rethink the neighborhood.
lines.script: [grandly calling, salesman bright] Mr. Prime! [breezy, smug] Please give them a moment to rethink the neighborhood.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s the biggest car in the WORLD.
lines.script: [awestruck, whispering, thrilled] It’s the biggest car in the WORLD.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Every light on the block is red. Every single one.
lines.script: [grim, tense, observing] Every light on the block is red. [low, flat] Every single one.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. Its headlights are pointed at the ground. It looks sad.
lines.script: [soft, sympathetic, worried] Tah Tah. Its headlights are pointed at the ground. [tender, sad] It looks sad.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: It’s not angry. It’s stuck. Stuck is very quiet, and Mr. Vance likes quiet. Do be quick. The notes are due at five.
lines.script: [smooth, unbothered, patronizing] It’s not angry. It’s stuck. [airy, cold] Stuck is very quiet, and Mr. Vance likes quiet. [clipped, officious] Do be quick. The notes are due at five.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: It’s not angry. It’s stuck. Stuck is very quiet, and Mr. Vance likes quiet. Do be quick. The notes are due at five.
lines.script: [smooth, unbothered, patronizing] It’s not angry. It’s stuck. [airy, cold] Stuck is very quiet, and Mr. Vance likes quiet. [clipped, officious] Do be quick. The notes are due at five.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: If it’s stuck, maybe it just needs somewhere to go. Kindness first. Hit it if it hits back.
lines.script: [easy, gentle, thoughtful] If it’s stuck, maybe it just needs somewhere to go. [calm, wry] Kindness first. Hit it if it hits back.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Here’s the plan. I stay with the girls. If anybody needs a break, sit on a couch or a bench and we’ll swap.
lines.script: [coaching, brisk, protective] Here’s the plan. I stay with the girls. [clear, practical] If anybody needs a break, sit on a couch or a bench and we’ll swap.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody gets run over. I’ll step in front of anyone who needs it.
lines.script: [calm, firm, protective] Nobody gets run over. [steady, low] I’ll step in front of anyone who needs it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody okay? Good. It floors Rush Hour every third turn, so we heal before, not after.
lines.script: [checking in, brisk] Everybody okay? Good. [coaching, clear, tactical] It floors Rush Hour every third turn, so we heal before, not after.

lines.speaker: Gridlock Prime
lines.text: ...SigAlert cleared. Merging left. I’m sorry. Everybody was in my lane.
lines.script: [exhausted, apologetic, deflating engine sigh] ...SigAlert cleared. Merging left. [small, sheepish] I’m sorry. [mournful] Everybody was in my lane.

lines.speaker: Gridlock Prime
lines.text: ...SigAlert cleared. Merging left. I’m sorry. Everybody was in my lane.
lines.script: [exhausted, apologetic, deflating engine sigh] ...SigAlert cleared. Merging left. [small, sheepish] I’m sorry. [mournful] Everybody was in my lane.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s fine. Nobody was in your lane. You were in everybody’s. Take the exit.
lines.script: [kind, wry, gentle] It’s fine. Nobody was in your lane. [warm, teasing] You were in everybody’s. Take the exit.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The green lamp just popped off the traffic light. It’s still warm, and it’s humming.
lines.script: [quiet, curious, gentle] The green lamp just popped off the traffic light. [soft, marveling] It’s still warm, and it’s humming.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The pink is back! The jacaranda has its pink back!
lines.script: [overjoyed, squealing, pointing] The pink is back! The jacaranda has its pink back!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And the music is back in the window.
lines.script: [soft, relieved, listening] And the music is back in the window.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: ...and that is why you never trust a Tuesday. Hm? Why is everybody looking at me? Did I fall asleep? Again?
lines.script: [slow, mid-story, rumbling, then confused] ...and that is why you never trust a Tuesday. [bewildered, gentle] Hm? Why is everybody looking at me? [wry, sheepish] Did I fall asleep? Again?

lines.speaker: Larry
lines.text: I’m blowing leaves. The leaf landed. It LANDED. Thirty years I’ve waited. Thank you.
lines.script: [blissful, reverent, choked up, gruff] I’m blowing leaves. The leaf landed. It LANDED. [slow, emotional, dignified] Thirty years I’ve waited. [heartfelt] Thank you.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Love it. Hate it. Love it. Notes withdrawn.
lines.script: [airy, flippant, then grudging] Love it. Hate it. Love it. [breezy, brushing it off] Notes withdrawn.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Love it. Hate it. Love it. Notes withdrawn.
lines.script: [airy, flippant, then grudging] Love it. Hate it. Love it. [breezy, brushing it off] Notes withdrawn.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I’ll be Downtown, at the Movie Palace. Come by. I’ll have notes for the rest of the family.
lines.script: [smooth, sly, parting shot] I’ll be Downtown, at the Movie Palace. Come by. [teasing, silky] I’ll have notes for the rest of the family.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I’ll be Downtown, at the Movie Palace. Come by. I’ll have notes for the rest of the family.
lines.script: [smooth, sly, parting shot] I’ll be Downtown, at the Movie Palace. Come by. [teasing, silky] I’ll have notes for the rest of the family.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Where is my mother?
lines.script: [tight, low, urgent, barely holding] Where is my mother?

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Long Island is under glass, you know. A very safe house. Your mother is in the kitchen. She’s making a crisp. She’s been making it for hours.
lines.script: [smooth, taunting, in no hurry] Long Island is under glass, you know. A very safe house. [light, cruelly casual] Your mother is in the kitchen. She’s making a crisp. [dry, sly] She’s been making it for hours.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Long Island is under glass, you know. A very safe house. Your mother is in the kitchen. She’s making a crisp. She’s been making it for hours.
lines.script: [smooth, taunting, in no hurry] Long Island is under glass, you know. A very safe house. [light, cruelly casual] Your mother is in the kitchen. She’s making a crisp. [dry, sly] She’s been making it for hours.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Tell me where.
lines.script: [cold, quiet, dangerous] Tell me where.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Notes are due at five.
lines.script: [bland, singsong, refusing] Notes are due at five.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Notes are due at five.
lines.script: [bland, singsong, refusing] Notes are due at five.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He just told us something he shouldn’t have.
lines.script: [sharp, alert, quick] He just told us something he shouldn’t have.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Long Island is under glass. So we go under the glass. Or around it.
lines.script: [calm, practical, thinking] Long Island is under glass. [easy, clever] So we go under the glass. Or around it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sal and Sol know every road between here and there. We start with the cab stand.
lines.script: [focused, steady, plotting] Sal and Sol know every road between here and there. [decisive] We start with the cab stand.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We’ll get them back. We always make our connection.
lines.script: [quiet, warm, resolute] We’ll get them back. [steady, certain] We always make our connection.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sol. Sal says there’s a way under the dome. Tell me you know where.
lines.script: [urgent, direct, hopeful] Sol. Sal says there’s a way under the dome. [low, pleading] Tell me you know where.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Tom. Sit. Not that chair. That chair is Sal’s. I keep it warm for him out of spite.
lines.script: [brisk, warm, fast-talking, bossy host] Tom. Sit. Not that chair. [petty, proud] That chair is Sal’s. I keep it warm for him out of spite.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Okay. Sal and I are cousins. You know that. What you don’t know is what we do between airport runs.
lines.script: [chatty, leaning in, conspiratorial] Okay. Sal and I are cousins. You know that. [sly, teasing] What you don’t know is what we do between airport runs.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Is it crimes?
lines.script: [wide-eyed, hopeful, thrilled] Is it crimes?

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Letters. Eleven years of letters, Snail Mail to Los Angeles, in the trunks of cabs. Nobody ever opened a bag. Nobody ever asked why two cab companies need a hundred sacks of stamps.
lines.script: [proud, dramatic, rolling] Letters. Eleven years of letters, Snail Mail to Los Angeles, in the trunks of cabs. [wry, boasting] Nobody ever opened a bag. Nobody ever asked why two cab companies need a hundred sacks of stamps.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You’ve been running a secret mail route.
lines.script: [dry, impressed, incredulous] You’ve been running a secret mail route.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: A dispatch network. We call it the Network. We never came up with a better name.
lines.script: [proud, grandly casual] A dispatch network. We call it the Network. [shrugging, amused] We never came up with a better name.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Sol. Sol, come in. It’s Sal. Cab seven says hi. She’s fine. She’s the only thing in town that’s moving.
lines.script: [radio voice, brisk, cheerful] Sol. Sol, come in. It’s Sal. [proud, warm] Cab seven says hi. She’s fine. [wry] She’s the only thing in town that’s moving.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Sal. I have Tom, his sister, two nieces, a boyfriend and a dog in my lobby. Say hi.
lines.script: [radio voice, loud, showman] Sal. I have Tom, his sister, two nieces, a boyfriend and a dog in my lobby. [cheerful, prompting] Say hi.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Tommy! It’s quiet in here. Even the clocks are quiet. Your mother’s in the kitchen. Don’t panic. She’s fine. She just won’t stop baking.
lines.script: [radio voice, crackly, warm, then lowering] Tommy! It’s quiet in here. Even the clocks are quiet. [reassuring, gentle] Your mother’s in the kitchen. Don’t panic. She’s fine. [wry, exasperated] She just won’t stop baking.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sal. Can you get me in?
lines.script: [urgent, restrained, direct] Sal. Can you get me in?

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: I’m under the dome with a shovel and a very worried shopkeeper. I can’t get out. But I can dig toward you.
lines.script: [radio voice, gruff, regretful, then determined] I’m under the dome with a shovel and a very worried shopkeeper. I can’t get out. [resolute, warm] But I can dig toward you.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: The Sub-Rail. Sal and I bored a tunnel under the Layover, from both coasts, for a hobby. It was supposed to open in 2031. It meets in the middle, right under the dome.
lines.script: [proud, hushed, revealing a secret] The Sub-Rail. Sal and I bored a tunnel under the Layover, from both coasts, for a hobby. [sly, matter of fact] It was supposed to open in twenty thirty-one. It meets in the middle, right under the dome.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You built a transcontinental subway. As a hobby.
lines.script: [dry, delighted, deadpan amazed] You built a transcontinental subway. [flat] As a hobby.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: We got a very good deal on a drill.
lines.script: [shrugging, cheerful, proud] We got a very good deal on a drill.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: The drill stopped answering when the dome came down. Something put a chip in it. Be careful of the worm.
lines.script: [serious, lowering voice, warning] The drill stopped answering when the dome came down. Something put a chip in it. [grave, urgent] Be careful of the worm.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The worm.
lines.script: [flat, deadpan, bracing] The worm.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: The drill. We call her the Dual-Coast Drill. The kids at the depot call her the Worm. She doesn’t love it.
lines.script: [quick, correcting, amused] The drill. We call her the Dual-Coast Drill. [fond, wry] The kids at the depot call her the Worm. She doesn’t love it.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: I need dispatchers. Two of them. Radio only. Somebody has to read me the tunnel.
lines.script: [brisk, businesslike, urgent] I need dispatchers. Two of them. Radio only. [serious] Somebody has to read me the tunnel.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I’m extremely good at being in charge.
lines.script: [smug, instantly volunteering, bossy] I’m extremely good at being in charge.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I’m in charge of snacks.
lines.script: [proud, serious, claiming her role] I’m in charge of snacks.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Girls. Dispatch is the most important job in the building. If Sol says stay, you stay.
lines.script: [firm, serious, teacher voice] Girls. Dispatch is the most important job in the building. [stern, loving] If Sol says stay, you stay.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Copy.
lines.script: [crisp, professional, thrilled] Copy.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Copy copy.
lines.script: [echoing, solemn, tiny salute] Copy copy.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Sol. I am leaving my children with a cab driver.
lines.script: [deadpan, strained, doubtful] Sol. I am leaving my children with a cab driver.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Thirty years. Never lost a passenger. Found two in the trunk. Both were fine.
lines.script: [proud, reassuring, deeply unreassuring] Thirty years. Never lost a passenger. [cheery, casual] Found two in the trunk. Both were fine.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Somehow that is not comforting.
lines.script: [flat, dry, unconvinced] Somehow that is not comforting.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We’ll be on the radio the whole way. Grace, you’re the voice. Rose, you’re the snacks.
lines.script: [calm, warm, reassuring the girls] We’ll be on the radio the whole way. [dry, affectionate] Grace, you’re the voice. Rose, you’re the snacks.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Snacks are critical infrastructure.
lines.script: [grave, earnest, lecturing] Snacks are critical infrastructure.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB. Nara. Amy. With me. We go down.
lines.script: [focused, steady, calling the team] TNB. Nara. Amy. With me. [resolute, low] We go down.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I have my thermos. I’m always ready for a tunnel.
lines.script: [easy, amused, patting his bag] I have my thermos. [calm, wry] I’m always ready for a tunnel.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Out the door, the Metro stairs on the boulevard. Past the turnstile, there’s a door that says EMPLOYEES ONLY. That’s you. You’re employees now.
lines.script: [brisk, instructive, grinning] Out the door, the Metro stairs on the boulevard. Past the turnstile, there’s a door that says EMPLOYEES ONLY. [proud, playful] That’s you. You’re employees now.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: EMPLOYEES ONLY. A platform under the boulevard. And a tunnel.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, amazed] EMPLOYEES ONLY. A platform under the boulevard. [low, uneasy] And a tunnel.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I have ridden every line in this city. I didn’t know this one existed. I’m a little bit offended.
lines.script: [wry, wounded pride, amused] I have ridden every line in this city. I didn’t know this one existed. [dry, deadpan] I’m a little bit offended.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. Radio check. Say “over.”
lines.script: [crisp, professional, bossy radio voice] Dispatch to Tom. Radio check. [firm, instructing] Say “over.”

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Over.
lines.script: [flat, deadpan, obedient] Over.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: At the END, Tata. You say it at the end of what you say.
lines.script: [exasperated, patient, schooling him] At the END, Tah Tah. [pointed] You say it at the end of what you say.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I said it at the end. It was the only thing I said.
lines.script: [dry, deadpan, patient] I said it at the end. [flat] It was the only thing I said.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Snack check! Check your pockets! I put a pretzel in your left one!
lines.script: [bright, urgent, official] Snack check! Check your pockets! [proud, giggly] I put a pretzel in your left one!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...There’s a pretzel in my left pocket.
lines.script: [dry, beat, quietly touched] ...There’s a pretzel in my left pocket.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Tom! Good. Okay. Before you go in, I have to tell you something, and I have to say it fast, because Penny made me promise.
lines.script: [rapid-fire, flustered, urgent] Tom! Good. Okay. Before you go in, I have to tell you something, [fast, breathless] and I have to say it fast, because Penny made me promise.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nickel. You’re shaking.
lines.script: [gentle, concerned, quiet] Nickel. You’re shaking.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: A man in a long coat bought gold coins from our shops. For years. Paid double. Never took his hat off.
lines.script: [fast, uneasy, guilty] A man in a long coat bought gold coins from our shops. For years. Paid double. [slower, uneasy] Never took his hat off.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Julian Vance.
lines.script: [low, grim, recognizing] Julian Vance.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: We didn’t know. We thought he was a collector. We took the money. And we kept the best coins in the back, in case he ever paid triple.
lines.script: [rueful, fast, ashamed] We didn’t know. We thought he was a collector. We took the money. [small, wincing] And we kept the best coins in the back, in case he ever paid triple.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Penny called on the Network from under the dome. She said, “Tell Tom we’re sorry.” And then she said, “The drawer is under the counter.”
lines.script: [quick, emotional, relaying] Penny called on the Network from under the dome. She said, “Tell Tom we’re sorry.” [softer, wobbling] And then she said, “The drawer is under the counter.”

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Eleven coins. Hers and mine. The last of the old gold. They were supposed to be a retirement.
lines.script: [quiet, heavy, laying it down] Eleven coins. Hers and mine. The last of the old gold. [wistful, wry] They were supposed to be a retirement.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Why bring them?
lines.script: [gentle, curious, probing] Why bring them?

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Sal says gold remembers being warm. If amber is warmth that got stuck, then gold can give it somewhere to go. He says. I don’t know. He’s a cab driver.
lines.script: [unsure, earnest, half hopeful] Sal says gold remembers being warm. If amber is warmth that got stuck, then gold can give it somewhere to go. [shrugging, rueful] He says. I don’t know. He’s a cab driver.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You’re giving up your retirement.
lines.script: [quiet, moved, gentle] You’re giving up your retirement.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: I’m giving up a drawer. It’s the best drawer I ever had. Go. I’ll bring them down behind you. Sol’s driving me to the second mile marker and making me run.
lines.script: [brave, light, brushing it off] I’m giving up a drawer. It’s the best drawer I ever had. [brisk, rallying] Go. I’ll bring them down behind you. [wry, quick] Sol’s driving me to the second mile marker and making me run.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You don’t have to do this.
lines.script: [soft, concerned, kind] You don’t have to do this.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Yes, I do. Somebody gave me a shop. I’d like to be somebody who gave something back.
lines.script: [steady, sincere, quiet resolve] Yes, I do. Somebody gave me a shop. [warm, heartfelt] I’d like to be somebody who gave something back.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The tracks run east. We follow the rails.
lines.script: [quiet, focused, leading the way] The tracks run east. [steady] We follow the rails.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Stay together. Nobody falls behind. I’ll be counting.
lines.script: [coaching, firm, protective] Stay together. Nobody falls behind. [brisk, determined] I’ll be counting.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. You’re at mile marker one thousand two hundred and fifty. But the tunnel is forty feet long. Is that normal?
lines.script: [radio dispatch voice, crisp, official] Dispatch to Tom. You're at mile marker one thousand two hundred and fifty. [puzzled, suspicious] But the tunnel is forty feet long. [pointed] Is that normal?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The sign says halfway. I’m choosing to believe the sign.
lines.script: [dry, deadpan, stubborn] The sign says halfway. [calm, fully committed] I'm choosing to believe the sign.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, did you see the stone in the doorway? It’s STANDING. I think it’s the bouncer.
lines.script: [whisper-shouting, awed] Tah Tah, did you see the stone in the doorway? [hushed, certain] It's STANDING. [matter-of-fact] I think it's the bouncer.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. You’re breaking up. Say... over... Tata?
lines.script: [radio voice, worried, signal breaking up] Dispatch to Tom. You're breaking up. [uneasy, pleading] Say... over... Tah Tah?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata? I can’t hear the... Tata? Tata?
lines.script: [small, scared, signal fading] Tah Tah? I can't hear the... [panicked, rising] Tah Tah? Tah Tah?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Grace? Rose? The radio’s gone. It’s not static. It’s just gone.
lines.script: [alarmed, calling into a dead radio] Grace? Rose? [quiet, unsettled] The radio's gone. [flat, worried] It's not static. It's just gone.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: THIS IS A QUIET CAR.
lines.script: [flat PA announcement, cold, echoing] THIS IS A QUIET CAR.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: THIS IS A QUIET CAR.
lines.script: [flat PA announcement, cold, echoing] THIS IS A QUIET CAR.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: Noise is a leak. Families are the loudest leak I have ever measured.
lines.script: [clinical, monotone, disapproving] Noise is a leak. [measured, faintly appalled] Families are the loudest leak I have ever measured.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Who are you?
lines.script: [sharp, teacher voice, unafraid] Who are you?

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: HUSH-9. Quiet Car, Series Nine. Property of Mr. Vance. Mr. Vance likes it quiet. Quiet is safe.
lines.script: [polite robot, soothing corporate] HUSH-9. Quiet Car, Series Nine. Property of Mr. Vance. [hushed, reverent] Mr. Vance likes it quiet. [soft, final] Quiet is safe.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: HUSH-9. Quiet Car, Series Nine. Property of Mr. Vance. Mr. Vance likes it quiet. Quiet is safe.
lines.script: [polite robot, soothing corporate] HUSH-9. Quiet Car, Series Nine. Property of Mr. Vance. [hushed, reverent] Mr. Vance likes it quiet. [soft, final] Quiet is safe.

lines.text: That’s the second time today somebody has told me quiet is safe. Marlowe said it too.
lines.script: [dry, tightening, connecting the dots] That's the second time today somebody has told me quiet is safe. [flat, pointed] Marlowe said it too.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: Marlowe takes the color. I take the sound. We are a very good team. Please lower your voices.
lines.script: [serene, proud machine] Marlowe takes the color. I take the sound. [pleased] We are a very good team. [gentle, firm] Please lower your voices.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: Marlowe takes the color. I take the sound. We are a very good team. Please lower your voices.
lines.script: [serene, proud machine] Marlowe takes the color. I take the sound. [pleased] We are a very good team. [gentle, firm] Please lower your voices.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: We’re being pretty quiet right now.
lines.script: [easy, amused, dry whisper] We're being pretty quiet right now.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: You are breathing audibly.
lines.script: [flat, accusing, clinical] You are breathing audibly.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: You are breathing audibly.

lines.script: [sweet, vacant, hosting] Hello, Amy. Rhubarb crisp, nine minutes. [offering, bright] Do you want a bite? [looping] Rhubarb crisp. Nine minutes.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: She’s looping. Look at the tray. It’s the same crisp. Every time. It’s fresh, it’s perfect, and nobody ever eats it.
lines.script: [quiet, observing, sad] She's looping. [careful, analytical] Look at the tray. It's the same crisp. Every time. [aching] It's fresh, it's perfect, and nobody ever eats it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Amber is warmth that got stuck. She’s been giving it to nobody for hours. It needs somewhere to go.
lines.script: [soft, understanding] Amber is warmth that got stuck. [gentle, sad] She's been giving it to nobody for hours. [quiet, resolved] It needs somewhere to go.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Maybe nobody ate it.
lines.script: [small, tentative, thinking aloud] Maybe nobody ate it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Rose. That is the smartest thing you have said all week.
lines.script: [impressed, sincere, grudging] Rose. [warm, proud] That is the smartest thing you have said all week.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I say smart things every day. They just come out as noise.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact, unbothered, earnest] I say smart things every day. [shrugging] They just come out as noise.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Deedee. I’m going to eat the crisp now. Okay? Okay.
lines.script: [gentle, resolved, tender] Deedee. I'm going to eat the crisp now. [soft, asking permission] Okay? [brave, sweet] Okay.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: ...It’s SO good. It’s the best one. Deedee, it’s the best one you ever made.
lines.script: [mouth full, amazed, overflowing] ...It's SO good. [emotional, sincere] It's the best one. [tender, earnest] Deedee, it's the best one you ever made.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh. Somebody ate it. Oh, Rosie.
lines.script: [dawning, soft, voice catching] Oh. Somebody ate it. [tender, wondering] Oh, Rosie.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh. I was making that for a long time, wasn’t I.
lines.script: [dazed, wistful, waking up] Oh. I was making that for a long time, [quiet, realizing] wasn't I.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom?
lines.script: [tearful, hopeful, trembling] Mom?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Amy. Tommy. My girls. How long was I gone?
lines.script: [warm, groggy, relieved] Amy. Tommy. My girls. [worried, gentle] How long was I gone?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A while.
lines.script: [soft, gentle, honest] A while.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Your father put on that armor. He said the glass would keep us all safe. He’s been standing out there for hours and he hasn’t sat down. Not once. Not for his back.
lines.script: [worried, nurse-practical, fretting] Your father put on that armor. He said the glass would keep us all safe. [concerned, scolding] He's been standing out there for hours and he hasn't sat down. [heartache] Not once. Not for his back.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: He thinks the armor takes the ache away. It doesn’t. It just stops him from feeling it. There’s a difference. I was a nurse for forty years. There is a very big difference.
lines.script: [firm, knowing, tender authority] He thinks the armor takes the ache away. It doesn't. [emphatic] It just stops him from feeling it. [steady] There's a difference. I was a nurse for forty years. [pointed] There is a very big difference.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Can you walk?
lines.script: [concerned, quick, practical] Can you walk?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: The glass has my feet. It’s up to my knees. I can’t go anywhere. But I can see him.
lines.script: [calm, brave, rueful] The glass has my feet. It's up to my knees. [resigned] I can't go anywhere. [soft, loving] But I can see him.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Don’t hit him, Tommy. He can’t be hit. He hates being hit and it makes the gold stronger. Make him laugh. He laughs when he’s scared. He did at our wedding.
lines.script: [urgent, tender, instructing] Don't hit him, Tommy. He can't be hit. [low, knowing] He hates being hit and it makes the gold stronger. [warm, fond] Make him laugh. He laughs when he's scared. [tender, smiling] He did at our wedding.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I have a whole bit.
lines.script: [proud, ready, mischievous] I have a whole bit.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I have a whole VIDEO.
lines.script: [competitive, haughty, one-upping] I have a whole VIDEO.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Dad used to run cross country. If I can get him to walk a lap, I can get him to talk.
lines.script: [thinking, coaching, strategic] Dad used to run cross country. [determined] If I can get him to walk a lap, I can get him to talk.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: When he’s ready, I’ll call out. You won’t miss it. I’ve been calling that man for fifty years.
lines.script: [steady, fond, firm] When he's ready, I'll call out. You won't miss it. [wry, loving] I've been calling that man for fifty years.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We’ll be careful.
lines.script: [quiet, a promise, soft] We'll be careful.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: You were always the careful one. Now be the kind one. Go.
lines.script: [loving, proud] You were always the careful one. [warm, urgent] Now be the kind one. [sending him off] Go.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dad. We’re not here to fight you.
lines.script: [steady, gentle, hands lowered] Dad. We're not here to fight you.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Then you’re here to leave.
lines.script: [cold, flat, sealed off] Then you're here to leave.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mom’s on the porch. She’s awake.
lines.script: [soft, hopeful, careful] Mom's on the porch. She's awake.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: She is NOT. She’s fine. She’s baking. That’s the deal. Nobody gets hurt, nobody gets old, nobody gets left.
lines.script: [denial, sharp, panicked] She is NOT. [forced, flat] She's fine. She's baking. [recited, strained] That's the deal. Nobody gets hurt, nobody gets old, nobody gets left.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Stand down, Tommy. I don’t want to hurt you.
lines.script: [heavy, pained, warning] Stand down, Tommy. [low, anguished] I don't want to hurt you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then don’t. And I won’t hurt you either.
lines.script: [calm, firm, tender] Then don't. [steady] And I won't hurt you either.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The gold hums. It likes it when somebody swings. I can’t stop it from liking it.
lines.script: [troubled, haunted, low] The gold hums. It likes it when somebody swings. [helpless, ashamed] I can't stop it from liking it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: So we just don’t swing!
lines.script: [bright, triumphant, solution found] So we just don't swing!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We’re the opposite of swinging. We’re the family that shows up.
lines.script: [proud, rallying, declaring] We're the opposite of swinging. [warm, certain] We're the family that shows up.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...Last warning.
lines.script: [heavy, resigned, sad] ...Last warning.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Noted.
lines.script: [calm, steady, accepting] Noted.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody okay? He hits like a dad who loves you and is very upset about it.
lines.script: [winded, wry, checking in] Everybody okay? [rueful, dry] He hits like a dad who loves you and is very upset about it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The gold goes soft. Then it runs, slow, down the front of him, like warm wax, and soaks into the porch. The helmet is the last to go.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, awed] The gold goes soft. [slow, wondering] Then it runs, slow, down the front of him, like warm wax, and soaks into the porch. [quiet, almost a smile] The helmet is the last to go.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The bucket rolled down the steps. Can I have it? Is it mine?
lines.script: [bright, hopeful, practical] The bucket rolled down the steps. [wheedling] Can I have it? [pleading] Is it mine?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Ow.
lines.script: [wincing, gruff, startled] Ow.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Ow. My back. My back is back.
lines.script: [groaning, pained chuckle] Ow. [wondering, rueful] My back. [dry, grumbling] My back is back.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The ache came back!
lines.script: [alarmed, dramatic] The ache came back!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: It never left. I just had a bucket on it.
lines.script: [tired, honest, dry] It never left. [wry, sheepish] I just had a bucket on it.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: A man in a long coat came to the door. Very polite. He never took his hat off. He said he could stop the aches. Stop the slowing down.
lines.script: [quiet, haunted, recounting] A man in a long coat came to the door. [slow, uneasy] Very polite. He never took his hat off. [low, tempted, ashamed] He said he could stop the aches. Stop the slowing down.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: He said the girls would be safe. In the good part, forever. All I had to do was stand here.
lines.script: [thick, raw, ashamed] He said the girls would be safe. In the good part, forever. [small, broken] All I had to do was stand here.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And you said yes.
lines.script: [quiet, gentle, no judgment] And you said yes.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I signed a thing. It said WARDEN on the top. I didn’t read the bottom.
lines.script: [sheepish, rueful, dry] I signed a thing. It said WARDEN on the top. [mumbling] I didn't read the bottom.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody reads the bottom.
lines.script: [soft, rueful, understanding] Nobody reads the bottom.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I’m seventy-some years old. Every year the girls get faster and I get slower. I’m not mad about it. I’m just... one day I won’t be able to catch you.
lines.script: [honest, vulnerable, gruff] I'm seventy-some years old. [quiet, tender] Every year the girls get faster and I get slower. [steadying himself] I'm not mad about it. [cracking, small] I'm just... one day I won't be able to catch you.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I just didn’t want to get too old to keep you all safe.
lines.script: [choked, raw, quiet] I just didn't want to get too old to keep you all safe.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: You big nut.
lines.script: [tender, tearful, fond scolding] You big nut.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: We keep each other safe. That is the whole deal. That’s the only one. You don’t get to keep us safe alone.
lines.script: [firm, loving, nurse authority] We keep each other safe. That is the whole deal. [gentle, certain] That's the only one. [fierce, tender] You don't get to keep us safe alone.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Deedee.
lines.script: [broken, gentle, grateful] Deedee.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Robert.
lines.script: [soft, tearful, tender] Robert.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is this the part where everybody cries?
lines.script: [innocent, curious, whispered] Is this the part where everybody cries?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Yes. Rose. Yes it is.
lines.script: [soft, tearful, sisterly] Yes. Rose. [gentle] Yes it is.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy. You’re allowed to be slow. We’ll wait. I’ll film it. For the memories. I’ll pause and wait for you.
lines.script: [tender, bossy-gentle, tearing up] Boppy. You're allowed to be slow. We'll wait. [warm, a sniffle] I'll film it. For the memories. [soft, sincere] I'll pause and wait for you.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I’ll walk slow. I’ll walk like a snail. A snail wearing a hat.
lines.script: [earnest, sweet, serious] I'll walk slow. I'll walk like a snail. [giggling, proud] A snail wearing a hat.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Rosie. That’s the best offer I’ve had in eleven years.
lines.script: [choked up, warm] Rosie. [gruff, tender, laughing softly] That's the best offer I've had in eleven years.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Dad. Come on. I’ll walk you in. Short laps. You can complain the whole time.
lines.script: [warm, brisk, fond coaching] Dad. Come on. I'll walk you in. [teasing, gentle] Short laps. You can complain the whole time.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: My stomach is doing something.
lines.script: [grumbling, relieved, back to himself] My stomach is doing something.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: There he is.
lines.script: [laughing through tears, delighted] There he is.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Vance said the girls would be safe in the good part, forever. We told him no once. He won’t take it well.
lines.script: [serious, dry, warning] Vance said the girls would be safe in the good part, forever. [grim] We told him no once. [low, wary] He won't take it well.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We always make our connection.
lines.script: [quiet, resolved, family motto] We always make our connection.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We always make our connection.
lines.script: [warm, certain, joining in] We always make our connection.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Take the key, Tommy. It opens the gate. It also opens the door. It doesn’t matter which. Nobody gets past us.
lines.script: [gruff, solemn, handing it over] Take the key, Tommy. [firm] It opens the gate. It also opens the door. [steady, proud] It doesn't matter which. Nobody gets past us.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody gets past us.
lines.script: [quiet, steady, echoing] Nobody gets past us.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Nobody gets past us.
lines.script: [gruff, solemn, a vow] Nobody gets past us.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Eight chairs. Deedee, there are seven of us and a dog.
lines.script: [dry, counting, mildly bewildered] Eight chairs. [wry] Deedee, there are seven of us and a dog.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Nara counts. Nara is people. Sit, sit, sit. Everybody sit.
lines.script: [brisk, warm, bossy] Nara counts. Nara is people. [shooing, cheerful] Sit, sit, sit. Everybody sit.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: This is the first time all of us have been at one table. I’m going to film it. For the memories.
lines.script: [self-important, excited, phone out] This is the first time all of us have been at one table. [dreamy, filming] I'm going to film it. For the memories.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Phone down. Eat first. Film after.
lines.script: [firm mom voice, fond] Phone down. Eat first. Film after.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Eating is also content.
lines.script: [deadpan, matter-of-fact, unbothered] Eating is also content.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: TNB, sweetheart. Look at you. You’re too thin. Is Tommy feeding you? Tommy, are you feeding him?
lines.script: [fussing, doting, scolding] TNB, sweetheart. Look at you. You're too thin. [sharp, turning to Tom] Is Tommy feeding you? Tommy, are you feeding him?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He makes the bowls I eat out of. We’re even.
lines.script: [dry, proud, smug] He makes the bowls I eat out of. [deadpan] We're even.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s a very good bowl, Deedee. I’m biased.
lines.script: [modest, smiling, easy] It's a very good bowl, Deedee. [wry, shy] I'm biased.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Polite, and he makes bowls. Tommy. Keep this one.
lines.script: [delighted, approving] Polite, and he makes bowls. [firm, matchmaking] Tommy. Keep this one.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s the plan.
lines.script: [warm, quiet, sincere under the dry] That's the plan.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Nara, honey. Come here. Crust, from the very edge of the pie. That’s the best part. Don’t tell Tommy.
lines.script: [coaxing, conspiratorial, sweet] Nara, honey. Come here. Crust, from the very edge of the pie. [whispering, naughty] That's the best part. Don't tell Tommy.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Nara doesn’t eat from strangers. She ate from you.
lines.script: [amazed, whispering, impressed] Nara doesn't eat from strangers. [awed] She ate from you.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I’m not a stranger. I’m a woman with crust.
lines.script: [mock offended, proud, dry] I'm not a stranger. [grinning] I'm a woman with crust.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Nobody touch the peppers. Those came off the plant by the window. They are not for the faint of heart.
lines.script: [gruff, warning, relishing it] Nobody touch the peppers. Those came off the plant by the window. [proud, low] They are not for the faint of heart.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: TNB. You work in a fancy restaurant. You eat anything?
lines.script: [squinting, sizing him up, sly] TNB. You work in a fancy restaurant. [challenging] You eat anything?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Mostly I serve it.
lines.script: [easy, wry, honest] Mostly I serve it.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That’s a no.
lines.script: [flat, unimpressed, gruff] That's a no.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s a “professionally, I’m very polite about it.”
lines.script: [smooth, dry, diplomatic] That's a "professionally, I'm very polite about it."

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: One pepper each. You and me. First one to reach for water loses.
lines.script: [challenging, grinning, gruff] One pepper each. You and me. [gleeful, daring] First one to reach for water loses.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I’ll time it. Nobody move. Nobody breathe. Ready? Go.
lines.script: [crisp, race starter, relishing it] I'll time it. Nobody move. Nobody breathe. [sharp] Ready? Go.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is somebody going to die?
lines.script: [wide-eyed, whispered, genuinely worried] Is somebody going to die?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Rose. Not in front of the pepper.
lines.script: [dry, calm, hushed] Rose. [deadpan, grave] Not in front of the pepper.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: It’s nothing. It’s fine. It’s... it’s fine.
lines.script: [strained, sweating, bluffing] It's nothing. It's fine. [choked, tight] It's... it's fine.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s actually quite floral. There’s a bright citrus note at the front.
lines.script: [calm, polite, serving] It's actually quite floral. [pleasant, voice thin, eyes watering] There's a bright citrus note at the front.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...Citrus.
lines.script: [wheezing, hoarse, suspicious] ...Citrus.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dad, you’re sweating.
lines.script: [dry, amused, deadpan] Dad, you're sweating.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: It’s warm in here. It’s the oven. Deedee, what is the oven doing?
lines.script: [defensive, flustered, hoarse] It's warm in here. It's the oven. [gruff, blaming] Deedee, what is the oven doing?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Nothing. It’s off. Robert.
lines.script: [flat, patient, knowing] Nothing. It's off. [warning, dry] Robert.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Forty seconds. Boppy’s hand is moving toward the water. It is hovering. It is hovering.
lines.script: [announcer, tense, timekeeping] Forty seconds. [hushed, breathless] Boppy's hand is moving toward the water. [rising, gripped] It is hovering. It is hovering.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That’s the pepper!
lines.script: [triumphant, pointing, accusing] That's the pepper!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: It was doing something BEFORE.
lines.script: [defensive, hoarse, grumbling] It was doing something BEFORE.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I’m calling it a draw. Neither of us reached. I’m going to breathe through my nose for a minute. I can’t feel my face. Nobody say anything.
lines.script: [wheezing, dazed, polite] I'm calling it a draw. Neither of us reached. [slow, breathy] I'm going to breathe through my nose for a minute. [numb, deadpan] I can't feel my face. Nobody say anything.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...You’ll do.
lines.script: [gruff, grudging respect, quiet] ...You'll do.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: That’s the nod. Tommy. Your father gave him the nod.
lines.script: [stage whisper, thrilled] That's the nod. Tommy. [delighted] Your father gave him the nod.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know what the nod is. I got it after the third visit.
lines.script: [dry, smug, slightly wounded pride] I know what the nod is. [deadpan] I got it after the third visit.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Okay. Toast. Everybody up. Glasses. Nara, paw.
lines.script: [bright, commanding, party host] Okay. Toast. Everybody up. Glasses. [playful] Nara, paw.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: To the table.
lines.script: [warm, quiet, sincere] To the table.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: To the eight chairs!
lines.script: [bright, delighted] To the eight chairs!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: To the CRUST!
lines.script: [gleeful, shouting] To the CRUST!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: To the moon and back.
lines.script: [tender, glowing, simple] To the moon and back.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The laughing stops. Nobody stops it. The sound just goes. Rose’s mouth is open and nothing is coming out.
lines.script: [reading aloud, unsettled, hushed] The laughing stops. Nobody stops it. [dread, quiet] The sound just goes. [alarmed, soft] Rose's mouth is open and nothing is coming out.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s a dining room.
lines.script: [flat, defiant, deadpan] It's a dining room.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: It is the loudest dining room I have ever measured. Forty-one decibels of laughing. Mr. Vance does not want laughing. Laughing is how people leak.
lines.script: [clinical, measuring, appalled] It is the loudest dining room I have ever measured. [monotone] Forty-one decibels of laughing. [cold, prissy] Mr. Vance does not want laughing. [ominous] Laughing is how people leak.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: It is the loudest dining room I have ever measured. Forty-one decibels of laughing. Mr. Vance does not want laughing. Laughing is how people leak.
lines.script: [clinical, measuring, appalled] It is the loudest dining room I have ever measured. [monotone] Forty-one decibels of laughing. [cold, prissy] Mr. Vance does not want laughing. [ominous] Laughing is how people leak.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s a family dinner. Everybody gets to be loud at a family dinner.
lines.script: [firm, protective, steely] It's a family dinner. [clear, teacherly] Everybody gets to be loud at a family dinner.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: That is the problem. You are happiest here. I have been upgraded. I am quiet in all directions. FINAL FORM.
lines.script: [flat, cold, booming] That is the problem. You are happiest here. [triumphant, mechanical] I have been upgraded. I am quiet in all directions. [loud, echoing, bass] FINAL FORM.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: That is the problem. You are happiest here. I have been upgraded. I am quiet in all directions. FINAL FORM.
lines.script: [flat, cold, booming] That is the problem. You are happiest here. [triumphant, mechanical] I have been upgraded. I am quiet in all directions. [loud, echoing, bass] FINAL FORM.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Nobody gets past us. Nobody comes to this table and shushes my wife’s cooking.
lines.script: [gruff, fierce, protective] Nobody gets past us. [indignant] Nobody comes to this table and shushes my wife's cooking.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Robert. Your back.
lines.script: [worried, scolding, nurse] Robert. Your back.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I’ll do it with my back.
lines.script: [stubborn, gruff, defiant] I'll do it with my back.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dad, sit. We’re rotating. Amy’s up front with us. You’re on the bench. When somebody needs a break, wave, and tag in a friend.
lines.script: [calm, commanding, coach] Dad, sit. We're rotating. [brisk, organizing] Amy's up front with us. You're on the bench. [clear] When somebody needs a break, wave, and tag in a friend.

lines.text: A bench call. We have a bench. I have been waiting my whole life to say bench call.
lines.script: [thrilled, reverent] A bench call. We have a bench. [dreamy, fervent] I have been waiting my whole life to say bench call.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can I raspberry the train?
lines.script: [eager, serious, hopeful] Can I raspberry the train?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You may raspberry the train.
lines.script: [dry, permitting, grand] You may raspberry the train.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Up, up. Eat something. Sit a minute. Then we try again.
lines.script: [bossy, loving, tucking him in] Up, up. Eat something. [soft, firm] Sit a minute. [warm] Then we try again.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The chip cracks right down the middle. HUSH-9 lowers its glove. For a moment the room is exactly as quiet as it wanted.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, tense] The chip cracks right down the middle. [slow, wary] HUSH-9 lowers its glove. [still, quiet] For a moment the room is exactly as quiet as it wanted.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Somebody’s laughing.
lines.script: [tiny, awed whisper, delighted] Somebody's laughing.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It’s the TRAIN.
