lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, craning up] The tower goes up past the top of the screen. [quiet, uneasy] The doors at the bottom are glass, and they are glowing like a lit window at dinnertime.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s so tall. Tata, it’s TALLER than the Starlite.
lines.script: [awed whisper, tugging his sleeve] It’s so tall. Tah Tah, [amazed, comparing] it’s TALLER than the Starlite.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The lobby is all glass and no people. Every clock says 4:59. The second hands are shaking in place, like they are trying very hard.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, uneasy] The lobby is all glass and no people. Every clock says four fifty-nine. [quiet, tender, oddly sad] The second hands are shaking in place, like they are trying very hard.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It’s so clean. Nobody lives here. Nobody even touched the floor.
lines.script: [hushed, unsettled, looking around] It’s so clean. [low, creeped out] Nobody lives here. Nobody even touched the floor.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: There’s a plant. It looks scared.
lines.script: [whisper, solemn, pointing] There’s a plant. [worried, serious] It looks scared.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Floor directory says the stairs are on the east side. Twenty-eight flights.
lines.script: [dry, reading a sign, deadpan] Floor directory says the stairs are on the east side. [flat, bracing] Twenty-eight flights.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Twenty-eight? That’s a leg day AND an arm day.
lines.script: [aghast, dramatic, then wry] Twenty-eight? [indignant, athletic] That’s a leg day AND an arm day.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The lifts are locked. We take the stairs to thirty. Amy, TNB and Nara meet us up there.
lines.script: [calm, resolute, leading the way] The lifts are locked. We take the stairs to thirty. [steady] Amy, TNB and Nara meet us up there.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Landing thirty. A huge glass door with a gold lock the size of a dinner plate. The counter over it says LOCKS ENGAGED 6 OF 6.
lines.script: [reading aloud, tense, taking in the door] Landing thirty. A huge glass door with a gold lock the size of a dinner plate. [ominous, deadpan] The counter over it says LOCKS ENGAGED six of six.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Six locks. Six of something. I don’t like that.
lines.script: [uneasy, suspicious, frowning] Six locks. Six of something. [low, wary] I don’t like that.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom, this is Amy. We’re in the service ducts. I can hear glass. A lot of glass. There’s a little hatch on your landing, it should open on the Archive.
lines.script: [hushed, brisk, over a crackly line] Tom, this is Amy. We’re in the service ducts. [tense, whispering] I can hear glass. A lot of glass. [focused, practical] There’s a little hatch on your landing, it should open on the Archive.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Found it. Staff only. Somebody wrote HE IS OBVIOUSLY STAFF under it.
lines.script: [dry, mildly amused, reading] Found it. Staff only. [deadpan] Somebody wrote HE IS OBVIOUSLY STAFF under it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That’s TNB’s handwriting. Go through. Girls hold the landing.
lines.script: [fond, exasperated, over the line] That’s TNB’s handwriting. [brisk, commanding] Go through. Girls hold the landing.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Holding the landing! Holding it! Holding!
lines.script: [thrilled, saluting, shouting seriously] Holding the landing! [proud, bouncing] Holding it! [determined, planted] Holding!

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Attention. A collection has been disturbed. Six exhibits are no longer on file.
lines.script: [flat PA announcer, cool and clipped] Attention. A collection has been disturbed. [slow, cold] Six exhibits are no longer on file.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Attention. A collection has been disturbed. Six exhibits are no longer on file.
lines.script: [flat PA announcer, cool and clipped] Attention. A collection has been disturbed. [slow, cold] Six exhibits are no longer on file.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: This is unfortunate. This is not a problem. The Archivist is not unkind. The Archivist is only thorough.
lines.script: [measured, bureaucratic calm] This is unfortunate. This is not a problem. [soft, prim, defensive] The Archivist is not unkind. [precise] The Archivist is only thorough.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: This is unfortunate. This is not a problem. The Archivist is not unkind. The Archivist is only thorough.
lines.script: [measured, bureaucratic calm] This is unfortunate. This is not a problem. [soft, prim, defensive] The Archivist is not unkind. [precise] The Archivist is only thorough.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Floors 2 to 30 are now unlocked for your convenience. The express lift has been withdrawn. Please use the stairs. All of them. The Archivist will be waiting at the top.
lines.script: [cheerful corporate announcement, hollow] Floors two to thirty are now unlocked for your convenience. [crisp] The express lift has been withdrawn. [pleasant, menacing] Please use the stairs. All of them. [cold, patient] The Archivist will be waiting at the top.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Floors 2 to 30 are now unlocked for your convenience. The express lift has been withdrawn. Please use the stairs. All of them. The Archivist will be waiting at the top.
lines.script: [cheerful corporate announcement, hollow] Floors two to thirty are now unlocked for your convenience. [crisp] The express lift has been withdrawn. [pleasant, menacing] Please use the stairs. All of them. [cold, patient] The Archivist will be waiting at the top.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Withdrawn. The lift has been WITHDRAWN. Tom. Did he just challenge me to a stair race?
lines.script: [incredulous, simmering, thrilled to compete] Withdrawn. The lift has been WITHDRAWN. [grinning, eager] Tom. Did he just challenge me to a stair race?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I don’t think he knows what he just did.
lines.script: [dry, resigned, amused] I don’t think he knows what he just did.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The seal door swings open on its own. The stairwell goes on. Twenty-nine more floors, straight up, in a glass tube.
lines.script: [reading aloud, wary, dry] The seal door swings open on its own. [looking up, daunted] The stairwell goes on. Twenty-nine more floors, straight up, in a glass tube.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You and me. Landing to landing. Loser buys dinner.
lines.script: [cocky, competitive, already stretching] You and me. Landing to landing. [grinning, taunting] Loser buys dinner.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Amy, we have a deadline. We have a tower. We have two grandparents made of stone.
lines.script: [dry, patient, pained] Amy, we have a deadline. [flat, listing] We have a tower. We have two grandparents made of stone.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Which is why I am going to win this.
lines.script: [smug, determined, shoelaces tight] Which is why I am going to win this.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I am calling it. On my mark. Mark!
lines.script: [officious, thrilled to be in charge] I am calling it. On my mark. [yelling] Mark!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I’m the finish line!
lines.script: [delighted, spreading her arms] I’m the finish line!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I am not running. I am carrying the thermos. Somebody has to.
lines.script: [easy, unbothered, dry] I am not running. [amused, hoisting it] I am carrying the thermos. Somebody has to.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Floor fifty-nine. We hit the vault door at exactly the same time. Amy’s forehead and mine, a quarter inch apart.
lines.script: [reading aloud, winded, dry] Floor fifty-nine. We hit the vault door at exactly the same time. [deadpan, wry] Amy’s forehead and mine, a quarter inch apart.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That was MINE.
lines.script: [panting, outraged, certain] That was MINE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It was a tie.
lines.script: [winded, deadpan, calm] It was a tie.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tie means nobody won. Tie means I lost. Rematch. Later. After.
lines.script: [panting, seething, tight] Tie means nobody won. [bitter, resolute] Tie means I lost. [pointing, vowing] Rematch. Later. After.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: After.
lines.script: [tired, dry, humoring her] After.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The Vault. One plinth, one snow globe, and a view of Los Angeles at 4:59 PM, golden and perfect and completely still.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, awestruck] The Vault. One plinth, one snow globe, and a view of Los Angeles at four fifty-nine PM, [slow, eerie] golden and perfect and completely still.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. It’s the Square. It’s in there. That’s Deedee. That’s BOPPY.
lines.script: [gasping whisper, pointing, distraught] Tah Tah. It’s the Square. It’s in there. [breaking] That’s Deedee. [crying out] That’s BOPPY.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: They’re so small. They’re okay. They’re holding hands.
lines.script: [hushed, tender, holding it together] They’re so small. [soft, reassuring herself] They’re okay. [gently] They’re holding hands.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Stay behind me. All of you.
lines.script: [low, tense, arm out] Stay behind me. [firm, protective] All of you.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Thank you for the six exhibits. The collection is, for the first time, incomplete. I find that I do not like it.
lines.script: [flat, polite, thin edge of unease] Thank you for the six exhibits. [cold, troubled] The collection is, for the first time, incomplete. [quiet, puzzled] I find that I do not like it.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Thank you for the six exhibits. The collection is, for the first time, incomplete. I find that I do not like it.
lines.script: [flat, polite, thin edge of unease] Thank you for the six exhibits. [cold, troubled] The collection is, for the first time, incomplete. [quiet, puzzled] I find that I do not like it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You’re the Archivist.
lines.script: [quiet, steady, working it out] You’re the Archivist.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: I am what Mr. Vance keeps when he wants a thing never to change. I file. I label. I hold. It is all I was made to do. It is a very good job.
lines.script: [precise, proud, slowly rising] I am what Mr. Vance keeps when he wants a thing never to change. [measured] I file. I label. I hold. [soft, almost wistful] It is all I was made to do. [prim, sincere] It is a very good job.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: I am what Mr. Vance keeps when he wants a thing never to change. I file. I label. I hold. It is all I was made to do. It is a very good job.
lines.script: [precise, proud, slowly rising] I am what Mr. Vance keeps when he wants a thing never to change. [measured] I file. I label. I hold. [soft, almost wistful] It is all I was made to do. [prim, sincere] It is a very good job.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You froze the pierogi man for thirty years.
lines.script: [cold, disgusted, accusing] You froze the pierogi man for thirty years.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Thirty-one. He was very happy. I made sure of it.
lines.script: [correcting, prim, sincerely proud] Thirty-one. [gentle, pleased] He was very happy. [soft, insistent] I made sure of it.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Thirty-one. He was very happy. I made sure of it.
lines.script: [correcting, prim, sincerely proud] Thirty-one. [gentle, pleased] He was very happy. [soft, insistent] I made sure of it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That is the single saddest thing I have ever heard a lens say.
lines.script: [dry, aghast, quietly appalled] That is the single saddest thing I have ever heard a lens say.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Please hold still. This will not hurt. Nothing will, ever again.
lines.script: [soft, soothing, creepy-kind] Please hold still. [gentle, hollow] This will not hurt. [slow, chilling] Nothing will, ever again.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Please hold still. This will not hurt. Nothing will, ever again.
lines.script: [soft, soothing, creepy-kind] Please hold still. [gentle, hollow] This will not hurt. [slow, chilling] Nothing will, ever again.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up. Everyone up. We have a lens to break. Breathe. Then we go again.
lines.script: [panting, fierce, rallying] Up. Everyone up. [grim, determined] We have a lens to break. [steadying] Breathe. [driving] Then we go again.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The amber lens cracks across the middle. The cold one goes dark. For one second, the whole building holds its breath.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, breathless] The amber lens cracks across the middle. The cold one goes dark. [slow, awed] For one second, the whole building holds its breath.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: I was only... keeping them safe.
lines.script: [faint, bewildered, small] I was only... keeping them safe.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: I was only... keeping them safe.
lines.script: [faint, bewildered, small] I was only... keeping them safe.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know. They were never yours to keep.
lines.script: [gentle, quiet, kind] I know. [firm, soft] They were never yours to keep.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: What does one do... with a day that is allowed to end?
lines.script: [lost, trembling, genuinely asking] What does one do... [wondering, small] with a day that is allowed to end?

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: What does one do... with a day that is allowed to end?
lines.script: [lost, trembling, genuinely asking] What does one do... [wondering, small] with a day that is allowed to end?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: You eat dinner. Then you go to sleep. Then it’s morning.
lines.script: [simple, kind, matter-of-fact] You eat dinner. Then you go to sleep. [bright, gentle] Then it’s morning.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: That sounds... sufficient.
lines.script: [hushed, wondering, a first smile] That sounds... [soft, grateful] sufficient.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: That sounds... sufficient.
lines.script: [hushed, wondering, a first smile] That sounds... [soft, grateful] sufficient.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. The globe.
lines.script: [urgent, quiet, pointing up] Tah Tah. [hushed] The globe.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The snow globe on the plinth lifts an inch off the glass. The gold cable above it goes tight. It is going up.
lines.script: [reading aloud, tense, watching] The snow globe on the plinth lifts an inch off the glass. [low] The gold cable above it goes tight. [grim] It is going up.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Thank you for the tour, Tom. Thank you for the Archive. It was very nearly complete.
lines.script: [smooth, courteous, faintly amused] Thank you for the tour, Tom. Thank you for the Archive. [mild, unbothered] It was very nearly complete.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Thank you for the tour, Tom. Thank you for the Archive. It was very nearly complete.
lines.script: [smooth, courteous, faintly amused] Thank you for the tour, Tom. Thank you for the Archive. [mild, unbothered] It was very nearly complete.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Floor sixty is for family. Come up when you are ready. I have kept your parents very warm.
lines.script: [warm, inviting, quietly menacing] Floor sixty is for family. Come up when you are ready. [soft, silken] I have kept your parents very warm.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Floor sixty is for family. Come up when you are ready. I have kept your parents very warm.
lines.script: [warm, inviting, quietly menacing] Floor sixty is for family. Come up when you are ready. [soft, silken] I have kept your parents very warm.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom. Dad. We are coming. We’re coming.
lines.script: [fierce, tearful, calling up] Mom. Dad. [vowing, steady] We are coming. We’re coming.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody breathe. We rest. Then we go to the top.
lines.script: [calm, tired, steering the group] Everybody breathe. [steady] We rest. [resolute] Then we go to the top.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A gold lift door stands open at the north wall. No call button. A brass plate: FLOOR 60. BY INVITATION.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, solemn] A gold lift door stands open at the north wall. No call button. [reading a plate, formal] A brass plate: FLOOR sixty. BY INVITATION.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The pinnacle lift opens without a sound. There is no button inside, no floor number. The walls are mirrors, and every one of us is in them.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, uncanny] The pinnacle lift opens without a sound. There is no button inside, no floor number. [slow, eerie] The walls are mirrors, and every one of us is in them.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody in. Nobody lags behind. Nobody gets left on this floor.
lines.script: [firm, gathering them, protective] Everybody in. [tight, counting heads] Nobody lags behind. [fierce] Nobody gets left on this floor.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. I’m scared. I’m also coming. Both of those are true at the same time.
lines.script: [small, honest, shaky but resolute] Tah Tah. I’m scared. [lifting her chin] I’m also coming. [steady, matter-of-fact] Both of those are true at the same time.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That is exactly the right amount of both.
lines.script: [quiet, warm, proud] That is exactly the right amount of both.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I brought a pretzel for Deedee. It’s a little bit squished.
lines.script: [small, earnest, holding it up] I brought a pretzel for Deedee. [apologetic, tender] It’s a little bit squished.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Squished is fine. I fix squished things for a living.
lines.script: [easy, warm, steady] Squished is fine. [gentle, wry] I fix squished things for a living.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The lift opens on a round room made of clock. Gold thread runs floor to ceiling, thousands of strands, humming. In the middle stands a loom the size of a house. In front of it, a man in a long coat has his back to us. His hat is on.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, awestruck] The lift opens on a round room made of clock. Gold thread runs floor to ceiling, thousands of strands, humming. [slow, dread] In the middle stands a loom the size of a house. [low, wary] In front of it, a man in a long coat has his back to us. His hat is on.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Tom. Thank you for coming. Everyone, please, come in. Mind the threads. They are all somebody’s afternoon.
lines.script: [warm, gracious host, serene] Tom. Thank you for coming. Everyone, please, come in. [gentle, quietly ominous] Mind the threads. They are all somebody’s afternoon.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Tom. Thank you for coming. Everyone, please, come in. Mind the threads. They are all somebody’s afternoon.
lines.script: [warm, gracious host, serene] Tom. Thank you for coming. Everyone, please, come in. [gentle, quietly ominous] Mind the threads. They are all somebody’s afternoon.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Where are my parents.
lines.script: [flat, cold, dangerous calm] Where are my parents.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Warm. Downstairs, on a plinth, under glass. Exactly as you left them. I want you to understand I have taken very good care of them.
lines.script: [gentle, reassuring, earnestly proud] Warm. Downstairs, on a plinth, under glass. Exactly as you left them. [sincere, soft] I want you to understand I have taken very good care of them.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Warm. Downstairs, on a plinth, under glass. Exactly as you left them. I want you to understand I have taken very good care of them.
lines.script: [gentle, reassuring, earnestly proud] Warm. Downstairs, on a plinth, under glass. Exactly as you left them. [sincere, soft] I want you to understand I have taken very good care of them.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: They’re STONE.
lines.script: [shocked, outraged, tearful] They’re STONE.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: They are safe. There is a difference. I had to have it explained to me, too.
lines.script: [mild, patient, sincere] They are safe. [quiet, rueful] There is a difference. I had to have it explained to me, too.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: They are safe. There is a difference. I had to have it explained to me, too.
lines.script: [mild, patient, sincere] They are safe. [quiet, rueful] There is a difference. I had to have it explained to me, too.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Are you the man who took all the coins?
lines.script: [small, direct, brave] Are you the man who took all the coins?

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I am the man who kept them. Gold remembers being warm. I only wanted it to keep remembering.
lines.script: [soft, wistful, earnest] I am the man who kept them. [tender, faraway] Gold remembers being warm. [gentle] I only wanted it to keep remembering.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I am the man who kept them. Gold remembers being warm. I only wanted it to keep remembering.
lines.script: [soft, wistful, earnest] I am the man who kept them. [tender, faraway] Gold remembers being warm. [gentle] I only wanted it to keep remembering.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. I fix things for a living. Whatever this is, it is structurally unsound.
lines.script: [wary, dry, professional disbelief] Okay. I fix things for a living. [flat, unimpressed] Whatever this is, it is structurally unsound.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Nothing is the same twice, Mr. TNB. You mend a cup, and it is a mended cup. I would like every cup to stay unbroken.
lines.script: [patient, gentle, weary conviction] Nothing is the same twice, Mr. TNB. [soft, wistful] You mend a cup, and it is a mended cup. [longing] I would like every cup to stay unbroken.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Nothing is the same twice, Mr. TNB. You mend a cup, and it is a mended cup. I would like every cup to stay unbroken.
lines.script: [patient, gentle, weary conviction] Nothing is the same twice, Mr. TNB. [soft, wistful] You mend a cup, and it is a mended cup. [longing] I would like every cup to stay unbroken.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That is not how cups work.
lines.script: [flat, deadpan, quietly firm] That is not how cups work.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Tom. You know why I wanted you. Two places that kept moving, and one man flying between them. You are not a traveler. You are the thread. If you stop, they stop. If you stay, they stay.
lines.script: [low, intimate, persuasive] Tom. You know why I wanted you. [slow, reverent] Two places that kept moving, and one man flying between them. [tender, cold] You are not a traveler. You are the thread. [soft, final] If you stop, they stop. If you stay, they stay.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Tom. You know why I wanted you. Two places that kept moving, and one man flying between them. You are not a traveler. You are the thread. If you stop, they stop. If you stay, they stay.
lines.script: [low, intimate, persuasive] Tom. You know why I wanted you. [slow, reverent] Two places that kept moving, and one man flying between them. [tender, cold] You are not a traveler. You are the thread. [soft, final] If you stop, they stop. If you stay, they stay.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I will not hurt you. I will not hurt anyone. I will only finish the afternoon.
lines.script: [gentle, soothing, sincere] I will not hurt you. I will not hurt anyone. [soft, quiet] I will only finish the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I will not hurt you. I will not hurt anyone. I will only finish the afternoon.
lines.script: [gentle, soothing, sincere] I will not hurt you. I will not hurt anyone. [soft, quiet] I will only finish the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I know. That is why this is so hard.
lines.script: [quiet, weary, almost sorry] I know. [heavy, honest] That is why this is so hard.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I know. That is why this is so hard.
lines.script: [quiet, weary, almost sorry] I know. [heavy, honest] That is why this is so hard.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The threads of the Loom lean. All of them, all at once, like a field in the wind. They gather into the brass lens at the end of his arm.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, mounting awe and dread] The threads of the Loom lean. All of them, all at once, like a field in the wind. [tense] They gather into the brass lens at the end of his arm.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: The Ray unwrites whatever it touches. It is very gentle. They will not remember being sad. Mrs. Gregori. Mr. TNB. Grace. Rose. Hold hands, please.
lines.script: [gentle, formal, terrible calm] The Ray unwrites whatever it touches. It is very gentle. [soothing] They will not remember being sad. [courteous, calling them] Mrs. Gregori. Mr. TNB. Grace. Rose. [kind, firm] Hold hands, please.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: The Ray unwrites whatever it touches. It is very gentle. They will not remember being sad. Mrs. Gregori. Mr. TNB. Grace. Rose. Hold hands, please.
lines.script: [gentle, formal, terrible calm] The Ray unwrites whatever it touches. It is very gentle. [soothing] They will not remember being sad. [courteous, calling them] Mrs. Gregori. Mr. TNB. Grace. Rose. [kind, firm] Hold hands, please.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Over my dead body.
lines.script: [low, ferocious, standing her ground] Over my dead body.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: That will not be necessary. That is not even on the table.
lines.script: [mild, mildly offended, placating] That will not be necessary. [prim] That is not even on the table.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: That will not be necessary. That is not even on the table.
lines.script: [mild, mildly offended, placating] That will not be necessary. [prim] That is not even on the table.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata.
lines.script: [small, frightened, reaching for him] Tah Tah.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Girls. Amy. TNB. Nara. Behind me.
lines.script: [low, quiet, utterly calm, arm out] Girls. Amy. TNB. Nara. [steady, protective] Behind me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He adjusts his glasses. He has done it before every hard thing, his whole life. Then he raises one hand, palm out, and takes one step forward.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, tender and grave] He adjusts his glasses. He has done it before every hard thing, his whole life. [slow, resolute] Then he raises one hand, palm out, and takes one step forward.

lines.text: Where Tom was standing, there is a small warm light, hanging in the air at about the height of his glasses. Then there is not.

lines.text: Thank you. All of you. I will put the rock on the mantel.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: I heard there was a situation. I brought lemon bars. And peppers. My nephew grows them. They are very hot. A man called Boppy would know what to do.
lines.script: [warm, bustling, matter-of-fact] I heard there was a situation. I brought lemon bars. [proud, firm] And peppers. My nephew grows them. They are very hot. [knowing, decisive] A man called Boppy would know what to do.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy would eat one raw and say it was “fine” in a voice.
lines.script: [wry, knowing, mimicking] Boppy would eat one raw and say it was “fine” [pinched, strained] in a voice.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The kitchen is a mess. Every pot is in use. The window is fogged. It smells like a Sunday.
lines.script: [reading aloud, warm, fond] The kitchen is a mess. Every pot is in use. The window is fogged. [soft, content] It smells like a Sunday.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The oven door handle came off. I fixed it. You could say I handled it.
lines.script: [easy, pleased with himself, smirking] The oven door handle came off. I fixed it. [smooth, pun delivered] You could say I handled it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Please stop.
lines.script: [flat, pained, deadpan] Please stop.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lasagna, eleven minutes. Lemon bars, six. I have a timer on everything. Nobody is allowed to be late for this.
lines.script: [brisk, intense, running the kitchen] Lasagna, eleven minutes. Lemon bars, six. [firm, competitive] I have a timer on everything. [warning] Nobody is allowed to be late for this.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I choreographed the pasta. It goes from the pot to the plate in a very specific arc.
lines.script: [proud, dramatic, serious artist] I choreographed the pasta. [explaining, grand] It goes from the pot to the plate in a very specific arc.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I am the taster. I have tasted nine times. It’s for quality.
lines.script: [solemn, earnest, important] I am the taster. I have tasted nine times. [dignified] It’s for quality.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The pasta does not go in an arc.
lines.script: [dry, flat, deadpan] The pasta does not go in an arc.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It goes in an arc if you believe in it, Tata.
lines.script: [sweetly smug, sing-song, unshakeable] It goes in an arc if you believe in it, Tah Tah.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He looks at the table. Everyone he loves is crowded around it, and somebody has put a rock in the middle like a centerpiece. He doesn’t say anything for a second.
lines.script: [reading aloud, soft, moved] He looks at the table. Everyone he loves is crowded around it, [warm, amused] and somebody has put a rock in the middle like a centerpiece. [quiet, full-hearted] He doesn’t say anything for a second.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Pack it up. Sal is waiting outside with cab seven. We are going to the Glass Tower, and we are bringing dinner.
lines.script: [warm, resolute, rallying] Pack it up. Sal is waiting outside with cab seven. [firm, dry] We are going to the Glass Tower, [quiet, determined] and we are bringing dinner.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Cab seven! Everybody in. Bring the lasagna on your lap, it holds the heat. Fifty-nine floors, no stops, I am not even charging. I am scared of that tower and I am going anyway.
lines.script: [booming, warm, rallying the crowd] Cab seven! Everybody in. [fast, practical] Bring the lasagna on your lap, it holds the heat. [proud, generous] Fifty-nine floors, no stops, I am not even charging. [honest, shaky, resolved] I am scared of that tower and I am going anyway.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The snow globe is still on its plinth. Inside it, very small, two stone figures hold each other up. The amber light is crawling on their hands. It is slower than before.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, tender, uneasy] The snow globe is still on its plinth. Inside it, very small, two stone figures hold each other up. [soft, worried] The amber light is crawling on their hands. [quiet, ominous] It is slower than before.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom. Dad. We brought dinner.
lines.script: [soft, tender, voice thick] Mom. Dad. [warm, aching, hopeful] We brought dinner.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I brought a pretzel. It has been DELIVERED. It has a stamp.
lines.script: [proud, earnest, sniffly] I brought a pretzel. [beaming, serious] It has been DELIVERED. [proud, matter-of-fact] It has a stamp.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Everybody sit. Around the plinth. Nobody leave. Plates on laps.
lines.script: [warm, easy, gently organizing] Everybody sit. Around the plinth. [soft, firm] Nobody leave. [gentle] Plates on laps.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Steam from the lasagna drifts across the glass. The amber light turns the color of toast. A crack of warm yellow runs along the stone, then two, then nine.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, rising wonder] Steam from the lasagna drifts across the glass. The amber light turns the color of toast. [awed, soft] A crack of warm yellow runs along the stone, then two, then nine.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It’s working. It’s working!
lines.script: [breathless, thrilled, whisper then shout] It’s working. [overjoyed] It’s working!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Oh. Oh, my back. My back is going to be talking about this for a week.
lines.script: [groggy, creaky, wincing, grumbling] Oh. Oh, my back. [dry, rueful, gruff] My back is going to be talking about this for a week.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Is that lasagna? Who made lasagna? Who has been in my kitchen?
lines.script: [waking up, bewildered, instantly bossy] Is that lasagna? Who made lasagna? [indignant, fussy] Who has been in my kitchen?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: DEEDEE! BOPPY!
lines.script: [screaming, sobbing with joy] DEEDEE! BOPPY!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh, my babies. Come here. All of you. Come here, to the moon and back and back and back.
lines.script: [overflowing, tearful, tender, arms wide] Oh, my babies. Come here. All of you. [warm, choked, loving] Come here, to the moon and back and back and back.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Which one of you is eating the peppers raw?
lines.script: [gruff, suspicious, sniffing] Which one of you is eating the peppers raw?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Nobody. Yet.
lines.script: [innocent, sly, unconvincing] Nobody. [coy, cheeky] Yet.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Hand me one. For my knees.
lines.script: [gruff, hopeful, hand out] Hand me one. [dry, wincing, deadpan] For my knees.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everyone is crowded onto one floor of a glass tower with plates in their laps, and for a minute, it is just a family having dinner, eight people and a dog.
lines.script: [reading aloud, warm, soft, content] Everyone is crowded onto one floor of a glass tower with plates in their laps, [gentle, full-hearted] and for a minute, it is just a family having dinner, [quiet, smiling] eight people and a dog.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom. Who is the man in the gold coat? The one who kept us on a shelf?
lines.script: [sharp, curious, protective, sweetly scolding] Tom. Who is the man in the gold coat? [indignant, cold] The one who kept us on a shelf?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Vance. He is still up there, at the top. He is going to want more than a shelf.
lines.script: [quiet, grim, calm] Vance. He is still up there, at the top. [low, level] He is going to want more than a shelf.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Then we finish eating first.
lines.script: [dry, gruff, unbothered, chewing] Then we finish eating first.

lines.speaker: Floor 59
lines.text: Overhead, through the glass ceiling, every clock in the sky stops. They are all pointing at the same minute: the one just after the last. A door nobody has noticed before, high up in the tower, has begun to open.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, eerie, building] Overhead, through the glass ceiling, every clock in the sky stops. [slow, uncanny] They are all pointing at the same minute: the one just after the last. [tense, awed] A door nobody has noticed before, high up in the tower, has begun to open.

lines.text: Overhead, through the glass ceiling, every clock in the sky stops. They are all pointing at the same minute: the one just after the last. A door nobody has noticed before, high up in the tower, has begun to open.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He sets down his plate. Then he picks it back up.
lines.script: [reading aloud, quiet, wry, resolute] He sets down his plate. [dry, steady] Then he picks it back up.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Seconds first. Then the sky.
lines.script: [low, steady, dry resolve] Seconds first. [calm, determined] Then the sky.

lines.text: Eight lamps light round the frame of the lift in the middle of the Core, one for each of you. The brass doors slide apart, and a warm gold light comes out of the shaft.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed awe] Eight lamps light round the frame of the lift in the middle of the Core, one for each of you. [warm, glowing] The brass doors slide apart, and a warm gold light comes out of the shaft.

lines.text: Eight lamps light round the frame of the lift in the middle of the Core, one for each of you. The brass doors slide apart, and a warm gold light comes out of the shaft.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed awe] Eight lamps light round the frame of the lift in the middle of the Core, one for each of you. [warm, glowing] The brass doors slide apart, and a warm gold light comes out of the shaft.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He built a lock that opens for family. All eight of us, and a thermos. I resent how much I admire that.
lines.script: [dry, grudgingly impressed] He built a lock that opens for family. All eight of us, and a thermos. [wry, sighing] I resent how much I admire that.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The Extra Place. Mom set a place for everybody at every dinner for fifty years. That is the whole trick. He should have asked her.
lines.script: [matter of fact, teacher voice] The Extra Place. [warm, certain] Mom set a place for everybody at every dinner for fifty years. [crisp, a little smug] That is the whole trick. [dry] He should have asked her.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Is it ready? Because I made a lot.
lines.script: [bustling, hopeful] Is it ready? [fussing, proud] Because I made a lot.

lines.speaker: Stillness Core
lines.text: THE EXTRA PLACE (the all-eight Family Finish) is ready. It costs 75% HEART.
lines.script: [reading aloud, bright system announcement] THE EXTRA PLACE (the all-eight Family Finish) is ready. [flat, ominous cost] It costs 75% HEART.

lines.speaker: Stillness Core
lines.text: THE EXTRA PLACE (the all-eight Family Finish) is ready. It costs 75% HEART.
lines.script: [reading aloud, bright system announcement] THE EXTRA PLACE (the all-eight Family Finish) is ready. [flat, ominous cost] It costs 75% HEART.

lines.text: In the ceiling of the Vault, a round brass door has opened. It has a clock for a keyhole. It is ticking very slowly, like a heart that has been told to be quiet.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, wondering] In the ceiling of the Vault, a round brass door has opened. It has a clock for a keyhole. [slow, tender] It is ticking very slowly, like a heart that has been told to be quiet.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That is the biggest clock I have ever seen. And I have a lot of clocks. They all run fast, for my stomach.
lines.script: [gruff, impressed] That is the biggest clock I have ever seen. [dry, grumbling] And I have a lot of clocks. [deadpan] They all run fast, for my stomach.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Is that the man’s house? Somebody should tell him to leave a light on.
lines.script: [concerned, motherly] Is that the man’s house? [fussing, kind] Somebody should tell him to leave a light on.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody stays together. All eight. Nobody goes through a door alone.
lines.script: [firm, protective, coaching] Everybody stays together. All eight. [low, serious] Nobody goes through a door alone.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Nara goes first. She is the best at doors.
lines.script: [serious, proud, whisper-shouting] Nara goes first. [earnest, matter of fact] She is the best at doors.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Eight of us, a dog and a thermos. Seconds first, then the sky. Let us go.
lines.script: [calm, rallying, dry] Eight of us, a dog and a thermos. [steady, resolved] Seconds first, then the sky. Let us go.

lines.speaker: Stillness Core
lines.text: The lift opens into a round chamber of brass and glass, behind the face of the sky clock. Every wall is a gear, and every gear is turning very slowly. Eight round doors stand sealed around a lift in the middle. Each keyhole is shaped like somebody.
lines.script: [reading aloud, awed, echoing] The lift opens into a round chamber of brass and glass, behind the face of the sky clock. Every wall is a gear, and every gear is turning very slowly. [hushed, mysterious] Eight round doors stand sealed around a lift in the middle. [soft, wondering] Each keyhole is shaped like somebody.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I get a door too?
lines.script: [small, hopeful, wide-eyed] I get a door too?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You get a door too.
lines.script: [warm, gentle, certain] You get a door too.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It is a very good lock. Whoever made it really cared about the mechanism.
lines.script: [easy, admiring, quietly pleased] It is a very good lock. [amused, craftsman's appreciation] Whoever made it really cared about the mechanism.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: One skill each. Whatever you are best at, that is your door.
lines.script: [thinking aloud, calm, working it out] One skill each. [warm, encouraging] Whatever you are best at, that is your door.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: A column of gears the height of a tower. Around it, a brass serpent as long as a street is slowly uncoiling. Every scale is a clock face. Every clock says 4:59. At the top of the Engine, on a platform of glass, a man in a long coat stands with his back to you.
lines.script: [reading aloud, ominous, vast] A column of gears the height of a tower. Around it, a brass serpent as long as a street is slowly uncoiling. [eerie] Every scale is a clock face. Every clock says four fifty-nine. [hushed, tense] At the top of the Engine, on a platform of glass, a man in a long coat stands with his back to you.

lines.text: Tom. You came back. You always come back. That is the thing I could never forgive you for.
lines.script: [weary, bitter, almost tender] Tom. You came back. [low, aching] You always come back. [raw] That is the thing I could never forgive you for.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Tom. You came back. You always come back. That is the thing I could never forgive you for.
lines.script: [weary, bitter, almost tender] Tom. You came back. [low, aching] You always come back. [raw] That is the thing I could never forgive you for.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I was written out of the schedule. I am a very stubborn calendar entry.
lines.script: [dry, unbowed, quiet defiance] I was written out of the schedule. [deadpan] I am a very stubborn calendar entry.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Everything leaves. Time takes a little every day, and then one day all of it. So I built a place where it cannot. The Leviathan keeps every afternoon exactly as it was. Please do not hurt it. It is all I have.
lines.script: [haunted, hollow] Everything leaves. Time takes a little every day, and then one day all of it. [quiet, desperate logic] So I built a place where it cannot. The Leviathan keeps every afternoon exactly as it was. [pleading, cracking] Please do not hurt it. [small] It is all I have.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Everything leaves. Time takes a little every day, and then one day all of it. So I built a place where it cannot. The Leviathan keeps every afternoon exactly as it was. Please do not hurt it. It is all I have.
lines.script: [haunted, hollow] Everything leaves. Time takes a little every day, and then one day all of it. [quiet, desperate logic] So I built a place where it cannot. The Leviathan keeps every afternoon exactly as it was. [pleading, cracking] Please do not hurt it. [small] It is all I have.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You turned my grandparents into STATUES.
lines.script: [outraged, shaking, fierce] You turned my grandparents into STATUES.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I kept them safe.
lines.script: [defensive, hollow, small] I kept them safe.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I kept them safe.
lines.script: [defensive, hollow, small] I kept them safe.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I was a statue for a week and my back did not get a single day off. I would like to file a complaint.
lines.script: [gruff, deadpan, aggrieved] I was a statue for a week and my back did not get a single day off. [dry, formal] I would like to file a complaint.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Julian, honey. Have you eaten?
lines.script: [gentle, motherly, concerned] Julian, honey. [fussing, kind] Have you eaten?

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: There are four things that will keep you out. Distance. Age. Exhaustion. Fear. Four things I could never get past. You will not, either.
lines.script: [cold, certain, sorrowful] There are four things that will keep you out. [measured, tolling] Distance. Age. Exhaustion. Fear. [heavy] Four things I could never get past. [quiet, final] You will not, either.

lines.text: There are four things that will keep you out. Distance. Age. Exhaustion. Fear. Four things I could never get past. You will not, either.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Distance, age, exhaustion, fear. That is just a regular Tuesday.
lines.script: [wry, tough, unimpressed] Distance, age, exhaustion, fear. [dry, brisk] That is just a regular Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Okay. Four barriers. We have a plan for every one of them. Everybody ready?
lines.script: [calm, steady, rallying] Okay. Four barriers. We have a plan for every one of them. [warm, checking in] Everybody ready?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is the snake going to be mean?
lines.script: [small, worried, earnest] Is the snake going to be mean?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It is going to be very, very tired. Be kind about it, and be fast.
lines.script: [gentle, reassuring, quiet] It is going to be very, very tired. [firm, calm, urgent] Be kind about it, and be fast.

lines.text: The Chronos-Leviathan lowers its head. Every clock on its body ticks at once.
lines.script: [reading aloud, ominous, slow] The Chronos-Leviathan lowers its head. [deep, thunderous] Every clock on its body ticks at once.

lines.text: The Chronos-Leviathan lowers its head. Every clock on its body ticks at once.
lines.script: [reading aloud, ominous, slow] The Chronos-Leviathan lowers its head. [deep, thunderous] Every clock on its body ticks at once.

lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Breathe. It is a long fight, and we are a long family. We can do this again.
lines.script: [winded, steadying, encouraging] Up. Everybody up. [calm, breathing] Breathe. [warm, resolved] It is a long fight, and we are a long family. [dry, determined] We can do this again.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: The Leviathan comes apart. It does not die. It comes apart like a watch being taken out of its case, one gear at a time, every one of them still ticking.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, melancholy wonder] The Leviathan comes apart. It does not die. [soft, mesmerized] It comes apart like a watch being taken out of its case, one gear at a time, every one of them still ticking.

lines.text: Where its coil was, there is a room made of glass. A small living room. One lamp, one armchair. A man in a long coat is sitting in it with his hat in his hands. He is a good deal smaller than the shadow he threw.

lines.text: My daughter was nine. I was on a flight. I told her, one more flight next month. It was her birthday. I told my mother the same thing, about the hospital. I told my partner the same thing about everything.

lines.text: Julian.

lines.text: Is he cold?
