lines.script: [sniffing, suspicious, then letting it go] Moo-rielle! You smell like mint. [airy, ominous] We'll talk about it later.

lines.speaker: Pond Grump
lines.text: Grrrumble. Something moved into my pond. It's COLD. I'm a POND grump, not an ICE grump.
lines.script: [cranky, grumbling, offended] Grrrumble. Something moved into my pond. [sputtering] It's COLD. [indignant, wounded dignity] I'm a POND grump, not an ICE grump.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dice says nine. Nine scoops. Nine candles. Let’s go.
lines.script: [focused, ready, rallying] Dice says nine. Nine scoops. Nine candles. [determined] Let’s go.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Nine scoops. Nine candles. Nine years. All of it MELTS.
lines.script: [flat, cold monotone, bitter] Nine scoops. Nine candles. Nine years. [heavy, dread] All of it MELTS.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Not in here. Nothing melts in here. Nothing changes.
lines.script: [low, hollow, clinging] Not in here. [cold, firm] Nothing melts in here. [quiet, pleading underneath] Nothing changes.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Nobody came to MY birthday. So nobody gets one.
lines.script: [sulky, aching, lonely] Nobody came to MY birthday. [flat, final] So nobody gets one.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We get the scoops, we get the sundae, we're home by four. Everybody ready?
lines.script: [calm, steady, rallying] We get the scoops, we get the sundae, we're home by four. [warm, checking in] Everybody ready?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, nothing WORKS.
lines.script: [frustrated, dismayed, panicked] Tah Tah, nothing WORKS.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Good. Nothing changes. Nobody leaves.
lines.script: [slow, satisfied, cold] Good. [heavy, low] Nothing changes. Nobody leaves.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: The scoops stay. The cow stays. The small loud one stays.
lines.script: [flat, possessive, rumbling] The scoops stay. The cow stays. [cold, dismissive] The small loud one stays.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: MOO-RIELLE!
lines.script: [desperate, shrieking] MOO-RIELLE!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Grace. Grab Rose. The other end. Lift with your legs.
lines.script: [urgent but calm, directing, under strain] Grace. Grab Rose. The other end. [steady] Lift with your legs.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We're leaving. We're coming back. That's a promise, not a rule.
lines.script: [low, steady, firm, to the freezer] We're leaving. We're coming back. [warm, solemn] That's a promise, not a rule.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Nobody comes back. Nobody ever comes back.
lines.script: [cold, bleak, hollow] Nobody comes back. [dull, wounded] Nobody ever comes back.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. She's SLIDING.
lines.script: [alarmed, whispering, urgent] Tah Tah. [anxious] She's SLIDING.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: She's frozen, not broken. Keep walking. Don't tip her.
lines.script: [calm, careful, low] She's frozen, not broken. [coaching, steady] Keep walking. Don't tip her.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: He took the scoops. He took Moo-rielle. He FROZE my SISTER. On my BIRTHDAY.
lines.script: [furious, trembling, near tears] He took the scoops. He took Moo-rielle. [shaking, outraged] He FROZE my SISTER. [cracking] On my BIRTHDAY.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know. First things first. Rose. Deedee. Warm.
lines.script: [quiet, steady, compassionate] I know. [practical, commanding] First things first. Rose. Deedee. Warm.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Up, up. It's my birthday. Nobody stays down.
lines.script: [wiping her eyes, resolute, rallying] Up, up. It's my birthday. [fierce, determined] Nobody stays down.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: There's my Tommy! And my girls! And my... oh. OH. Why is Rose in an ice cube.
lines.script: [delighted, welcoming, then confused] There's my Tommy! And my girls! [trailing, spotting something] And my... oh. [alarmed, nurse mode] OH. [bewildered] Why is Rose in an ice cube.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A freezer did it. Long story. Short version: freezer.
lines.script: [dry, deadpan, tired] A freezer did it. Long story. [flat] Short version: freezer.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: He stole the scoops AND Moo-rielle AND he froze Rose. On my BIRTHDAY, Deedee.
lines.script: [indignant, tattling, outraged] He stole the scoops AND Moo-rielle AND he froze Rose. [dramatic] On my BIRTHDAY, Deedee.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: On her BIRTHDAY. Boppy, did you hear that?
lines.script: [scandalized, fierce] On her BIRTHDAY. [calling out, bossy] Boppy, did you hear that?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I heard. I'm sitting. The knee.
lines.script: [gruff, wincing, settled in] I heard. [pained, dry] I'm sitting. The knee.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Hold on, honey. Let me read the cake box first. It has to say dairy free. Where are my glasses.
lines.script: [flustered, fussing, patting her pockets] Hold on, honey. Let me read the cake box first. It has to say dairy free. [frazzled] Where are my glasses.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I had them. I had them a MINUTE ago.
lines.script: [frantic, searching] I had them. [indignant] I had them a MINUTE ago.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: They're in the oven mitt, Dee. You're wearing them. On your hand.
lines.script: [dry, patient, deadpan] They're in the oven mitt, Dee. [flat, amused] You're wearing them. On your hand.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: ...So they are. Don't say anything.
lines.script: [sheepish, caught, defensive] ...So they are. [low, warning] Don't say anything.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I didn't. I said it to Tom.
lines.script: [innocent, dry, straight-faced] I didn't. [deadpan] I said it to Tom.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Dairy free. Good. Now. Rose. Come here, sweetheart. Deedee's got you.
lines.script: [satisfied, brisk, then tender] Dairy free. Good. [softening, warm] Now. Rose. Come here, sweetheart. [tender, hugging her] Deedee's got you.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I was in the MIDDLE of a boo.
lines.script: [groggy, indignant, thawing] I was in the MIDDLE of a boo.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: To the moon and back, Rosie. The MOON. And BACK.
lines.script: [overflowing love, hugging tight] To the moon and back, Rosie. [warm, emphatic] The MOON. And BACK.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Cold doesn't beat cold, Tommy. Warm beats cold. Always has. Ask any nurse.
lines.script: [firm, wise, nurse's certainty] Cold doesn't beat cold, Tommy. [warm, sure] Warm beats cold. Always has. [brisk] Ask any nurse.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Warm beats cold. Okay. What do we have that's warm.
lines.script: [thinking aloud, dry, working it out] Warm beats cold. Okay. [quick, practical] What do we have that's warm.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: My peppers. Out back, in the garden. The hose flinched.
lines.script: [gruff, pointing, grudging] My peppers. Out back, in the garden. [dry, deadpan] The hose flinched.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Don't take the ghost one. The ghost one is MINE.
lines.script: [sharp, possessive, warning] Don't take the ghost one. [firm] The ghost one is MINE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Which one is the ghost one?
lines.script: [curious, practical] Which one is the ghost one?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The one that's looking at you.
lines.script: [low, deadpan, ominous] The one that's looking at you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Boppy's peppers. Red, redder, and one that's looking at me.
lines.script: [reading aloud, dry, deadpan] Boppy's peppers. Red, redder, [wary, uneasy] and one that's looking at me.

lines.speaker: Sprinkle Gremlin
lines.text: Brr! HOT! Ours! He said take every warm thing in town!
lines.script: [shivering, greedy, shrill] Brr! HOT! Ours! [whiny, quoting orders] He said take every warm thing in town!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: He sent gremlins to the GARDEN? Tata, this freezer is organized.
lines.script: [stunned, impressed despite herself, indignant] He sent gremlins to the GARDEN? [dry, exasperated] Tah Tah, this freezer is organized.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boo. I'm practicing.
lines.script: [whispering, practicing, serious] Boo. [earnest] I'm practicing.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Up. Gremlins. We're not losing to GREMLINS on my birthday.
lines.script: [fierce, bossy] Up. Gremlins. [declaring] We're not losing to GREMLINS on my birthday.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: (from the window) That's enough peppers! Leave the ghost one!
lines.script: [hollering, gruff, alarmed] (from the window) That's enough peppers! [warning, firm] Leave the ghost one!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I took a little one. For later. For boos.
lines.script: [sheepish, small, secretive] I took a little one. [earnest] For later. For boos.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Rose, give me the... fine. Keep it. Don't lick it.
lines.script: [dry, resigned, giving in] Rose, give me the... fine. [firm, warning] Keep it. Don't lick it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Three peppers. Warm things, check. Now who knows how a FREEZER works?
lines.script: [brisk, taking charge] Three peppers. Warm things, check. [pondering] Now who knows how a FREEZER works?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mr. Pistachio. He owns a creamery. He's basically a freezer scientist.
lines.script: [dry, lightbulb moment] Mr. Pistachio. [deadpan] He owns a creamery. He's basically a freezer scientist.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: You're back! Did you... oh. No scoops. And the little one looks defrosted.
lines.script: [cheerful, hopeful, then deflating] You're back! Did you... oh. [disappointed] No scoops. [concerned] And the little one looks defrosted.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I was in an ice cube. It was boring.
lines.script: [unimpressed, matter of fact] I was in an ice cube. [flat, bored] It was boring.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mr. Pistachio. Brain Freeze. He came out of YOUR shop. Tell us everything.
lines.script: [serious, steady, direct] Mr. Pistachio. Brain Freeze. He came out of YOUR shop. [gently pressing] Tell us everything.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: ...He was mine. My first chest freezer. Twenty years in the back room. Hum, hum, hum.
lines.script: [quiet, rueful, fond] ...He was mine. My first chest freezer. [soft, nostalgic] Twenty years in the back room. [low, imitating the hum] Hum, hum, hum.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: Every birthday cake in this town sat in him first. Every one. And nobody ever says thank you to a freezer.
lines.script: [wistful, earnest, tender] Every birthday cake in this town sat in him first. Every one. [sad, rueful] And nobody ever says thank you to a freezer.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: I replaced him in the spring. Newer. Quieter. I unplugged him on a Tuesday and I didn't even say goodbye.
lines.script: [guilty, subdued] I replaced him in the spring. Newer. Quieter. [heavy, ashamed] I unplugged him on a Tuesday and I didn't even say goodbye.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: So nobody came to his birthday because... he never HAD one.
lines.script: [slow, dawning realization, softening] So nobody came to his birthday because... [quiet, understanding] he never HAD one.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: He kept everybody else's. He never got his own.
lines.script: [quiet, heavy, rueful] He kept everybody else's. [aching] He never got his own.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: Here's the thing about a freezer, Tom. The outside is the soft part. The door. People stick things on it. Photos. Drawings. Report cards.
lines.script: [gentle, explaining, warm] Here's the thing about a freezer, Tom. The outside is the soft part. The door. [fond, listing] People stick things on it. Photos. Drawings. Report cards.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: In twenty years, nobody stuck one thing on him. Not one.
lines.script: [hushed, sorrowful] In twenty years, nobody stuck one thing on him. [barely a whisper] Not one.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. Is the present a puppy?
lines.script: [hopeful, tugging his sleeve, scheming] Tah Tah. [earnest] Is the present a puppy?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...After cake.
lines.script: [dry, flustered, glancing at his bag] ...After cake.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, you looked at your BAG.
lines.script: [accusing, triumphant, gotcha] Tah Tah, you looked at your BAG.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I looked at the floor. The floor is near the bag.
lines.script: [deadpan, innocent, flat] I looked at the floor. [straight-faced] The floor is near the bag.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: Take these. Hot cocoa. My recipe. If you're going back up there, you'll want something warm in you.
lines.script: [warm, pressing things into their hands] Take these. Hot cocoa. My recipe. [kind, practical] If you're going back up there, you'll want something warm in you.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: And Tom. If you get his door open, tell him I said happy birthday. Twenty years late.
lines.script: [warm, heartfelt, thick-voiced] And Tom. If you get his door open, tell him I said happy birthday. [soft, rueful] Twenty years late.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: There they are. No scoops. One defrosted child. Tom, status report. Ten words or less.
lines.script: [brisk, coach voice, surveying] There they are. No scoops. One defrosted child. [crisp, demanding] Tom, status report. Ten words or less.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Freezer. Sad. Never had a birthday. Stole everything. We're going back.
lines.script: [rapid, clipped, deadpan] Freezer. Sad. Never had a birthday. Stole everything. [steady] We're going back.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Nine words. Good.
lines.script: [approving, dry, counting] Nine words. Good.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Okay. Listen to me. I've run thirty marathons and taught four hundred kids. You don't out-freeze a freezer.
lines.script: [firm, coaching, intense] Okay. Listen to me. [proud, matter of fact] I've run thirty marathons and taught four hundred kids. [sharp, conviction] You don't out-freeze a freezer.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You bring the party TO him. Warm things. Loud things. The works.
lines.script: [rallying, brisk, strategic] You bring the party TO him. [punchy] Warm things. Loud things. The works.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dad, why does a BANNER have copper?
lines.script: [puzzled, suspicious, to her dad] Dad, why does a BANNER have copper?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Freezers have doors. Doors take magnets. Hang it ON him.
lines.script: [brisk, inspired, certain] Freezers have doors. Doors take magnets. [commanding] Hang it ON him.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: ON him?
lines.script: [puzzled, small] ON him?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: ON him. And Rose, baby, you Boo him so hard he forgets his own name.
lines.script: [firm, emphatic, then affectionate] ON him. [warm, coaching] And Rose, baby, you Boo him so hard he forgets his own name.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I have a pepper for it.
lines.script: [proud, earnest, serious] I have a pepper for it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: ...We'll talk about the pepper later.
lines.script: [dry, trailing, side eye] ...We'll talk about the pepper later.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Pip, Moss and Dot are coming at four. Deedee's cake is done. All you need is nine scoops and one freezer.
lines.script: [brisk, laying out the plan] Pip, Moss and Dot are coming at four. Deedee's cake is done. [crisp, encouraging] All you need is nine scoops and one freezer.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And Moo-rielle.
lines.script: [quiet, determined, tender] And Moo-rielle.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: And Moo-rielle. Go. Love you. Don't tip your sister.
lines.script: [warm, proud, sending them off] And Moo-rielle. Go. [tender, loving] Love you. [brisk, teasing] Don't tip your sister.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Up, up. It's still my birthday. We go AGAIN.
lines.script: [fierce, rallying, a little worn] Up, up. It's still my birthday. [determined] We go AGAIN.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: ...You came back.
lines.script: [startled, flat, thrown] ...You came back.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Nobody comes back.
lines.script: [hollow, bitter, disbelieving] Nobody comes back.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's STILL my birthday. And you have my COW.
lines.script: [defiant, bossy, hands on hips] It's STILL my birthday. [furious] And you have my COW.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I have a pepper in my pocket and I'm not afraid to use it.
lines.script: [grim, serious, whisper-shouting] I have a pepper in my pocket and I'm not afraid to use it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody's afraid of the pepper, Rose. Everybody ready? Warm things out.
lines.script: [dry, deadpan, then rallying] Nobody's afraid of the pepper, Rose. [steady, calm] Everybody ready? Warm things out.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He tried to freeze me AGAIN. I'm spicy now. He can't.
lines.script: [defiant, proud, indignant] He tried to freeze me AGAIN. [fierce] I'm spicy now. He can't.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Good. Nothing changes. Nobody leaves. Nobody grows up. Nobody forgets a birthday.
lines.script: [cold, heavy, clinging] Good. Nothing changes. Nobody leaves. [low, bleak] Nobody grows up. [sad, brittle] Nobody forgets a birthday.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: ...Wait. Mr. Pistachio said. The DOOR.
lines.script: [stopping short, dawning realization] ...Wait. [excited whisper] Mr. Pistachio said. The DOOR.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. He needs something on his door. Something that's HIS.
lines.script: [urgent, thinking fast] Tah Tah. He needs something on his door. [sure, gentle] Something that's HIS.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...Okay. Presents are before cake. New rule.
lines.script: [thoughtful, dry, conceding] ...Okay. [decisive, a small smile] Presents are before cake. New rule.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: An INSTAX. Tata. A PRINTER. For PHOTOS.
lines.script: [squealing, awed, clutching the box] An INSTAX. Tah Tah. [breathless] A PRINTER. For PHOTOS.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: ...The cab photo. This morning. All of us.
lines.script: [soft, remembering, lighting up] ...The cab photo. This morning. All of us.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Pair it to my phone. One tap. It's still on there.
lines.script: [quick, calm, practical] Pair it to my phone. One tap. [reassuring] It's still on there.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Printing...
lines.script: [hushed, anticipating, watching the printer] Printing...

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You don't have to freeze it. You just take a picture. See? It stays.
lines.script: [gentle, earnest, to the freezer] You don't have to freeze it. You just take a picture. [soft, sure] See? It stays.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That's us. On your door. Happy birthday, Brain Freeze.
lines.script: [tender, warm, sticking it on the door] That's us. On your door. [soft, heartfelt] Happy birthday, Brain Freeze.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: And the BANNER. Dad made it light up.
lines.script: [proud, bouncing, helpful] And the BANNER. [beaming] Dad made it light up.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: ...It's warm. Why's the picture WARM.
lines.script: [stunned, small, bewildered] ...It's warm. [wondering, cracking] Why's the picture WARM.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: My lid. My LID. It's OPENING.
lines.script: [panicked, creaking, astonished] My lid. My LID. [overwhelmed] It's OPENING.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Then it's round two. Birthday Wish is ready. All three of us.
lines.script: [triumphant, fierce, rallying] Then it's round two. [bold] Birthday Wish is ready. All three of us.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody ready? It's still her birthday.
lines.script: [calm, steady, rallying] Everybody ready? [dry, quietly fond] It's still her birthday.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: ...Nobody ever warmed me up before. Take the scoops. They're in the freezer. Where scoops go.
lines.script: [soft, stunned, humble] ...Nobody ever warmed me up before. [quiet, sincere] Take the scoops. [small, with a hum] They're in the freezer. Where scoops go.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Fine. FINE. Take the scoops. They're in the freezer. Where scoops go.
lines.script: [gruff, embarrassed, huffing] Fine. FINE. [muttering, softened] Take the scoops. They're in the freezer. Where scoops go.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: All nine. Still perfect. And MOO-RIELLE. You were on a FREEZER. We'll talk about it later.
lines.script: [checking, relieved, gleeful] All nine. Still perfect. [clutching her, scolding lovingly] And MOO-RIELLE. You were on a FREEZER. [airy, ominous] We'll talk about it later.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mr. Pistachio says happy birthday. Twenty years late.
lines.script: [quiet, warm, gentle] Mr. Pistachio says happy birthday. [soft, rueful] Twenty years late.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: ...He remembered?
lines.script: [small, thrown, tender] ...He remembered?

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Hum.
lines.script: [soft, content hum, thawing] Hum.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Come to my party.
lines.script: [warm, simple, inviting] Come to my party.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: ...Nobody has ever... Is there cake?
lines.script: [hesitant, wondering, vulnerable] ...Nobody has ever... [shy, hopeful] Is there cake?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: There's a LOT of cake.
lines.script: [warm, dry, reassuring] There's a LOT of cake.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: I'll bring the ice. I'm mostly ice.
lines.script: [shy, pleased, eager] I'll bring the ice. [dry, deadpan] I'm mostly ice.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He can sit next to the duck.
lines.script: [earnest, generous, matter of fact] He can sit next to the duck.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You got them? All nine? Tom, I could KISS you. I won't. I'm sweaty.
lines.script: [flushed, delighted, breathless] You got them? All nine? [warm, gushing] Tom, I could KISS you. [teasing, wry] I won't. I'm sweaty.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Cake is on the counter. Dairy free. I read the box nine times. With my glasses.
lines.script: [proud, fussy, satisfied] Cake is on the counter. Dairy free. [emphatic, a little frazzled] I read the box nine times. [pointed, smug] With my glasses.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Nine scoops. In my day we got one scoop. And a lecture.
lines.script: [gruff, nostalgic, grumbling] Nine scoops. [dry, deadpan] In my day we got one scoop. [wry] And a lecture.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: My rock says happy birthday. He's on the counter. Please don't frost him.
lines.script: [soft, earnest, protective] My rock says happy birthday. [gentle, worried] He's on the counter. Please don't frost him.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: I brought a tree. A small one. It said it wanted to come.
lines.script: [slow, dreamy, quietly pleased] I brought a tree. A small one. [mellow] It said it wanted to come.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Twelve people, one duck, one cow. I counted twice. The freezer counts as a person.
lines.script: [crisp, rapid, proud of her accuracy] Twelve people, one duck, one cow. I counted twice. [matter of fact] The freezer counts as a person.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: I brought ice. Where do you want the ice.
lines.script: [flat, hesitant, awkward but eager] I brought ice. [stiff, earnest] Where do you want the ice.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Nobody told me there'd be a FREEZER at the table.
lines.script: [suspicious, gruff, grumbling] Nobody told me there'd be a FREEZER at the table.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: He's a guest, Boppy. Sit. He can sit next to you. You could use the cold on that knee.
lines.script: [firm, scolding sweetly, bossy] He's a guest, Boppy. Sit. [practical, nurse tone] He can sit next to you. You could use the cold on that knee.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: Cones for everybody. And... hey, old friend. Happy birthday. I'm sorry it took twenty years.
lines.script: [booming, warm, then soft and sincere] Cones for everybody. And... hey, old friend. [heartfelt, tender] Happy birthday. [quiet, remorseful] I'm sorry it took twenty years.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: ...Hum.
lines.script: [quiet, overwhelmed, soft hum] ...Hum.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: That's a happy hum.
lines.script: [soft, shy, glowing] That's a happy hum.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody, this is the Nine Scoop Sundae. Vanilla, strawberry, mint, chocolate, cookie dough, coffee, peanut butter, lemon, and black and white cookie on top.
lines.script: [proud, announcing, dry warmth] Everybody, this is the Nine Scoop Sundae. [reading the list, savoring] Vanilla, strawberry, mint, chocolate, cookie dough, coffee, peanut butter, lemon, [pleased] and black and white cookie on top.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Moo-rielle gets her own tiny scoop. Mint. She earned it.
lines.script: [tender, proud, generous] Moo-rielle gets her own tiny scoop. [warm, matter of fact] Mint. She earned it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Candles! Everybody sing! Grace, make a wish!
lines.script: [cheering, brisk, joyful] Candles! Everybody sing! [warm, excited] Grace, make a wish!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: ...I blew them out. The duck made me.
lines.script: [sheepish, small, matter of fact] ...I blew them out. [blaming, earnest] The duck made me.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: ROSE.
lines.script: [outraged, shrieking, betrayed] ROSE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Relight. Nine candles. Hold still, please.
lines.script: [dry, patient, resigned] Relight. Nine candles. [calm, gentle] Hold still, please.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Okay. For real this time. I wish...
lines.script: [eyes closed, solemn, hushed] Okay. For real this time. [slow, quiet, wishing] I wish...

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I'm not telling. That's the rule. I didn't make the rule.
lines.script: [coy, smug, sassy] I'm not telling. [pert, matter of fact] That's the rule. I didn't make the rule.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Nine candles, one breath. I counted. Perfect score.
lines.script: [crisp, delighted, proud] Nine candles, one breath. I counted. [beaming] Perfect score.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: ...This is a good birthday. I'm putting it on my door.
lines.script: [quiet, content, wondering] ...This is a good birthday. [soft, shy] I'm putting it on my door.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Oh! Penny called. She's got birthday things for you at the shop, Grace. Three of them. On the house.
lines.script: [bright, excited, announcing] Oh! Penny called. She's got birthday things for you at the shop, Grace. [warm, teasing] Three of them. On the house.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: A SASH? Is one of them a SASH?
lines.script: [gasping, squealing, hopeful] A SASH? Is one of them a SASH?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Go see. After cake.
lines.script: [warm, teasing, knowing] Go see. [firm, playful] After cake.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hold on. It's your mom.
lines.script: [dry, glancing at his phone, bracing] Hold on. [wry] It's your mom.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom. Don't panic. I'm panicking enough for both of us.
lines.script: [brisk, frayed, forced calm] Tom. Don't panic. [wry, high-strung] I'm panicking enough for both of us.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The invitations never went out. Justin was supposed to mail them Monday. Justin was at work Monday. Justin is at work now.
lines.script: [clipped, mounting disbelief] The invitations never went out. Justin was supposed to mail them Monday. [flat, pointed] Justin was at work Monday. [weary] Justin is at work now.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Grace's friends are in the Square. Pip, Moss and Dot. Hand them out. By HAND. Like it's 1994.
lines.script: [commanding, coaching] Grace's friends are in the Square. Pip, Moss and Dot. Hand them out. [emphatic] By HAND. [dry] Like it's nineteen ninety-four.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: MOM. It's fine. I'll invite them myself. I'm very persuasive.
lines.script: [bossy, unbothered, tossing her hair] MOM. It's fine. [smug] I'll invite them myself. I'm very persuasive.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You get that from me. Go. Love you. Scoops, friends, home by four.
lines.script: [proud, fond, rushing them out] You get that from me. Go. Love you. [quick, briskly listing] Scoops, friends, home by four.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can I invite the duck?
lines.script: [hopeful, very serious, hugging the duck] Can I invite the duck?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The duck is already coming. The duck is in your arms.
lines.script: [deadpan, gently amused] The duck is already coming. [dry beat] The duck is in your arms.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Pip! My party. Today. Four o'clock. There's a sundae with NINE scoops.
lines.script: [bright, bossy, pulling Pip aside] Pip! My party. Today. Four o'clock. [thrilled, wide-eyed] There's a sundae with NINE scoops.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Can my rock come? He's never been to a party.
lines.script: [earnest, soft, protective] Can my rock come? [gently pleading] He's never been to a party.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: He gets nervous around cake. He'll be fine. He's a rock.
lines.script: [tender, reassuring like about a pet] He gets nervous around cake. [sincere, matter of fact] He'll be fine. He's a rock.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Rocks LOVE cake.
lines.script: [fiercely certain, whisper-shouting] Rocks LOVE cake.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Then we'll be there. Both of us. He'll bring a gift. It's a smaller rock.
lines.script: [relieved, soft joy] Then we'll be there. Both of us. [proud, hushed] He'll bring a gift. It's a smaller rock.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Three friends. Three scoops so far. I like threes.
lines.script: [pleased, tallying like a tidy fact] Three friends. Three scoops so far. [fond, satisfied] I like threes.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Six scoops to go. North. Into the Hollow.
lines.script: [dry, rallying, pointing north] Six scoops to go. [steady] North. Into the Hollow.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Moss! Party. My house. Four. Bring nothing. Bring yourself.
lines.script: [bright, bossy host, warm] Moss! Party. My house. Four. [grand, generous] Bring nothing. Bring yourself.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: I asked the tree if I should go.
lines.script: [slow, dreamy, quietly proud] I asked the tree if I should go.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: It said nothing. That means yes. Trees are very supportive.
lines.script: [slow, mellow, pleased with his logic] It said nothing. [long pause, serene] That means yes. [warm] Trees are very supportive.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: Also, the tree says a freezer went north this morning. Humming. It wasn't happy.
lines.script: [lowering his voice, drifting, a little uneasy] Also, the tree says a freezer went north this morning. [slow] Humming. [soft, sorry] It wasn't happy.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thank the tree for us.
lines.script: [dry, kind, playing along] Thank the tree for us.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: I already did. It said nothing. Very gracious.
lines.script: [slow, content, tiny smile] I already did. [mellow, pleased] It said nothing. Very gracious.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dot! My birthday party. Today. Will you come?
lines.script: [bright, hopeful, hands clasped] Dot! My birthday party. Today. [bossy-sweet] Will you come?

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Nine years. Nine scoops. Nine candles. That's twenty-seven nines. I'll be there.
lines.script: [crisp, delighted by the math] Nine years. Nine scoops. Nine candles. [fast, proud of accuracy] That's twenty-seven nines. [brisk] I'll be there.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: I'll count the guests. Somebody has to.
lines.script: [brisk, dutiful, important] I'll count the guests. [dry] Somebody has to.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Count the duck too.
lines.script: [earnest, insistent] Count the duck too.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: One duck. Counted.
lines.script: [crisp, satisfied, ticking a box] One duck. Counted.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: I'm taking my pet rock for a walk.
lines.script: [soft, sincere, proud like a new pet owner] I'm taking my pet rock for a walk.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: He's shy. Please don't make eye contact.
lines.script: [hushed, protective] He's shy. [gentle, pleading] Please don't make eye contact.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Excellent. He's already learned 'stay'.
lines.script: [delighted, whispering with pride] Excellent. He's already learned 'stay'.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: I asked a tree for directions.
lines.script: [slow, dreamy, matter of fact] I asked a tree for directions.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: It said nothing. Very mysterious.
lines.script: [mellow, long pause, mildly impressed] It said nothing. [dreamy] Very mysterious.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: I think I'm barking up the wrong tree.
lines.script: [slow, quietly pleased with his own pun] I think I'm barking up the wrong tree.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: Ten doors and THREE gaps in the trees now. Somebody opened one by the school.
lines.script: [crisp, excited, tallying fast] Ten doors and THREE gaps in the trees now. [scandalized, quick] Somebody opened one by the school.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: I had to start all over. I'm at four hundred and six.
lines.script: [deflated, clipped, aggrieved] I had to start all over. [flat, precise] I'm at four hundred and six.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: You got the tin back? Ten doors, two gaps, one pie tin. All accounted for.
lines.script: [brisk, pleased] You got the tin back? [proud, ticking off] Ten doors, two gaps, one pie tin. All accounted for.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: A mud blob ran through the Square with a pie tin. One blob. One tin. I counted.
lines.script: [fast, indignant witness, precise] A mud blob ran through the Square with a pie tin. [crisp] One blob. One tin. [proud] I counted.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: It went north. Into the gap in the trees. Gap number one.
lines.script: [crisp, pointing] It went north. Into the gap in the trees. [exact] Gap number one.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: This town has ten doors and two gaps in the trees.
lines.script: [quick, matter of fact, tally voice] This town has ten doors and two gaps in the trees.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: I've counted them seventeen times.
lines.script: [proud, a little obsessive] I've counted them seventeen times.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: Tomorrow I'm moving on to windows.
lines.script: [brisk, resolved, already moving on] Tomorrow I'm moving on to windows.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: I'm training for the annual sit-down.
lines.script: [slow, dignified, deadpan serious] I'm training for the annual sit-down.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: My coach is a bench.
lines.script: [unhurried, deadpan] My coach is a bench.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: We have a very supportive relationship.
lines.script: [warm, creaky, dignified] We have a very supportive relationship.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: A mud blob just ran past me carrying a pie.
lines.script: [cheerful, amazed, quick] A mud blob just ran past me carrying a pie.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: I didn't stop it. I collect wrong turns, not pies.
lines.script: [breezy, unbothered, shrugging] I didn't stop it. [cheerful, proud] I collect wrong turns, not pies.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: Boppy went by with a fishing rod and a jar of peppers.
lines.script: [chatty, bright] Boppy went by with a fishing rod and a jar of peppers.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: He was walking slower than me. Nobody walks slower than me. I collect slow walks too, now.
lines.script: [rambling, marveling] He was walking slower than me. [astonished] Nobody walks slower than me. [cheerful] I collect slow walks too, now.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: I'm not lost. I'm collecting wrong turns.
lines.script: [sunny, breezy, unbothered] I'm not lost. [proud] I'm collecting wrong turns.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: That pond up north owes me an apology.
lines.script: [cheerful, mock grudge] That pond up north owes me an apology.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: Long story. Short socks.
lines.script: [light, cryptic, shrugging with a grin] Long story. Short socks.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Your father caught Old Iron-Gill? And let him GO? Forty years of telling that story, and now it's true.
lines.script: [astonished, slow, then roaring with delight] Your father caught Old Iron-Gill? And let him GO? [dry, wondering] Forty years of telling that story, and now it's true.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: He came by the shack this morning. The fish, not your father. Just floated there. I think he wanted to say hello.
lines.script: [quiet, wondering, a little moved] He came by the shack this morning. [dry] The fish, not your father. [soft] Just floated there. I think he wanted to say hello.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: You saw it? Old Iron-Gill? Forty years I have run this shack. I thought it was a story.
lines.script: [hushed, incredulous, dazed] You saw it? Old Iron-Gill? [slow, weighty] Forty years I have run this shack. [small, wondering] I thought it was a story.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: It went west, into the marsh. The Whispering Marsh. The reeds talk out there. Mostly nonsense.
lines.script: [low, pointing west, storyteller] It went west, into the marsh. The Whispering Marsh. [dry, shrugging] The reeds talk out there. Mostly nonsense.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Bait shack is open. Worms, minnows, and a sandwich I'm not selling.
lines.script: [dry, gravelly, flat sales pitch] Bait shack is open. Worms, minnows, and a sandwich I'm not selling.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Your father has been fishing this pier since before the pier. He has caught nothing. Very consistent.
lines.script: [deadpan, quietly fond] Your father has been fishing this pier since before the pier. [flat, tickled] He has caught nothing. [dry] Very consistent.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: They say a catfish lives out there older than the boards. I say they say a lot.
lines.script: [low, sly, skeptical] They say a catfish lives out there older than the boards. [dry shrug] I say they say a lot.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Thirty parents. Zero tears. One very well-behaved pen. Best conference night in thirty-one years.
lines.script: [tired, deadpan, quietly delighted] Thirty parents. Zero tears. [dry] One very well-behaved pen. [warm, proud] Best conference night in thirty-one years.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Come to Field Day, Tom. Amy runs the relay. Amy always runs the relay.
lines.script: [warm, easy invitation] Come to Field Day, Tom. [wry] Amy runs the relay. [dry, knowing] Amy always runs the relay.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Conferences start at seven. SEVEN. The bells say otherwise. The bells are wrong.
lines.script: [stern, exasperated, pointed] Conferences start at seven. [emphatic] SEVEN. [irritated] The bells say otherwise. [flat] The bells are wrong.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Clear the rooms, set the hallway clocks to seven, and the Cafetorium will open. I hope.
lines.script: [brisk, hopeful, giving orders] Clear the rooms, set the hallway clocks to seven, and the Cafetorium will open. [fingers crossed, small] I hope.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Principal Pruitt. Thirty-one years at Long Island Elementary. I've seen everything. Not tonight, though. Tonight is new.
lines.script: [proud, weathered, then electric] Principal Pruitt. Thirty-one years at Long Island Elementary. [seasoned] I've seen everything. [low, excited] Not tonight, though. Tonight is new.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: Marco is reading at a third-grade level! Mrs. Gregori showed me the chart. There was a chart!
lines.script: [bursting with pride, giddy] Marco is reading at a third-grade level! [thrilled] Mrs. Gregori showed me the chart. [gleeful] There was a chart!

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: I cried a little. In the minivan. Don't tell Marco.
lines.script: [sheepish, tender] I cried a little. In the minivan. [hushed, pleading] Don't tell Marco.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: I'm Marco’s dad. Marco says Mrs. Gregori is the toughest teacher in the whole school.
lines.script: [friendly, chatty, proud dad] I'm Marco's dad. [amused, impressed] Marco says Mrs. Gregori is the toughest teacher in the whole school.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: Marco also says she's his favorite. Please don't tell Marco I told you.
lines.script: [warm, conspiratorial, smiling] Marco also says she's his favorite. [quick, whispering] Please don't tell Marco I told you.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: Thirty conferences, nine hundred cookies, one laminator. Everything went on schedule. MY schedule.
lines.script: [crisp, triumphant, tallying] Thirty conferences, nine hundred cookies, one laminator. [smug, regal] Everything went on schedule. [pointed] MY schedule.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: Tell Mrs. Gregori her bulletin board is the best in the building. Don't tell the other teachers.
lines.script: [low, conspiratorial, leaning in] Tell Mrs. Gregori her bulletin board is the best in the building. [sly, hushed] Don't tell the other teachers.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: Kowalski. PTA president. I brought nine hundred cookies and a laminator.
lines.script: [brisk, commanding, proud] Kowalski. PTA president. [matter of fact, smug] I brought nine hundred cookies and a laminator.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: The sign-up sheet RAN AWAY. On little paper legs. I've never been so offended.
lines.script: [scandalized, vibrating with offense] The sign-up sheet RAN AWAY. [incredulous] On little paper legs. [wounded] I've never been so offended.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: They fixed the bells! In my lifetime! I'm going to tell everyone at the diner.
lines.script: [delighted, creaky, amazed] They fixed the bells! [wondering] In my lifetime! [chuffed] I'm going to tell everyone at the diner.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: I'm here for my grandson. He's in the second grade. I was in the second grade here in 1956.
lines.script: [slow, warm, proud grandpa] I'm here for my grandson. He's in the second grade. [dry, reminiscing] I was in the second grade here in nineteen fifty-six.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: The bells were wrong in 1956 too. Nobody fixed them. Things were simpler.
lines.script: [dry, unhurried, nostalgic] The bells were wrong in nineteen fifty-six too. [shrug, deadpan] Nobody fixed them. [fond] Things were simpler.

lines.speaker: bun
lines.text: Welcome! Our bread is emotionally available.
lines.script: [bubbly, bright shop greeter, smiling] Welcome! [pleased with her pun] Our bread is emotionally available.

lines.speaker: bun
lines.text: The baguettes? A little crusty.
lines.script: [playful, wink in her voice] The baguettes? [giggling] A little crusty.

lines.speaker: bun
lines.text: Today's special is yesterday's tomorrow toast.
lines.script: [chipper, proud of the pun, grand announcement] Today's special is yesterday's tomorrow toast.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: It's quiet. Properly quiet. The good kind. Thank you, Tom.
lines.script: [hushed, deeply relieved, sincere] It's quiet. Properly quiet. The good kind. [warm whisper] Thank you, Tom.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: Story time is Saturdays now. The Unread asked for Grace. By name.
lines.script: [soft whisper, pleased, a little amazed] Story time is Saturdays now. [wondering] The Unread asked for Grace. By name.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: The Stacks are through the staff door. Please be careful. And please don't answer the books.
lines.script: [low whisper, grave, warning] The Stacks are through the staff door. Please be careful. [urgent hush] And please don't answer the books.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: I'm fine. Everything is fine. The dictionaries haven't slept in a week.
lines.script: [brittle whisper, sleepless, forced calm] I'm fine. Everything is fine. [haggard] The dictionaries haven't slept in a week.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: It's fine. Everything is fine. Please whisper.
lines.script: [strained whisper, twitchy, unconvincing] It's fine. Everything is fine. [sharp hush] Please whisper.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: ...Did you hear that? That wasn't me. I'd know my own shush.
lines.script: [whispering, freezing, spooked] ...Did you hear that? [prim, rattled] That wasn't me. I'd know my own shush.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: Please whisper. The dictionaries are sleeping.
lines.script: [prim whisper, precise] Please whisper. [hushed, deadpan] The dictionaries are sleeping.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: Someone shelved a sandwich under 'S'.
lines.script: [scandalized whisper, droll] Someone shelved a sandwich under 'S'.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: Technically correct. Deeply concerning.
lines.script: [dry whisper, pained] Technically correct. [grave] Deeply concerning.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: I name every plant here.
lines.script: [soft, airy, tender with her plants] I name every plant here.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: They're all called Steve. It saves time.
lines.script: [gentle, quietly funny] They're all called Steve. [serene] It saves time.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Except that one. That's Assistant Steve.
lines.script: [hushed, fond, nodding toward one plant] Except that one. [affectionate] That's Assistant Steve.

lines.speaker: kit
lines.text: Your parcel is arriving any Tuesday now.
lines.script: [chipper, brisk, wink in the voice] Your parcel is arriving any Tuesday now.

lines.speaker: kit
lines.text: The snails asked for smaller uniforms.
lines.script: [cheery, deadpan report] The snails asked for smaller uniforms.

lines.speaker: kit
lines.text: I deliver good news. Bad news has to walk.
lines.script: [bright, proud, then a wry shrug] I deliver good news. [wink] Bad news has to walk.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: The kettle is still going on about that man in the long coat. Gold coins. Paying double.
lines.script: [leaning in, gossipy, relishing it] The kettle is still going on about that man in the long coat. [low, scandalized] Gold coins. Paying double.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: I told it to mind its own business. It's a kettle. It has no business.
lines.script: [prim, sly, little cackle] I told it to mind its own business. [dry] It's a kettle. It has no business.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: The kettle has been gossiping again.
lines.script: [conspiratorial whisper, cozy and sly] The kettle has been gossiping again.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: It spilled the tea. Literally.
lines.script: [delighted, pleased with the pun, small cackle] It spilled the tea. [sly beat] Literally.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: Please mind the dramatic biscuits.
lines.script: [breezy, warm, mock serious] Please mind the dramatic biscuits.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: The moon is back. I looked at it for an hour. I didn't even write anything down.
lines.script: [soft, wondering, quietly joyful] The moon is back. I looked at it for an hour. [dreamy, a little amazed] I didn't even write anything down.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: I swept the club stairs. Twelve years of wondering, and it was just a very dusty party.
lines.script: [drifting, wry, a little rueful] I swept the club stairs. [soft, wondering] Twelve years of wondering, and it was just a very dusty party.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: The door is open. Twelve years I have swept this floor, and that door is open.
lines.script: [slow, hushed awe] The door is open. [drifting, weighty] Twelve years I have swept this floor, and that door is open.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: If you see the moon up there, please tell it to come home. My telescope misses it.
lines.script: [wistful, tender, a bit embarrassed] If you see the moon up there, please tell it to come home. [small, sincere] My telescope misses it.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: There's supposed to be a full moon tonight. My telescope can't find it.
lines.script: [worried, soft, puzzled] There's supposed to be a full moon tonight. [quiet, uneasy] My telescope can't find it.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: It's not behind a cloud. It's just not THERE. I checked four times.
lines.script: [spacey, rattled, insisting] It's not behind a cloud. [hushed, unsettled] It's just not THERE. [small] I checked four times.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: I've discovered a new constellation.
lines.script: [dreamy, thrilled discovery] I've discovered a new constellation.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: It's shaped exactly like my laundry.
lines.script: [sheepish, soft, deflating] It's shaped exactly like my laundry.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: Space is asking me to tidy up.
lines.script: [drifting, gently resigned] Space is asking me to tidy up.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Welcome to Penny's Pockets. I sell things for pockets. Also things for people.
lines.script: [bright saleswoman, warm, fast patter] Welcome to Penny's Pockets. I sell things for pockets. [playful] Also things for people.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Gear for the whole family, snacks for fights, and a few things that go POP. Gently.
lines.script: [quick pitch, winking] Gear for the whole family, snacks for fights, and a few things that go POP. [sweet, cheeky] Gently.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Got something to sell? I buy almost anything. Not Steve. Never Steve.
lines.script: [eager, coaxing, then firm] Got something to sell? I buy almost anything. [sharp, dramatic] Not Steve. Never Steve.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Back again! The coins missed you.
lines.script: [delighted, warm, mock fond] Back again! [playful] The coins missed you.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Browse all you like. Browsing is free. Buying is better.
lines.script: [easy, pitchy, teasing] Browse all you like. Browsing is free. [cheeky, sing-song] Buying is better.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Fresh stock. Same Penny.
lines.script: [breezy, proud, quick] Fresh stock. [wink] Same Penny.

lines.speaker: sal
lines.text: Long Island Taxi. We go anywhere in town. Town is small, so mostly here.
lines.script: [fast, friendly, proud of his cab] Long Island Taxi. We go anywhere in town. [dry, chuckling] Town is small, so mostly here.

lines.speaker: sal
lines.text: I have one cab. It's cab seven. Cabs one through six are a dream I'm working on.
lines.script: [proud, dramatic, grand] I have one cab. It's cab seven. [wistful, chuckling] Cabs one through six are a dream I'm working on.

lines.speaker: sal
lines.text: You just rode with me. You tipped in sourdough starter. Odd. Generous.
lines.script: [warm, puzzled, amused] You just rode with me. You tipped in sourdough starter. [shrugging, fond] Odd. Generous.

lines.text: I work at Meta. I build things that connect people. Right now I'm connecting a four-year-old to a nap.

lines.text: Yes, Olivia. Heard you. Handled. Lachlan, we do not lick the fence.

lines.text: Isla said her first word last week. It was no. She uses it very well.
lines.script: [deadpan, proud dad] Isla said her first word last week. [dry] It was no. [amused] She uses it very well.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: I took a meeting today with Isla on my lap. She muted me. Best meeting of the quarter.
lines.script: [dry, weary, tickled] I took a meeting today with Isla on my lap. She muted me. [deadpan] Best meeting of the quarter.

lines.text: My arms have never been stronger. I haven't lifted a weight in four years.
lines.script: [dry, flat, mildly proud] My arms have never been stronger. [deadpan] I haven't lifted a weight in four years.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Olivia writes about AI taking jobs. Nobody is coming for mine. Nobody wants bedtime.
lines.script: [wry, calm, amused] Olivia writes about AI taking jobs. [dry] Nobody is coming for mine. [deadpan] Nobody wants bedtime.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington

lines.text: ...and that’s why you never trust a Tuesday. Hm? Did I fall asleep? Again?

lines.text: Back in 1979, nobody got stuck on a sentence. Well. Harold did.
lines.script: [slow, fond, reminiscing] Back in nineteen seventy-nine, nobody got stuck on a sentence. [dry, warm] Well. Harold did.

lines.text: That coat looks right on you. My daddy would say so. Then he'd say stand up straight.
lines.script: [warm, slow, fond] That coat looks right on you. My daddy would say so. [gentle, chuckling] Then he'd say stand up straight.

lines.text: Forty loaves. I ate four. Don't tell Bernadette.
lines.script: [slow, confiding, a little guilty] Forty loaves. I ate four. [low, sly] Don't tell Bernadette.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: Forty years I've made gumbo for this potluck. Today the stove won't light. The flame just leans. Toward the boulevard.
lines.script: [slow, worried, puzzled] Forty years I've made gumbo for this potluck. Today the stove won't light. [low, uneasy] The flame just leans. Toward the boulevard.

lines.script: [wry, fond, reminiscing] Back in nineteen seventy-nine the squirrels were polite. [dry] They waited until you finished your sandwich.

lines.text: Somebody took my reading glasses off the porch rail. I have read the same headline for three days.

lines.text: I think it says WEATHER. It might say WHETHER.
lines.script: [squinting, uncertain, wry] I think it says WEATHER. [dry beat] It might say WHETHER.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: Back in 1979, this whole block...
lines.script: [slow, settling into a story, then trailing off] Back in nineteen seventy-nine, this whole block...

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: Such a nice afternoon. It should always be this afternoon. Nobody needs to get any older.
lines.script: [drowsy, content, sighing] Such a nice afternoon. [soft, wishing] It should always be this afternoon. [gentle] Nobody needs to get any older.

lines.text: Where was I? Oh. 1979. This whole block smelled like gumbo on a Saturday night.
lines.script: [slow, waking, then warm and fond] Where was I? Oh. Nineteen seventy-nine. [savoring] This whole block smelled like gumbo on a Saturday night.

lines.text: Thank you, Tom. And your young man. And the dog. Especially the dog.
lines.script: [warm, heartfelt, gravelly] Thank you, Tom. And your young man. [fond, chuckling] And the dog. Especially the dog.

lines.script: [slow, contented, settled] Bought this house in nineteen seventy-nine. [warm] Same porch, same chair, same view.

lines.script: [fond, wistful, drifting back] Back then you could hear zydeco from the boulevard on a Saturday night.

lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, tender wonder] Marisol is amber from her shoulders to her sneakers. The leash runs from her hand to a very loyal dog. [soft, gladdened] The dog is free. The dog is sitting beside her. [gentle, moved] He didn't leave.

lines.text: The color’s back! My dog’s back! He never left! He was just being loyal. Look at him. So loyal.
lines.script: [overjoyed, laughing, relieved] The color's back! My dog's back! [fond, proud] He never left! He was just being loyal. [melting] Look at him. So loyal.

lines.text: My dog ate a whole loaf. I found him. He was under the table. He's always under the table.
lines.script: [wry, tired, fond] My dog ate a whole loaf. I found him. [dry] He was under the table. He's always under the table.

lines.script: [deadpan, drifting, vaguely worried] My tamales are cold. My dog is cold. [flat, uncertain] My dog is somewhere. He's probably cold.

lines.text: Eleven tennis balls! Back! My dog is beside himself. Wherever he is.
lines.script: [delighted, gasping] Eleven tennis balls! Back! [laughing] My dog is beside himself. [dry beat] Wherever he is.

lines.text: Angel City Cab Co. I'm Sol. Sal's cousin. Also one cab.
lines.script: [fast, friendly, proud] Angel City Cab Co. I'm Sol. Sal's cousin. [cheerful, matter of fact] Also one cab.

lines.speaker: sal
lines.text: Cab eight. Sal has cab seven. We don't talk about what happened to the other six.
lines.script: [proud, brisk] Cab eight. Sal has cab seven. [dropping low, ominous] We don't talk about what happened to the other six.

lines.speaker: sal
lines.text: I go to the airport, the airport, and sometimes the airport.
lines.script: [chatty, dramatic, listing his route] I go to the airport, the airport, [wry, shrugging] and sometimes the airport.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: Mrs. Alvarez is amber, mid-NO, one finger out. Still warm. Still firm.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, gentle wonder] Mrs. Alvarez is amber, mid-NO, one finger out. [soft, fond] Still warm. Still firm.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: I said NO. I lost the sentence. It was a good NO.
lines.script: [waking up, indignant, then proud] I said NO. [flustered] I lost the sentence. [satisfied, firm] It was a good NO.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: That woman who runs can come back any time. She can run in my kitchen. Tell her.
lines.script: [warm, firm, generous, commanding] That woman who runs can come back any time. [fond, insistent] She can run in my kitchen. Tell her.

lines.speaker: carmen
lines.text: TEN. Ten people in a two-bedroom house from 1912. One bathroom. ONE.
lines.script: [exasperated, scandalized, counting] TEN. Ten people in a two-bedroom house from nineteen twelve. [rising, outraged] One bathroom. ONE.

lines.speaker: carmen
lines.text: Tony, feet off my table! Kevin, the baby isn't a football! Mateo, give Abuela the remote! ...Tom, mijo, sit. If you can find a chair.
lines.script: [bellowing, scolding across the room] Tony, feet off my table! Kevin, the baby isn't a football! Mateo, give Abuela the remote! [softening, warm and wry] ...Tom, mijo, sit. [dry] If you can find a chair.

lines.speaker: carmen
lines.text: Everybody says, 'Mama, the house is so full of love.' It's full of SOMETHING. Take tamales. Please. I need the room in my fridge.
lines.script: [dry, put upon, mimicking visitors] Everybody says, 'Mama, the house is so full of love.' [exasperated] It's full of SOMETHING. [pressing, generous, pushing food] Take tamales. Please. [pleading] I need the room in my fridge.

lines.speaker: Don Beto
lines.text: Don Beto is amber in his recliner, one fist up. The TV is stuck on a goal. Nobody has ever seen him so quiet.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, amused] Don Beto is amber in his recliner, one fist up. The TV is stuck on a goal. [quiet, awed] Nobody has ever seen him so quiet.

lines.speaker: Don Beto
lines.text: Foul! That was a foul! Wait. Is the game over? What year is it?
lines.script: [waking up, indignant, then lost] Foul! That was a foul! [blinking, confused] Wait. Is the game over? [dazed] What year is it?

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: I've been in this chair since the game started. Which game? Yes.
lines.script: [slow, dreamy, settled in] I've been in this chair since the game started. [deadpan] Which game? [long pause, serene] Yes.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: Ten people. I counted once. Then I lost count. Then I took a nap.
lines.script: [slow, mellow, drifting] Ten people. I counted once. [yawning, trailing off] Then I lost count. [sleepy] Then I took a nap.

lines.speaker: Tony
lines.text: Tony is amber, a plate in each hand, mid-step. A tortilla hangs in the air over him. It hasn’t decided yet.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, amused] Tony is amber, a plate in each hand, mid-step. [soft, wondering] A tortilla hangs in the air over him. [whisper, droll] It hasn't decided yet.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Me and Yesenia are saving for our own place. In this market? We'll be here until Mateo goes to college.
lines.script: [calm, dry, a little tired] Me and Yesenia are saving for our own place. [flat, wry] In this market? [resigned] We'll be here until Mateo goes to college.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: The two houses next door sold for more than this whole block cost in 1990. My mom isn't okay about it.
lines.script: [dry, incredulous] The two houses next door sold for more than this whole block cost in nineteen ninety. [flat, wry] My mom isn't okay about it.

lines.speaker: Yesenia
lines.text: Yesenia is amber, one earbud out, mid-eye-roll. She would hate this. She would hate it SO much.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, amused] Yesenia is amber, one earbud out, mid-eye-roll. [droll, whispering] She would hate this. [deadpan, emphatic] She would hate it SO much.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: Sofi, no. Sofi. SOFI. ...She bit something. We don't have a dog. I don't know what she bit.
lines.script: [warning, escalating, losing patience] Sofi, no. Sofi. SOFI. [bewildered, flat] ...She bit something. [worried, deadpan] We don't have a dog. I don't know what she bit.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: Baby Lupita is finally asleep. If you wake her, you're moving in.
lines.script: [hushed, tired, fierce whisper] Baby Lupita is finally asleep. [low, threatening] If you wake her, you're moving in.

lines.speaker: Claudia
lines.text: Claudia is amber, phone in hand. The screen says 47 unread. It will say 47 forever.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, wry] Claudia is amber, phone in hand. [flat, droll] The screen says forty-seven unread. [soft, resigned] It will say forty-seven forever.

lines.script: [exhausted, deadpan, drowsy] Night shift nurse. I sleep in the bathtub. [dreamy, matter of fact] It's the only room with a lock.

lines.speaker: luna

lines.script: [slow, drowsy] Until somebody needs the bathroom. [beat, flat, resigned] Somebody always needs the bathroom.

lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed, fond] Kevin is amber on the bottom bunk, mid-yawn. [soft, amused] He looks very peaceful. [dry whisper] He always does.

lines.script: [bored, deadpan, unimpressed] I share the bunk bed with Uncle Tony's exercise bike.

lines.script: [flat, deadpan, patient] It's not a metaphor. [dry] The bike is on the top bunk.

lines.script: [bursting, thrilled, pointing] Truck! TRUCK!

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: Ba! Ba! ...Truck.

lines.script: [amused, fond, teasing] Horror movie tonight. You pick. [dry, grinning] You always pick the scary one and then hold my arm the whole time.

lines.script: [content, glowing, easygoing] Rode the train to the clay studio. Forty minutes. [warm] Best forty minutes of my day. [delighted] Met a man who knows every line.

lines.script: [warm, flirty, low] The slime? It just needs someone to mold it. [sly, grinning] I have more of these. [smooth] You know I do.

lines.script: [tender, soft, teasing] Be careful out there. [warm, low] I like you un-cracked.

lines.script: [wistful, precise, small] 34th floor. From my desk I can see Griffith Park. [quiet, rueful] I've never been to Griffith Park.

lines.script: [amused, shaking her head, warm] The juice bar next door asked me what a pupusa is. I gave them three. [laughing, satisfied] Now they ask every day.

lines.script: [earnest, embarrassed, soft] Mrs. Alvarez brought us tamales. We posted them. We tagged her. [sheepish, small] She doesn't have Instagram.

lines.script: [crisp, impressed, retelling] Mr. Washington told us the windows are older than his father. [solemn, dry] He was very serious about it.

lines.speaker: Mudling
lines.text: Round {n}. I brought more mud.

lines.speaker: mudling
lines.text: ...I'm a puddle now. Give me a minute.
lines.script: [sloppy, spent, melting] ...I'm a puddle now. [drained, mumbling] Give me a minute.

lines.speaker: mudling
lines.text: The sprout is fine. I'm fine. Everything is fine.

lines.speaker: skeeter
